גא.def:
H1341. ge

גֵּא‎ adjective proud, scribal error for גֵּאֶה‎ Isa 16:6 (as in Jer 48:29).

גאה.def:
H1344. geah

גֵּאָה‎ noun feminine pride, Prov 8:13.

גֵּוָה‎ noun feminine pride (גֵּיוָה ᵑ7‎; Biblical Hebrew גֵּאָה‎; compare K§ 55, l (but also 6 a)); — absolute ׳בְּג‎ Dan 4:34 in pride.

גאואל.def:
H1345. Geuel

גְּאוּאֵל‎ proper name, masculine (majesty of El) the spy of the tribe of Gad Num 13:15.

גאוה.def:
H1346. gaavah

גַּאֲוָה‎ noun feminine majesty, pride (compare Syriac ) — Job 41:7 6t.; construct גַּאֲוַת‎ Prov 29:23 2t.; suffix גַּאֲוָתִי‎ Isa 13:3 8t.; —

1 rising up, swelling of the sea Psa 46:4.

2 majesty, of Israel Deut 33:29, Moab Isa 16:6 = Jer 48:29, scales of crocodile Job 41:7, of God Deut 33:26; Psa 68:35.

3 pride, haughtiness Psa 10:2; 31:19; 31:24; 36:12; 73:6; Prov 14:3; 29:23; Isa 9:8; 13:11; 25:11; גאותי עליזי‎ my proudly exulting ones 13:3 compare Zeph 3:11.

גאולים.def:
H1350. gaal

I. גָּאַל‎ verb redeem, act as kinsman (Late Hebrew, Niph`al be redeemed; also גְּאוּלָּה גּוֺאֵל,‎) —

Qal Perfect ׳ג‎, etc. Isa 44:23 14t.; Imperfect יִגְאַל‎, etc. Lev 25:33 18t.; Imperative גְּאַל‎, etc. Ruth 4:6 3t.; Infinitive absolute גָּאֹל‎ Lev 27:13 2t.; construct לִגְאוֺל‎ Ruth 4:4 2t.; suffix לְגָאֳלֵךְ‎ 3:13; Participle גֹּאֵל‎ Lev 25:26 24t., גּוֺאֵל‎ Isa 59:20; Psa 103:4; suffix גֹּאַלְךָ‎ Isa 48:17, גֹּאֲלֵךְ‎ 54:8 (suffix 19 t.); passive plural גְּאוּלִים‎, etc. 35:9 4t.; —

1 act as kinsman, do the part of next of kin (chiefly in D H P Ruth), גֹּאֵל‎ kinsman Lev 25:25 (H) Num 5:8; 35:12 (P) Ruth 2:20; 3:9, 12; 4:1, 3, 6, 8, 14; 1Kin 16:11.

a. in taking a kinsman's widow וגאלתיך לגאלך יחפץ לא ואם יגאל טוב יגאלך אם‎ if he will do thee the kinsman's part (raise up children by the widow) well, let him do the kinsman's part; but if he is not pleased to do thee the kinsman's part then I will do thee the kinsman's part Ruth 3:13;

b. in redeeming from bondage Lev 25:48-49, (H);

c. in redeeming a field Lev 25:26, 33 (H) Ruth 4:4, 6;

d. claim as kinsman Job 3:5;

e. הַדָּם גֹּאֵל‎ the avenger of blood Num 35:19, 21, 24, 25, 27 (twice in verse); Josh 20:3, 5 (?; not in ᵐ5‎) 20:9 (P). Deut 19:6, 12 (D) 2Sam 14:11.

2 redeem, by payment of value assessed, of consecrated things, by the original owner Lev 27:13, 15, 19, 20, 31 (P).

3 redeem, with God as subject implying personal relationship, chiefly in poetry: —

a. individuals, from death Psa 103:4; Lam 3:58; Hosea 13:14, רע מכל‎ Gen 48:16 (E poetry), נפשׁ‎ Psa 69:19; 72:14, orphans Prov 23:11; Jer 50:34, וגאלני ריבי ריבה‎ Psa 119:154, גֹּאֲלִי‎ Job 19:25, וְגֹאֲלִי צוּרִי‎ Psalm 19:15.

b. Israel, from Egyptian bondage Exod 6:6 (P?) 15:13 (song) Psa 74:2; 77:16; 78:35, אויב מיד‎ 106:10.

c. from exile (chiefly Isa3, the verb not in Isa1) Isa 43:1; 44:22-23, 48:20; 52:9; 63:9; Micah 4:10, מיד‎ Psa 107:2; Jer 31:11; Yahweh is גֹּאֵל‎ Isa 41:14; 43:14; 44:6, 24; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7, 26; 54:5, 8; 59:20; 60:16; 63:16; and the people גְּאוּלִים‎ 35:9; 51:10; 62:12; 63:4 (compare גְּאוּלַי‎ below), Psa 107:2.

Niph`al Perfect נִגְאָ֑ל‎ Lev 25:49; Imperfect יִגָּאֵל‎ 25:30 5t.; תִּגָּאֵ֑לוּ‎ Isa 52:3; —

1 reflexive redeem oneself Lev 25:49 (H).

2 pass. be redeemed,

a. field Lev 25:30 (H), slave 25:54 (H);

b. consecrated things Lev 27:20, 27, 28, 33 (P);

c. Jerusalem by Yahweh Isa 52:3.

גְּאוּלַי‎ Isa 63:4, in ג ׳שְׁנַת‎,

noun abstract redemption, according to ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Ges Hi De MV Che Di RVm; then either plural abstract suffix year of (my) redemption (so most); or abstract form. in י֯‎, after Syriac analogy, LagSymm. ii. 101 f. Semitic i. 19, 68. BN 192 (ᵐ5‎ omit my); but < Passive participle plural suffix my ransomed (released) ones Ew Br Brd AV RV compare below גאל‎ above.

גאון.def:
H1347. ga

'own גָּאוֺן‎ noun masculineHosea 5:5 exaltation — Job 40:10 5t.; construct גְּאוֺן‎ Lev 26:19 31t.; suffix גְּאוֺנְךָ‎ etc. Exod 15:7 9t.; plural suffix גְּאוֺנָ֑יִךְ‎ Ezek 16:56; —

1 exaltation, majesty, excellence,

a. of nations, their wealth, power, magnificence of buildings, e.g. Egypt Ezek 32:12, Chaldeans Isa 13:11, 19; 14:11, Philistines Zech 9:6, Assyria 10:11, Jacob Psa 47:5; Amos 6:8; 8:7; Nahum 2:3, Israel Hosea 5:5; 7:10 (probably appellation of ׳י‎), Nahum 2:3, Judah Jer 13:9, Jerusalem 13:9; Ezek 16:56; עֻזָּהּ גְּאוֺן‎ pride of her strength 30:6, 18; 33:28; עזים גאון‎ 7:24 (but ᵐ5‎ Ew Hi Co read עזם‎); עזכם גאון‎ Lev 26:19; Ezek 24:21; the fruit of land of Judah will become ולתפארת לגאון‎ majestic and beautiful Isa 4:2; צבי כל גאון‎ the majesty of all the splendour (of Tyre) 23:9; Zion is to become עולם גאון‎ an everlasting excellency 60:15.

b. of God Exod 15:7; Isa 24:14; Micah 5:3; גְּאֹנוֺ הֲדַר‎ Isa 2:10, 19, 21; גְּאוֺנוֺ בְּקוֺל יַרְעֵם‎ Job 37:4; וָגֹבַהּ גָּאוֺן נָא עֲדֵה‎ 40:10.

c. הירדן גאון‎ majesty of Jordan, referring to the green and shady banks, clothed with willows, tamarisks, and cane, in which the lions made their covert Jer 49:19; 50:44; Zech 11:3, and therefore dangerous Jer 12:5 (Ew thinks of the swelling of its agitated waters); גַּלֶּיךָ גְּאוֺן‎ majesty of thy waves Job 38:11.

2 pride (bad sense) Job 35:12; Psa 59:13; Prov 8:13; 16:18; Ezek 7:20; 16:49; Zeph 2:10; of Moab Isa 16:6 (twice in verse) = Jer 48:29 (twice in verse).

גאות.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

גאל.def:
H1350. gaal

a. in taking a kinsman's widow וגאלתיך לגאלך יחפץ לא ואם יגאל טוב יגאלך אם‎ if he will do thee the kinsman's part (raise up children by the widow) well, let him do the kinsman's part; but if he is not pleased to do thee the kinsman's part then I will do thee the kinsman's part Ruth 3:13;

a. individuals, from death Psa 103:4; Lam 3:58; Hosea 13:14, רע מכל‎ Gen 48:16 (E poetry), נפשׁ‎ Psa 69:19; 72:14, orphans Prov 23:11; Jer 50:34, וגאלני ריבי ריבה‎ Psa 119:154, גֹּאֲלִי‎ Job 19:25, וְגֹאֲלִי צוּרִי‎ Psalm 19:15.

b. Israel, from Egyptian bondage Exod 6:6 (P?) 15:13 (song) Psa 74:2; 77:16; 78:35, אויב מיד‎ 106:10.

c. from exile (chiefly Isa3, the verb not in Isa1) Isa 43:1; 44:22-23, 48:20; 52:9; 63:9; Micah 4:10, מיד‎ Psa 107:2; Jer 31:11; Yahweh is גֹּאֵל‎ Isa 41:14; 43:14; 44:6, 24; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7, 26; 54:5, 8; 59:20; 60:16; 63:16; and the people גְּאוּלִים‎ 35:9; 51:10; 62:12; 63:4 (compare גְּאוּלַי‎ below), Psa 107:2.

Niph`al Perfect נִגְאָ֑ל‎ Lev 25:49; Imperfect יִגָּאֵל‎ 25:30 5t.; תִּגָּאֵ֑לוּ‎ Isa 52:3; —

2 pass. be redeemed,

a. field Lev 25:30 (H), slave 25:54 (H);

b. consecrated things Lev 27:20, 27, 28, 33 (P);

c. Jerusalem by Yahweh Isa 52:3.

גְּאוּלַי‎ Isa 63:4, in ג ׳שְׁנַת‎,

noun abstract redemption, according to ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Ges Hi De MV Che Di RVm; then either plural abstract suffix year of (my) redemption (so most); or abstract form. in י֯‎, after Syriac analogy, LagSymm. ii. 101 f. Semitic i. 19, 68. BN 192 (ᵐ5‎ omit my); but < Passive participle plural suffix my ransomed (released) ones Ew Br Brd AV RV compare below גאל‎ above.

גבור.def:
H1368. gibbor

גִּבּוֺר‎159 adjective strong, mighty (compare Arabic one who magnifies himself, behaves proudly, a tyrant, who is bold, audacious) — Gen 10:9 5t.; גִּבֹּר‎ 10:8 2t.; גִּבּוֺרָם‎ 1Sam 17:51; plural גִּבּוֺרִים‎ Jer 46:9 27t.; גִּבֹּרִים‎ Josh 10:2 21t.; construct גִּבּוֺרֵי‎ 1Chr 11:27 29t.; גִּבֹּרֵי‎ 9:26 4t.; suffix גִּבּוֺרֶיךָ‎ Hosea 10:13 + (variant reading suffixes 11 t.); —

1. adjective בַּבְּהֵמָה גִּבּוֺר‎ mightiest among beasts Prov 30:30; גִּבּוֺר אִישׁ‎ 1Sam 14:52; בָּאָרֶץ גִּבּוֺר‎ Psa 112:2; צַיִד גִּבּוֺר‎ mighty in hunting Gen 10:9 (J); גבור מלך‎ Dan 11:3; גִּבּוֺר אֵל‎ the Messiah Isa 9:5; attribute of God especially as fighting for his people Psa 24:8 (twice in verse); Deut 10:17; Neh 9:32; Isa 10:21; Jer 32:18 (compare Arabic ).

2. noun masculine strong, valiant man Josh 10:2 (E) Gen 6:4; 10:8(J) Judg 5:13, 23; 1Sam 2:4 16t. 1Kin 1:8, 10; 2Kin 24:16; 1Chr 1:10-11t. Ezra 7:28; Job 16:14; Psa 19:6; 33:16; 45:4; 52:3; 78:65; 89:20; 120:4; 127:4; Prov 16:32; 21:22; Song 3:7 (twice in verse); 4:4; Eccl 9:11; Isa 3:2; 13:3; 21:17; 42:13; 49:24-25, Jer 5:16-17t. Ezek 32:12 5t. Hosea 10:13; Joel 2:7; Joel 4:9; Joel 4:10; Joel 4:11; Amos 2:14, 16; Obadiah 9; Nahum 2:4; Zeph 1:14; 3:17; Zech 9:13; 10:5, 7; compare phrases חיל גִּבּוֺר‎ mighty man of valour Judg 6:12; 11:1; 1Sam 9:1; 16:18; 1Kin 11:28; 2Kin 5:1 (מְצֹרָ֑ע חַיִל גִּבּוֺר הָיָה וְהָאִישׁ‎ so ᵐ5‎ and others; but ᵐ5‎L ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἦν λεπός, compare also Klo's dubious emendation), 1Chr 12:28; 28:1; 2Chr 13:3; 17:16-17, 25:6; 32:21; חיל גבור אישׁ‎ Ruth 2:1; החיל גבורי‎ Josh 1:14 (D) 6:2; 10:7 (JE) 2Kin 15:20; 24:14; החיל גבורי אישׁ‎ Josh 8:3; חיל גברי‎ 1Chr 5:24 14t. Neh 11:14; חילים גבורי‎ 1Chr 7:5, 7, 11, 40; החילים גבורי‎ 11:26; כח גברי‎ Psa 103:20; מלחמה גבורי‎2Chr 13:3; השֹׁערים גברי‎ 1Chr 9:26; הגבורים בית‎ Neh 3:16; הגבורים (ה)צָבָא‎ 2Sam 10:7; 1Chr 19:8; הגברים ראשׁי‎ 11:10; לשׁתות גבורים‎ valiant to drink Isa 5:22.

גבורה.def:
H1369. geburah

גְּבוּרָה‎: 61 noun feminine strength, might — Exod 32:18 16t.; construct גְּבוּרַת‎ Psa 147:10; suffix גְּבוּרָתוֺ‎ + (suffixes 32 t.); plural גְּבוּרוֺת‎ Job 41:4 3t.; גְּבֻרוֺת‎ + Job 71:16; גְּבוּרֹתֶיךָ‎ Deut 3:24 + (suffixes 6 t.); —

1 strength, of horse Job 39:19; Psa 147:10, crocodile Job 41:4, sun Judg 5:31, body of man Psa 90:10; Exod 9:16; 10:17.

2 might, valour, of warriors Judg 8:21; Prov 8:14; Isa 3:25; 28:6; 30:15; Jer 9:22; 23:10; 49:35; 51:30; Ezek 32:29-30, Micah 3:8; 7:16; גְּבוּרָה עֲנוֺת קוֺל‎, noise of shouting in warlike strength Exod 32:18 (E); וּגְבוּרָה עֵצָה‎ 2Kin 18:20; Isa 11:2; 36:5; compare phrases of compiler of Kings גְּבוּרָתוֺ כֹּל‎ 1Kin 15:23; 2Kin 10:34; 20:20; וּגְבוּרָתוֺ עָשָׂה אֲשֶׁר‎ 1Kin 6:5, 27; 22:46; 2Kin 13:8, 12; 14:15, 28; compare also וּגְּבּוּרָתוֺ מַלְכוּתוֺ‎ 1Chr 29:30, וּגְבוּרָתוֺ תָקְמּוֺ‎ Est 10:2.

3 might of God Job 26:14; Psalm 21:14; Psa 54:3; 65:7; 66:7; 71:18; 80:3; 89:14; 106:8; 145:11; Isa 33:13; Jer 10:6; 16:21; compare phrases וגבורה כח‎ 1Chr 29:12; 2Chr 20:6, וג ׳חכמה‎ Job 12:13, וג ׳משׁפט‎ Micah 3:8, והג ׳הגדלה‎ 1Chr 29:11; גְּבוּרוֺת‎ mighty deeds of God Deut 3:24; Psa 20:7; 71:16; 106:2; 145:4; 145:12; 150:2; Isa 63:15.

גבח.def:
H1371. gibbeach

גִּבֵּחַ‎ adjective having a bald forehead, ׳ג הוּא‎ Lev 13:41 (P || הוּא קֵרֵחַ‎ 13:40).

גבחת.def:
H1372. gabbachath

גַּבַּ֫חַת‎ noun feminine bald forehead (Late Hebrew id., Aramaic ), only Leviticus 13 — absolute Lev 13:42 (P; asson. בַגַּבַּ֫חַת אוֺ בְּקָרַ֫חַת‎); גַּבַּחְתּוֺ‎ 13:42; 13:43 (both P & || קָרַחְתּוֺ‎); in all, as place of appearance of an eruption; 13:55 (P; || id.) = in its front, i.e. front of garment.

גֹּבַי‎ see below גבה‎.

סַלָּ֑י גַּבַּי גַּבַּי,‎ see below גבב‎.

גבי.def:
H1373. Gabbay

סַלָּ֑י גַּבַּי‎ apparently proper name, masculine (compare Aramaic , Talmud גַּבָּי‎, tax-gatherer) a Benjamite Neh 11:8; but text dubious compare 1Chr 9:8 & SmListen 7.

גבים.def:
H1374. Gebim

גֵּבִים‎ proper name, of a location see below גוב‎.

גבל‎ (according to Thes originally twist, wind, whence not only מִגְבָּלֹת גַּבְלֻת,‎, but also גְּבוּל‎ (cord and then) boundary, as determined by measuring cord, or line, whence verb denominative גָּבַל‎ bound, border, q. v. below; Late Hebrew גָּבַל‎, Aramaic גְּבַל‎ mean mix, knead; Arabic , Syriac = create, fashion; MV assume meaning massive, whence Arabic mountain (compare Assyrian gablu HA48), and גְּבוּל‎ as originally earth-wall, etc., serving as boundary; this explains גַּבְלֻת‎ etc. less well).

גּבִים‎ proper name, of a location (trenches) north from Jerusalem, with article ׳הַגּ‎ Isa 10:31; site unknown.

גביע.def:
H1375. gabia

גָּבִיעַ‎ noun masculineGen 44:12 cup, bowl — ׳ג‎ 44:12 2t.; construct גְּבִיעַ‎ 44:2; suffix גְּבִיעִי‎ 44:2; plural גְּבִיעִים‎ Exod 25:34, גְּבִעִים‎ 25:33; 25:33 4t.; suffix גְּבִיעֶיהָ‎ 25:31; 37:17; — cup (of Joseph) Gen 44:2, 12, 16, 17; plural cups (of golden candlestick in tabernacle) Exod 25:31, 33 (twice in verse); 25:34; 37:17, 19 (3 t. in verse); 37:20; bowls Jer 35:5 וכֹסוֺת יין מלאים גְּבִעִים‎.

גביר.def:
H1376. gebir

גְּבִיר‎ noun masculine lord, Gen 27:29, 37.

גבירה.def:
H1377. gebirah

גְּבִירָה‎ noun feminine 1. lady, queen, 1Kin 11:19;

2 queen-mother, 1Kin 15:13 2Chr 15:16; מִגּ ׳וַיְסִרֶהָ‎ he removed her from (the position of) queen-mother; compare 2Kin 10:13; Jer 13:18; 29:2.

גביש.def:
H1378. gabish

גָּבִישׁ‎ noun masculine crystal (compare אֶלְגָּבִישׁ‎ hail — on relation of meanings compare Greek κρύσταλλος, & Ethiopic usage of DiLex. Aeth.759 — Arabic gypsum, Assyrian gibšu, mass, abundance, COT Gloss) — וְגָבִישׁ רָא֯מוֺת‎ Job 28:18 coral and crystal.

גבל.def:
H1571. gam

גַּם‎768 adverb denoting addition, also, moreover, yea (Moabite id., also Zinjirli (Lzb250 Cooke166); probably akin to √ ; compare (accusative) in a mass, altogether) —

1 also, moreover, emphasizing sometimes the thought of an entire sentence, but more usually the word immediately following, as Gen 3:6 לְאִישָׁהּ גַּם וַתִּתֵּן‎ and gave also to her husband, Genesis 3:27 and take also of the tree of life, 7:3; 19:21; 24:19; 26:21; 29:27; 30:15; 32:21 (֗֗֗ הִגֵּה גַּם‎: so Est 7:9) Gen 48:11; Exod 8:28; 12:32b Deut 1:37; 1Sam 28:20; 2Sam 11:12; 2Kin 9:27; Isa 7:13 +. Often before pronouns, Gen 4:4 הוּא גַם הֵבִיא וְהֶבֶל‎ and Abel, he also brought, 20:5 וְהִיאגַֿםהִֿוא‎ (so only here) and she herself also, 20:6; 27:31 הוּא גַּם וַיַּעַשׂ‎, 30:8; Deut 3:20; Judg 3:31; 6:35; 9:19; 1Sam 19:20-24 Jer 12:6; 48:26 etc. (compare MI6 הא גם ויאמר‎): especially in Genealogies of J (BuUrg. 220) Gen 4:22, 26; 10:21; 19:38; 22:20, 24 compare Judg 8:31. גַּם‎ followed by pronoun also begins a sentence with emphasis in an elevated style, thou (they) also, Isa 14:10; Jer 12:6 (twice in verse); 48:7; Ezek 16:52; Nahum 3:11 (twice in verse). After a pronoun in an oblique case (Ges§ 135, 2) Gen 27:34; 1Sam 19:23; 2Sam 17:5; Jer 25:14; 27:7 +. וְגַם‎ and also (more often than גַּם‎ alone attaching a sentence) Gen 6:4; 14:16; 15:14; 17:16; 20:12; 24:14, 46; 30:6; 37:7; 38:24; 42:28; Exod 2:19; 3:9; 4:14; Josh 7:11 (5 t.) 1Sam 4:17; 1Kin 21:19 + often; with a negative = neither Exod 5:2; 34:3 and elsewhere — גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎ (like et ... et) both ... and Gen 44:16; 47:3, 19; Num 18:3; Jer 51:12; Psa 49:3 +: גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎ Gen 24:25; Judg 8:22; Eccl 9:6: with a negative neither ... nor Num 23:25; 1Sam 20:27; 1Kin 3:26, and (3t.) Gen 43:8; Exod 4:10; 1Sam 28:6. So (but seldom) גַּםוְ֗֗֗גַם‎ Gen 24:44; Exod 10:25f.; 1Sam 2:26; 12:14; 26:25: with negative 21:9. — N.B. In poetry independence and emphasis is sometimes given by גַּם‎ to a new idea, where in English we should be satisfied with and: Psa 107:5; 137:1; Job 24:19; Cant 7:14; Lam 4:15.

2 with stress on a particular word, even, Exod 4:9; Num 22:33 אוֺתְךָ גַּם‎ even thee I had slain, and kept her alive, 2Sam 17:10; Jer 2:33; Psa 132:12; Prov 14:13 even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, 14:20; 17:28; 20:11; Ruth 2:15; Nehemiah 3:35; and so often after כִּי‎, Deut 12:31 for even their sons they burn in the fire to their gods, 1Sam 22:17; Isa 26:12; Jer 6:11; 12:6; 14:5; Hosea 9:12 לָהֶם כִּיגַֿםאֿוֺי‎ for even woe is it to them when I depart from them; הֲגַם‎ Gen 16:13; 1Sam 10:11-12, = 19:24; 1Kin 17:20; Psa 78:20; Job 41:1; Est 7:8. Other cases: — 1Sam 24:12 רְאֵה גַּם רְאֵה‎ see, yea see ! (but HupQu. Job vi. רָאֹה גַּם‎: compare below) Psa 118:11; Job 2:10 נְקַבֵּל אֶתהַֿטּוֺב גַּם‎ shall we receive good (emphatic) from God and not evil ? 21:7; interposed once between a substantive and adjective Gen 20:4 Gentemne etiam justam interficies? emphasizing כֹּל‎, Deut 28:61; Judg 9:49b 1Sam 22:7 לְכֻלְּכֶם גַּםֿ‎ to all (emphatic) of you will he give ...? 2Sam 19:31 יִקָּ֑ח אֶתהַֿכֹּל גַּם‎ yea, the whole let him take! Isa 26:12; אֶחָד‎ 2Sam 17:12b and we will not leave ֗֗֗ אֶחָד גַּם‎ even one (similarly 17:13 b), Psa 14:3 (= 53:4) אֶחָד גַּם אֵין‎; an infinitive or cognate accusative attached to a verb, Gen 31:15; 46:4; Num 11:15; 16:13; 1Sam 1:6. שְׁנֵיהֶם גַּם‎ literally even both i.e. the one as well as the other (German alle beide) is said idiomatically, Gen 27:45 (שְׁנֵיכֶם‎), Deut 22:22; 23:19; 1Sam 25:43 (שְׁתֵּיהֶן‎), Prov 17:15; 20:10, 12; Ruth 1:5.

3 introducing a climax, yea, especially in a rhetorical style, Gen 27:33; Deut 23:3; 23:4; Judg 5:4 (twice in verse); Isa 13:3; 14:8; 43:13 yea, from to-day I am the same, 44:12 רָעֵב גַּם‎ yea, he is hungry, and has no strength, 47:3; 48:8 (3 t. in verse); 57:7; Jer 46:16; 48:2; 51:44; Hosea 7:9; Psa 41:10; 84:7; 139:12; Isa 66:8 אֶתבָּֿנֶיהָ צִיּוֺן גַּםיָָֽֿלְדָה, כִּיחָֿ֫לָה‎, Jer 5:28; 12:2; Ezek 24:5; Job 21:7; Song 8:1: emphasizing an extreme, or aggravated, case, yea, even, Isa 49:15 yea, these may forgot, Jer 8:17 yea, the stork knoweth, etc., Isa 23:12 שָׁם גַּם‎ even there no rest shall be for thee (so Psa 139:10), Isa 49:25; 57:6; Jer 23:11b; Mal 3:15; Psa 84:4.

4 expressing correspondence, especially in the matter of retribution (the גַּם‎ correlativum), so frequently אָנֹכִי גַּם אֲנִי, גַּם‎ I also (on my part): — Gen 20:6 I also [as well as thyself] know that thou hast done this innocently, Josh 24:18; Judg 2:21; 1Sam 1:28 (compare Dr) 28:22 אַתָּה גַּם‎ thou also (as I have done 28:21), 2Sam 12:13 ׳י‎ also [responding to thy confession] hath removed thy sin, 2Kin 2:3, 5; Isa 31:2; 66:3-4 (גם ֗֗֗ גם‎, emphasizing the action of both parties), Jer 2:36; 4:12 now will I also [in correspondence with their deeds] speak judgments with them, 7:11; 51:49 (גם ֗֗֗ גם‎), Ezek 5:8, 11; 16:43 (וְגַם‎ = therefore also), 23:35; Hosea 4:6 because thou hast forgotten the direction of thy God, I also (on my part) will forget thy children, Psa 52:7 (thou lovest evil, etc.) יִתָּצְךָ אֵל גַּם‎ God also (on his part) will pluck thee up, 71:22; 133:1; Prov 1:26; Job 7:11; 12:3; 16:4; so וְגַם‎ Judg 2:3; Amos 4:6-7, Micah 6:13; Mal 2:9. In the apodosis (uncommon): Gen 13:16 if a man could number the dust of the earth, יִמָּנֶה זַרְעֲךָ גַּם‎ thy seed also should be numbered, Jer 31:36-37, 33:21, 26; Zech 8:6. The correspondence is sometimes of the nature of a climax: Gen 27:33; 30:8 I have wrestled, יָכֹלְתִּי גַּם‎ (compare 1Kin 22:22 תּוּכָ֔ל וְגַם‎, Jer 50:24), Isa 66:8.

5 connecting two ideas which express (or imply) a contradiction, גַּם‎ acquires sometimes an adversative force (compare אַף‎ 1 end), yet, but, though: Psa 95:9 they tried me, but also (Che) saw my work (namely of judgment), 129:2; Jer 6:15 = 8:12; Ezek 20:23; Eccl 4:8, 16; 5:18; Neh 6:1. So וְגַם‎ Ezek 16:28; 20:15; Eccl 3:13; 6:7; Neh 5:8.

6 כִּי גַּם‎ (with imperfect) yea, when Lam 3:8, even when Prov 22:6; yea though (stating an imagined case) Isa 1:15; Hosea 8:10; 9:16; Psa 23:4 (so אִם גַּם‎ Eccl 8:17); also (is it) that Ruth 2:21 (see כִּי‎ 1d). גַם כִּי‎ = for even (see above 2); = though even, although (conceding a fact) Eccl 4:14 (see De) 8:12.

גבלי.def:
H1382. Gibli

גִּבְלִי‎ adjective, of a people of foregoing with article = collective noun Josh 13:5 הַגִּבְלִי והארץ‎, but read הַגּ ׳גְבוּל‎, compare Di. 1 Kings 5:32 הַגִּבְלִים‎ (but probably text error; Th reads וַיַּגְבִּלוּם‎ and they bordered them, made a border for them (the stones); ᵐ5‎ ἔβαλον, compare also Klo).

גבלת.def:
H1383. gabluth

גַּבְלֻת‎ noun feminine twisting — גַּבְלֻת שֹׁת שַׁרְ‎ Exod 28:22, גּ ׳שַׁרְשְׁרֹת‎ 39:15 (both P), cords of twisting, i.e. (well or tightly) twisted cords.

גבן.def:
H1384. gibben

גִּבֵּן‎ adjective crook-backed, hump-backed (compare Aramaic גְּבִין‎ id., Late Hebrew גַּבָּן‎ highlander; also Late Hebrew גבין‎, Aramaic גבינא‎, , all = brow (eye-brow, etc.); compare Arabic side of forehead), Lev 21:20.

גבנה.def:
H1385. gebinah

גְּבִינָה‎ noun feminine curd, or cheese (Late Hebrew id., Arabic Ethiopic Aramaic גּוּבְנָא‎, , compare) — תַּקְמִּיאֵנִי וְכַגְּבִינָה‎ Job 10:10 (|| חָלָב‎).

גבנן.def:
H2022. har

[הוֺר‎], assumed by Thes and others as ancient form for הַר‎ mountain, to explain הוֺרַי‎ Gen 49:26, read הוֺרֵיעָֿד‎; but better הַרֲרֵיעַֿד‎ everlasting mountains, see הַר‎ below הרר‎.

הַר‎558 noun masculineGen 7:19 mountain, hill, hill-country (Late Hebrew id., plural הֲרָרִים הָרִים,‎; Phoenician הר‎ CISi. 3, 17; Sabean suffix הרתהמו‎ DHMZMG 1876, 673); — ׳ה‎ absolute Josh 17:18 +; with article הָהָר‎ Exod 3:12 +; with ָ  ה‎ locative הֶ֫רָה‎ Gen 14:10, הָהָ֫רָה‎ 12:8 12t.; construct הַר‎ 10:30 +; suffix הַרֲרִי‎ Psa 30:8, הֲרָרִי‎ Jer 17:3; הַרְכֶם‎ Psa 11:1; הַרֲרָם‎ Gen 14:6; plural הָרִים‎ Deut 11:11 +; with article הֶהָרִים‎ Gen 7:19 +; construct הָרֵי‎ 8:4 27t.; הַרֲרֵי‎ Deut 33:15 8t. (all poetry); suffix הָרַי‎ Isa 14:25; 49:11; Zech 14:5 + Ezek 38:21 (B Co חרדה‎), הָרָ֑י‎ Isa 65:9; הָרָיו‎ Ezek 35:8; Mal 1:3; הֲרָרֶיהָ‎ Deut 8:9; —

1 mountain, hill (these often not sharply distinguished, but):

a. specifically mountain, high elevation, often in all the literature; — e. g. סִינַי הַר‎ Mount Sinai (properly, the Mount of Sinai; so always) Exod 19:11, 18, 20, 23; 24:16; 31:18; 34:2, 4, 29, 32; Lev 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num 3:1; 28:6; Neh 9:13 (see סִינַי‎); also הָהָר‎ = id., Exod 19:2 10t. Exodus 19 (19:18 read הָעָם‎, so Manuscripts ᵐ5‎ Di) 20:18; 24:4 6t. Exodus 24; 25:40; 26:30; 27:8; 32:1, 15, 19; 34:2-3,(twice in verse); 34:29; = חוֺרֵב הֵר‎ 33:6 (see חֹרֵב‎), also חֹרֵ֑בָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶלהַֿר‎ 3:1, חֹרֵב הָאֱלֹהִים הַר עַד‎ 1Kin 19:8; further הָהָר‎ = id., Deut 4:11 (twice in verse); 5:4-5, 19, 20; 9:9-10t. Deuteronomy 9.. 10, 1Kin 19:11; = הָאֱלֹהִים הַר‎ Exod 4:27; 18:5; 24:13 (all J E) = יחוה הַר‎ Num 10:33 (compare Di); see further הָהָר הֹר‎ Hor the mount (so always) 20:22 10t. Numbers; Deut 32:50; = חָחָר‎ Num 20:28 (twice in verse); נְבוֺ הַר‎ Deut 32:49; 34:1 = הָהָר‎ 32:50; = הַזֶּה הָעֲבָרִים הַר‎ Num 27:12; Deut 32:49, compare (נְבוֺ לִפְנֵי‎) הָעֲבָרִים הָרֵי‎ Num 33:47-48, גְּרִזִּים הַר‎ Mt. Gerizim Deut 11:29; 27:12; Josh 8:33; הַרגְּֿרִזִּים ראֹשׁ‎ Judg 9:7; עֵֹיבָ֑ל הַר‎ Mt. Ebal Deut 11:29; 27:4; 24:13; Josh 8:30, 33; also חֶרְמוֺן הַר‎ Mt. Hermon Deut 3:8; Josh 11:17; 12:1, 5; 13:5, 11; 1Chr 5:23; compare Deut 4:48 חֶרְמוֺן הוּא שִׂיאֹן הַר‎ (see חֶרְמוֺן‎), & חֶרְמוֺן בַּעַל הַר‎ (see id., & חרמון בעל‎ below בעל‎); חַלְּבָנוֺן הַר‎ Mt. Lebanon Judg 3:3, compare לְבָנוֺן יַרְכְּתֵי הָרִים מְרוֺם‎ 2Kin 19:23 = Isa 37:24 (see לבנון‎); הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל הַר‎ Mt. Carmel 1Kin 18:19-20, 2Kin 2:25; 4:25 (see כרמל‎); הָהָר‎ = id., 4:27, apparently also 1:9; תָּבוֺר הַר‎ Mt. Tabor, Judg 4:6, 12, 14, compare Jer 46:18 בֶּהָרִים תָּבוֺר‎ (opposed to בַּיָּם כַּרְמֶל‎); הַגִּלְבֹּעַ הַר‎ 1Sam 31:1, 8; 2Sam 1:6, also (poetry) בַּגּ ׳הָרֵי‎ 1:21 (compare Dr); הַרחֶֿרֶס‎ Judg 1:35 (Stu חֶרֶס עָר‎) compare חֶרֶס‎; הַזֵּיתִים הַר‎ Zech 14:4 (twice in verse) Mount of Olives, (opposed to גֵּיא‎) compare לָעִיר מִקֶּדֶם אֲשֶׁר הָהָר‎ Ezek 11:23; also יְרוּשָׁלַםִ עַלמְּֿנֵי אֲשֶׁר בָּהָר‎ 1Kin 11:7 (place of Solomon's idolatry) = הַרהַֿמַּשְׁחִית‎ 2Kin 23:13 mountain of the destroyer (same combination in another, figurative sense Jer 51:25), others derive ׳הַמ‎ here from משׁח‎ anoint, and render as = Mt. of Olives (cited as המשׁחה הר‎ Talmud, Shabb. 56 b), compare HoffmZAW 1882, 175; הֶהָרִים אַחַד‎ in land of Moriah Gen 22:2; mountains about Jerusalem in General, לָהּ סָבִיב הָרִים יְרוּשָׁלַםִ‎ Psa 125:2; compare also 121:1 (|| יהוה‎); הָהָר‎ of citadel of Jerusalem Isa 22:5; of temple hill הַבַּיִת הַר‎ Micah 3:12 = Jer 26:18; בֵּיתיֿ ׳הַר‎ Isa 2:2 = Micah 4:1; 2Chr 33:15; also בַּשָּׂדֶה הֲרָרִי‎ Jer 17:3; further צִיּוֺן הַר‎ Mt. Zion Isa 4:5; 8:18; 10:12; 18:7; 24:23; 29:8; 31:4; 37:32; Micah 4:7; Lam 5:18; Obadiah 17.. Joel 3:5; Psa 48:3; 48:12; 74:2; 78:68; 125:1 (see also צִיּוֺן‎); compare בַּ֯יתצִֿיּוֺן הַר‎ Isa 10:32, צ בַּת ׳הַר‎ 16:1; ׳הַריֿ‎ 2:3 = Micah 4:2; Isa 30:29; Psa 24:3; (id. of Horeb Num 10:33 J E); הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַר ׳הַריֿ צְבָאוֺת‎ Zech 8:3, הַרקָֿדְשִׁי‎ Zeph 3:11; Obadiah 16; Ezek 20:40; Isa 11:9 = 65:25, compare 56:7; 57:13; 65:11; Joel 2:1 (|| צִיּוֺן‎) Joel 4:17 (|| id.) Psa 2:6 (|| id.) 3:5; 15:1; 43:3; 48:2; see further יְרוּשָׁלַםִ הַרקָֿדְשִׁי‎ Isa 66:20 compare Dan 9:16 & יְרוּשָׁלַםִ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַר‎ Isa 27:13; also צְבִיקֹֿדֶשׁ הַר‎ Dan 11:45; הַרהַֿקֹּדֶשׁ‎ Jer 31:23; even אֱלֹהַי קֹדֶשׁ הַר‎ Dan 9:20; other designations of temple-hill are ׳א לְשִׁבְתּוֺ חָמַד הָהָר‎ Psa 68:17, & יִשְׂרָאֵל מְרוֺם הַר‎ Ezek 17:23; 20:40 (|| הַרקָֿדְשִׁי‎); אֱלֹהִים קֹדֶשׁ הַר‎ 28:14 of the distant abode of God (or gods?) so אֱלֹהִים הַר‎ 28:16 (הַראֱֿלֹהִים‎ Psa 68:16 is General, a God's mountain, i.e. a majestic mountain, likewise in simile מִשְׁמָּטֶיךָ כְּהַרֲרֵיאֵֿל‎ 36:7); — הָאֱלֹהִים הַר‎ elsewhere of Horeb (Sinai) Exod 4:27; 18:5; 24:13; 1Kin 19:8 (see above). Note particular הַרמֿוֺעֵד‎ Isa 14:13 mountain of meeting or of assembly, i.e. the dwelling-place of the gods, according to Babylonian conception, here represented as in the far north, see especially Che De Di, DlPa 117 ff. COTon the passage Jr57ff. JenKosmologie 23. Upon the mountain is עָלהָֿהָר‎ compare עַלהֶֿהָרִים עַלבְּֿתוּלָיהָ וַתֵּבְךְּ‎ Judg 11:38, & the peculiar phrase הֶהָרִים עַלֿ וְיָרַדְתִּי וְאֵלְכָה‎ 11:37; go up upon אָלֿ עָלָה‎ Exod 19:23; 24:13; 34:4 (all J E); compare accusative in הָהָר הֹר אֹתָם הַעַל‎ Num 20:25; speak with one upon is בהר דבר‎ Exod 31:18; 34:32; Num 3:1 (all P), Lev 25:1 (H), compare command, give commands, law, etc., בהר‎ 7:38; 26:46; 27:34 (all P or H); other phrases with בְּ‎ upon (literally in, i.e. in the midst of a group of mountains) Exod 34:3 בְּכָל‎ (JE) 25:40; 26:30; 27:8; Num 28:6 (all P), Isa 13:4; but בְּחֹרֵב‎ Psa 106:19 = at Horeb, הָהָר בְּהֹר‎ Num 33:37 at Mt. Hor; go down from the mountain is מִןהָֿהָר יָרַד‎ Exod 32:1, 15 (both J E) 34:29 (twice in verse) (both P), compare Judg 9:36 etc.

b. mountain-range הַרבָּֿשָׁן‎ Psa 68:16 (twice in verse) = הַראֱֿלֹהִים‎ 68:16; = הַרגַּֿבְנֻנִּים‎ 68:16, גַּבְנֻנִּים הָרִים‎ 68:17 (of the Jebel Hauran: see בשׁן‎).

c. mountain, indefinite, Job 14:18 (|| צוּר‎); usually plural mountains, in General, or the mountains, especially in poetry & the higher style; often figurative; הֶהָרִים הָרִים,‎, covered by flood Gen 7:20 compare 7:19; 8:5; covered by waters & freed therefrom by word of God (at creation) Psa 104:6; a chief work of God (in creation) Amos 4:13; Psa 65:7; 90:2; Prov 8:25 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎); weighed by God Isa 40:12; removed and overturned in anger of God Job 9:5 compare Psa 46:3; 46:4; devastated by God Isa 42:15 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎) compare Jer 9:9; smoking at God's touch Psa 104:32; 144:5; melting at presence of ׳י‎ Judg 5:5; Micah 1:4; Psa 97:5; Isa 63:19; 64:2; trembling 5:25 compare Jer 4:24 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎), Nahum 1:5 (|| id.), Hab 3:10; called to witness Yahweh's dealings with his people Micah 6:2 (|| אָ֑רֶץ מֹסְדֵי הָאֵתָנִים‎) compare 6:1 (|| הַגְּבָעוֺת‎), entreated to cover the guilty Hosea 10:8 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎); addressed by ׳י‎ also Ezek 6:3 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎, opposed to גֵּאָוֺת אֲפִיקִים,‎); specifically, mountains of Israel summoned to hear ׳י‎ and addressed by him 36:1 (twice in verse); 36:4, 8; 37:22; 38:8; 39:2, 4; summoned to praise ׳י‎ Psa 148:9 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎) compare Isa 44:23; 49:13; 55:12 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎); leaping in praise of ׳י‎ Psa 114:4; 114:6 (both || גְּבָעוֺת‎); הַרֲרֵיקֶֿדֶם‎ Deut 33:15 (|| עוֺלָם גִּבְעוֺת‎); הַרֲרֵיעַֿד‎ Hab 3:6 (|| id.); הַרֲרֵיעַֿד‎ also Psa 76:5 (according to ᵐ5‎ Bi Che; ᵑ0‎ has טֶרֶף‎ for עַד‎), and probably Gen 49:26 for עַד הוֺרַי ᵑ0‎ (|| עוֺלָם גִּבְעֹת‎) compare Di.

d. high mountain גָּבֹהַּ הַר‎ Isa 30:25 (|| נִשָּׂאָה גִּבְעָה‎) compare 40:9; 52:7; מְאֹד גָּכֹהַּ הַר‎ Ezek 40:2; וְתָלוּל גָּבֹהַּ הַר‎ 17:22; plural הַגְּבֹהִים הֶהָרִים‎ Gen 7:19; Psa 104:18 (|| סְלָעִים‎), ׳הֶה הָרָמִים‎ Isa 2:14 as symbol of strength and pride (|| הַנִּשָּׂאוֺת הַגְּבָעוֺת‎), compare הֶהָרִים‎ Ezek 38:20 (|| חוֺמָה מַדְרֵגוֺת,‎).

e. opposite valley or plain Josh 12:8 (D; opposed to שְׁפֵלָה עֲרָבָה, אֲשֵׁדוֺת, מִדְּבָּר,‎), compare Deut 1:7, also Jer 17:26 (opposed to שְׁפֵלָה‎); Gen 19:17 (J; opposed to כִּכָּר‎); often opposed to גַּיְא‎ 2Kin 2:16; Ezek 31:12 (figurative) 32:5 (id.) 35:8 (|| גִּבְעָה‎), 36:4 (|| id.), Isa 40:4 (|| id.), opposed to בִּקְעָה‎ Deut 8:7; 11:11; Psa 104:8; opposed to מִדְבָּר‎ Lam 4:19 (compare Josh 12:8 above); הָרִים בֵּין‎ Psa 104:10 is || בַּנְּחָלִים‎; see also י הָרִים ׳אֱלֹהֵי עֲמָקִים וְלֹאאֱֿלֹהֵי‎ 1Kin 20:28, compare 20:23 (opposed to מִישׁוֺר‎); note also הָעֵמֶק הַר‎ Josh 13:19 (P), & גֵּיהָֿרִים גֵּיאהָֿרַי,‎ Zech 14:5 (twice in verse); further הָרִים מִדְבַּר‎ Psa 75:7 mountainous desert Vrss. & most modern (Baer מִדְבָּר‎ but compare De); mountain-ward is הֶ֫רָה‎ Gen 14:10.

f. mountains as hiding-places: — בֶּהָרִים אֲוֶר הַמִּנְהָרוֺת‎ Judg 6:2 the burrows (Stanley, VB) which are in the mountains; compare Psa 11:1; Jer 16:16 (|| גִּבְעָה‎); הָרִים מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ הָפַךְ‎ Job 28:9 (of mining), see also Deut 8:9.

g. mountains as running-place of gazelles 1Chr 12:8; of leopards נְמֵרִים הַרֲרֵי‎ Song 4:8; hunting-ground for partridges 1Sam 26:20; הָרִים עוֺף‎ Psa 50:11; compare 11:1 (figurative); wandering-place of lost sheep (figurative) Nahum 3:18; 1Kin 22:17; Jer 50:6 compare 50:6 (|| גִּבְעָה‎), Ezek 34:6 (|| רָמָה כָּלגִּֿבְעָה‎) 2Chr 18:16.

h. grazing-places for cattle בְּהַרֲרֵיאָֿ֑לֶף בְּהֵמוֺת‎Psa 50:10 (read אֵל‎ for אלף‎ Ol Bi Che), compare הָרִים יְתוּר‎ Job 39:8 of pasture of wild ass; also (si vera lectio) הָרִים בּוּל‎ 40:20, i.e. mountains as furnishing food for hippopotamus; see further Song 4:6; 8:14; Prov 27:25.

i. as place of field and vineyards2Chr 26:10 (opposed to מִישׁוֺר שְׁפֵלָה,‎) Isa 7:25; see also חָצִיר הָרִים הַמַּצְמִיחַ‎ Psa 147:8 compare Hag 1:11; figurative Psa 72:3 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎); in promise חָלָב תֵּלַכְנָה וְהַגְּבָעוֺת עָסִיס הֶהָרִים יִטְּפוּ‎ Joel 4:18 compare Amos 9:13;

j. as kindled into flame (i.e. their forests; in simile) Psa 83:15.

k. as scene of massacre, (figurative) Isa 34:3 melting with blood; as place of battle array, height 1Sam 17:3 (twice in verse).

1 as places of illicit worship Isa 65:7 (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎) compare Jer 3:6 & apparently 3:25 (|| id.) so וְנִשָּׂא הַרגָּֿבֹהַּ‎ Isa 57:7, הָרָמִים הֶהָרִים‎ Deut 12:2 (|| הַגְּבָעוֺת‎); but Ezek 18:6, 15 read perhaps הַדָּם‎ for הרים‎ compare RSK 310 & 33:25. masculine in various combinations הָהָר צַד‎ 1Sam 23:26 (twice in verse); 2Sam 13:34 side of the mountain, הָהָר צֵלַע‎ 16:13 id.; הָרִים מֹץ‎ Isa 17:13 chaff of mountains; הָרִים זֶרֶם‎ Job 24:8 mountain-shower; הֶהָרִים צֵל‎ Judg 9:36 shadow of the mountains; נְחשֶׁת הָרֵי וְהֶהָרִים הָרִים שְׁנֵי מִבֵּין‎ Zech 6:1; top of mountain usually הָהָר ראֹשׁ‎ Num 14:40, 44; 1Sam 26:13; 2Kin 1:9; as place for beacon Isa 30:17 (|| גִּבְעָה‎), (compare הַרנִֿשְׁמֶּה‎ 13:2 & הָרִים נְשׂאֹנֵֿס‎ 18:3), הֶהָרִים ראֹשׁ‎ 2:2 = Micah 4:1, הָרִים ראֹשׁ‎ Isa 42:11 (|| סֶלַע‎ as dwelling-place) see also Psa 72:16; הֶהָרִים רָאשֵׁי‎ Gen 8:5; as lurking-places for ambuscade Judg 9:25, 36, placesfor altars Ezek 6:13 (|| רָמָה גִּבְעָה‎), for sacrifice Hosea 4:13 (|| הַגְּבָעוֺת‎); הָהָר ראֹשׁ‎ Josh 15:8 = mountain-ridge, compare 15:9; Judg 16:3; הָרִים תּוֺעֲפוֺת‎ Psa 95:4; foundations of mountains הָרִים מוֺסְדֵי‎ Deut 32:22; Psa 18:8 (|| הַשָּׁמַיִם מוֺסְדוֺת‎ 2Sam 22:8); compare יָרַדְתִּי הָרִים לְקִצְבֵי‎ Jonah 2:7.

noun in figure uses: תָּשִׂים כַּמֹּץ וּגְבָעוֺת וְתָדֹק הָרִים תָּדוּשׁ‎ Isa 41:15 figurative of Israel's overcoming its foes; נָ֑שֶׁף עַלהָֿרֵי רַגְלֵיכֶם יִתְנַגְּפוּ‎ Jer 13:16 of encountering hopeless calamities; הֶהָרִים‎ Isa 54:10 as less permanent & changeless than Yahweh's kindness (|| גְּבָעוֺת‎); הַמַּשְׁחִית הַר‎ Jer 51:25 & שְׂרֵפָה הַר‎ 51:25 figurative of Babylon.

2 hill-country, mountain-region,

a. opposed to plain, etc.: — dwelling-place of Canaanites, הָהָר‎ Num 13:17, 29 (of promised land; opposed to הַיָּם הַנֶּגֶב, אֶרֶץ‎ & יַדהַֿיַּרְדֵּן‎); הַיָּם וּבְחוֺף וּבַנֶּגֶב וּבַשְּׁפֵלָה בָּהָר בָּֽעֲרָבָה‎ Deut 1:7; מִיָּם דּוֺר וּבְנָפוֺת וּבַשְּׁפֵלָה כִּנְַּרוֺת נֶגֶב וּבָֽעֲרָבָה בָּהָר‎ Josh 11:2; וּבַנֶּגֶב וּבַמִּדְבָּר וּבָֽאֲשֵׁדוֺת וּבָֽעֲרָבָה וּבַשְּׁפֵלָה בָּהָר‎ 12:8; compare 9:1; 10:40; Judg 1:9; הָהָר‎ indefinite (the hill-country, the mountains, in General) 2Chr 2:1 (place for hewing wood) so v.2:17; Neh 8:15 (place for cutting boughs), etc.

b. of a particular mountain-region, hill-country: הָאֱמֹרִי הַר‎ Deut 1:7 (compare 1:7) 1:19 (compare 1:24), also Josh 10:6; of Amalekites Judg 12:15; of Ephraim Josh 17:15; 19:50; 20:7; 21:21; 24:30, 33; Judg 3:27; 4:5; 7:24; 9:48; 17:1 6t. Judges 17; 1Sam 1:1; 9:4; 14:22; 2Sam 20:21; 1Kin 4:8; 12:25; 2Kin 5:22; 1Chr 6:52; 2Chr 13:4; 15:8; 19:4; Jer 4:15; 31:6; Ephraim and Gilead 50:19 (compare also (ה)הר‎ Josh 17:16, 18; Judg 3:27); of Israel Josh 11:16, 21, cf. יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרֵי‎ Ezek 6:2; 19:9; 33:28; 34:13; 35:12; יִשְׂרָאֵל מְרוֺם הָרֵי‎ 17:23; 20:40 (|| הַרקָֿדְשִׁי‎) 34:14; הָהָר עָרֵי‎ i.e. in mountain-country Deut 2:37 (of Ammonites), Jer 32:44; 33:13; hill-country of Judah Josh 11:21; 15:48; 18:12; 20:7; 21:11; 2Chr 21:11 (יהודה הָרֵי‎) 27:4; abode of Jebusites Josh 11:3.

הֲרָרֶיהָ הַרֲרִי, הַרֲרָם, הֲרָרִי, הַרֲרִי,‎ see הר‎.

גבע.def:
H1387. Geba

גֶּ֫בַע‎ proper name, of a location — ׳ג‎ absolute Josh 21:17 +; construct Judg 20:10 +; גָּ֑בַע‎ Josh 18:24 +; — Levitical city, in Benjamin 21:17 = 1Chr 6:45; Josh 18:24 compare 1Chr 8:6; 1Kin 15:22; Neh 11:31; also 1Sam 13:16 & Judg 20:10, 33 ᵑ0‎, in all three read גִּבְעָה (גִּבְעַת)‎, compare context; — northernmost city in kingdom of Judah 2Kin 23:8 from Geba to Beersheba, compare Zech 14:10; situated south of pass of Michmash Isa 10:29; 1Sam 14:5 compare 13:3; mentioned also 2Chr 16:6; Ezra 2:26; Neh 7:30; 12:29; in 1Sam 13:18 ᵐ5‎ We Dr read הַגֶּבַע‎ for גְּבוּל ᵑ0‎ q. v.; (2Sam 5:25 read גבעון‎ with ᵐ5‎ and 1Chr 14:16). — Modern Jeba` RobBR i. 440 f. BdPal 120.

גבעא.def:
H1388. Giba

גִּבְעָא‎ proper name, masculine a son of Caleb 1Chr 2:49.

גבעה.def:
H1389. gibah

I. גִּבְעָה‎ noun feminine hill — absolute גִּבְעָה‎ 2Sam 2:25 13t. + Ezek 6:13 (strike out Co q. v.) 1Sam 7:1; 2Sam 6:3-4, (compare Dr); construct גִּבְעַת‎ Josh 5:3 8t. + 1Sam 10:5 (compare Dr); suffix גִּבְעָתִי‎ Ezek 34:26 (but strike out Co), גִּבְעָתָהּ‎ Isa 31:4; plural absolute גְּבָעוֺת‎ Deut 12:2 35t.; construct גִּבְעוֺת‎ 33:15; Hab 3:6, גִּבְעֹת‎ Gen 49:26; suffix גִּבְעוֺתֶיךָ‎ Ezek 35:8; — hill, height, elevation, both high and low, compare Psa 148:9 גבעות וכל ההרים‎, 65:13; —

1 in ordinary prose, hill, lower than mountain Exod 17:9-10, (E) 2Sam 2:25; it may be proper name in 1Sam 7:1; 10:10; 2Sam 6:3-4, see also below II. גִּבְעָה‎.

2 especially as place of illicit worship כָּלגֿ ׳עַל רענן עץ כל ותחת גְּבֹהָה‎ 1Kin 14:23; 2Kin 17:10; Jer 2:20; compare Deut 12:2; 2Kin 16:4; 2Chr 28:4 (these two + במות‎); also Hosea 4:13; Jer 13:27; 17:2; Ezek 6:13 (see above).

3 very commonly || הר‎ in poetry & prophets Deut 33:15; Psa 72:3; 114:4; 114:6; 148:9; Song 2:8; 4:6; Isa 2:2, 14; 30:17, 25; 31:4; 40:4, 12; 41:15; 42:15; 54:10; 55:12; 65:7; Jer 3:23; 4:24; 16:16; 50:7; Ezek 6:3; 34:6; 35:8; 36:4, 6; Hosea 4:13; 10:8; Josh 4:18; Amos 9:13; Micah 4:1; 6:1; Nahum 1:5; Hab 3:6; rarely in prose Deut 12:2; sometimes as high and majestic (poetry) ׳ג עולם‎ Gen 49:26; Deut 33:15; Hab 3:6 ('everlasting hills'); compare also Job 15:7; Prov 8:25(with adjective high, compare above); see also Jer 49:16.

4 hills with special names, some nearly or quite = proper name, of a location, which see under the respective words: ׳ג מֹרֶה‎ Judg 7:1 teacher's hill, in valley of Jezreel; ׳ג הָעֲרָלוֺת‎ Josh 5:3 hill of the fore-skins; ׳ג הָאֱלֹהִים‎ 1Sam 10:5 (a designation of Gibeah); ׳ג הַחֲכִילָה‎ 23:19; 26:1, 3; ׳ג אַמָּה‎ 2Sam 2:24; ׳ג הַלְּבוֺנָה‎ Song 4:6 (i.e. hill where frankincense is grown); ׳ג גָּרֵב֑‎ Jer 31:39; ׳ג יְרוּשָׁלַם‎ Isa 10:32; compare 31:4 (where || הַרצִֿיּוֺן‎), Ezek 34:26 (see above) & הַגְּבָעוֺת‎ Zeph 1:10 hills on which Jerusalem stands.

גבעון.def:
H1391. Gibon

גִּבְעוֺן‎ proper name, of a location — ׳ג‎ Josh 9:17 +; with ָ  ה‎ locative; גִּבְע֫וֺנָה‎ 2Sam 2:12 compare 1Kin 3:4; — Levitical city in tribe of Benjamin; formerly inhabited by Hivites Josh 9:17; 10:2, 4, 5, 10, 12, 41; 11:19; 18:25; 21:17; 2Sam 2:12-13, (pool of Gibeon) 2:16; 3:30; 20:8; Jer 28:1; 41:12 (great waters which are in Gibeon) 41:16; 1Chr 14:16; see especially ג ׳אַנְשֵׁי ג, ׳יוֺשְׁבַי‎ Josh 9:3, (called Hivites 9:7) 10:1, 6; 11:19; Neh 3:7, so ג ׳בְּנֵי‎ 7:25 (= גִבָּר בְּנֵי‎ Ezra 2:20, see גִּבָּר‎); compare also as proper name, masculine 1Chr 8:29 גִבְעוֺן אֲבִי יָָֽשְׁבו וּבְגִבְעוֺן‎ = 9:35; compare ג ׳מִדְבַּר‎ 2Sam 2:24, בְּג ׳עֵמֶק‎ Isa 28:21; it was the site of great Bamah 1Kin 3:4-5, 9:2, where was 'the tabernacle of Yahweh in the high place' according to 1Chr 16:39; compare 21:20; 2Chr 1:13 (twice in verse).

גבעוני.def:
H1393. Giboni

גִּבְעֹנִי‎ adjective, of a people — always with article הַגִּבְעֹנִי‎ Neh 3:7, הַגִּבְעוֺנִי‎ 1Chr 12:4, הַגִּבְעֹנִים‎ 2Sam 21:1-2,(twice in verse); 21:3-4, 9.

גבעל.def:
H1392. gibol

גִּבְעֹל‎ noun [masculine] bud (Ol§ 216 b) — Exod 9:31 the flax was bud (i.e. in bud Dr§ 188, (2)), compare RSJPh xii.299, 300.

גבעת.def:
H1394. Gibath

גִּבְעַת‎ proper name, of a location (Ges§ 80, R. 2) see foregoing, 2

גבעתי.def:
H1395. Gibathi

גִּבְעָתִי‎ adjective, of a people of גִּבְעָה‎ of Benjamin (?) 1Chr 12:3.

גבר.def:
H1401. gibbar

[גִּבָּר‎] noun masculine mighty one; — plural construct גִּבָּרֵיֿ חַיִל‎ Dan 3:20 (= Biblical Hebrew חַיִל גִּבּוֺרֵי‎).

גבריאל.def:
H1403. Gabriel

גַּבְרִיאֵל‎ proper name, masculine (man of El) an arch-angel Dan 8:16; 9:21(compare Luke 1:19).

גבשׁ‎ (be firm, massive, compare Assyrian gâbašu, be thick massive, ZimBP 76, & derivatives; compare also Aramaic גַּבֵּשׁ‎; Pa`el heap up & גַּבְשׁוּשִׁית‎ height, hill).

גברת.def:
H1404. gebereth

גְּבֶ֫רֶת‎ noun feminine 1. lady, queen, Isa 47:5, 7.

2 mistress of servants, suffix גְּבִרְתִּי‎ Gen 16:8; גְּבִרְתֵךְ‎ 16:9; גְּבִרְתָּהּ‎ 16:4; 2Kin 5:3; Psa 123:2; Prov 30:23; (plural גברת‎ women MI16).

גבתון.def:
H1405. Gibbethon

גִּבְּתוֺן‎ proper name, of a location (mound, height, compare גִּבְבָא ᵑ7‎ ridge) Philistine city 1Kin 15:27 (twice in verse); 16:15, 17; assigned to Dan Josh 19:44, and to Levites 21:23: site unknown; compare LagOnom. 246, 2nd ed. 255.

גבה‎ (collect, Arabic (= ?, compare גבא‎ above), Late Hebrew גָּבָה גְּבי,‎, Aramaic גְּבָא‎, ; || form גבא‎ q. v.)

גג.def:
H1406. gag

גָּג‎ noun masculine roof, top (Late Hebrew id.; Di compare Ethiopic vinculum (ferreum), jugo simil. collare ferreum; √ dubious; Thes proposes גגג‎; perhaps גנג‎ (= גנגן‎) cover Bö§ 292 Sta§ 189 a MV) — גָּג‎ Josh 2:6 9t. + 1Sam 9:26 Kt (Qr גָּ֫גָה‎), גָּ֫גָה‎ Josh 2:6; 1Sam 9:26 Qr (Kt גג‎); construct Judg 9:51 2t. + Ezek 40:13 (strike out Co see below); suffix גַּגֶּךָ֑‎ Deut 22:8, גַּגּוֺ‎ Exod 30:3 2t. + Ezek 40:13 (strike out Co see below); plural גַּגּוֺת‎ Isa 37:27 5t.; suffix גַּגּוֺתֶיהָ‎ 15:3, גַּגּוֺתֵיהֶם‎ Jer 32:29, גַּגֹּתֵיהֶם‎ 19:13; —

1 roof (of house) Deut 22:8; Josh 2:6 (twice in verse); 2:8; Joshua 16:27; 1Sam 9:25-26, 2Sam 11:2 (twice in verse); 16:22; 2Kin 19:26 = Isa 37:27; Neh 8:16; Psa 102:8; 129:6; Prov 21:9; 25:24; Isa 15:3; 22:1; Jer 48:38; as places of idolatrous worship (especially of heavenly bodies) 19:13; 32:29; Zeph 1:5; so אָחָז עֲלִיַּת הַגָּג‎ 2Kin 23:12, roof of tower Judg 9:51, 51, over gate 2Sam 18:24, of chamber Ezek 40:13 (twice in verse) (but ᵐ5‎ Co קיר‎).

2 top of altar of incense, in tabernacle Exod 30:3; 37:26 (both p).

גֻּדְגֹּדָה גִּדְּגָּד, גָּד, גַּד,‎ see below גדד‎.

גד.def:
H1410. Gad

III. גָּד‎71 proper name, masculine (fortunatus? perhaps derived from foregoing divine name SiegfJPTh 1875, 364 StaGeschichte.i.148; but see also BaeRel 159f.) — שָגּד‎ Gen 35:26 +, as well as גָּד֑‎ 30:11 +; —

1 son of Jacob and Zilpah;

a. strictly as personal name Gen 30:11; 35:26; 46:16; Exod 1:4 compare Gen 49:19; 1Chr 2:2.

b. as name of tribe Num 1:14; Deut 27:13; 33:20 (twice in verse); Josh 18:7; Ezek 48:27-28, compare גָּד אֶרֶץ‎ 1Sam 13:7 see also Jer 49:1, גָּד שַׁעַד‎ Ezek 48:34, on הַגָּד הַנַּחַל‎ 2Sam 24:5 compare We Dr; explicitly גָּד מַטֵּה‎ Num 1:25; 2:14; 13:15; Josh 13:24; 20:8; 21:7, 36; 1Chr 6:48; 6:65; once, בְנֵיגָֿד מַטֵּה צְבָא‎ Num 10:20; גָד בְּנֵי‎ (MI10 גד אש‎) 1:24 12t. Numbers; Josh 4:12 14t. Joshua; 1Chr 5:11; 12:14.

2 a prophet in David's time, called נָבִיא‎ 1Sam 22:5, but דָוִד חֹזֶה הַנָּבִיא‎ 2Sam 24:11 & דָוִיד חֹזֵה‎ || 1Chr 21:9, הַחֹזֶה‎ 29:29 & חֹזֵההַֿמֶּלֶךְ‎2Chr 29:25.

גדבר.def:
H1411. gedaberayya

דְָֽבְרַיָּא‎ noun masculine plural emphatic Dan 3:2-3, dubious: most think || form of [גַּזְבָּר‎] treasurer (or, MeyEntst. J. 23, textual error for ׳גז‎); Gr Bev and others read הַדָּֽבְרַיָּא‎ ministers (3:24); possibly (see Lag Dr and others) dittograph for following דְּתָֽבְרַיָּא‎.

גדגד.def:
H1412. Gudgodah

גֻּדְגֹּ֫דָה‎ with article הַגֻּדְגֹּ֫דָה‎ proper name, of a location (meaning dubious) station of Israel in wilderness Deut 10:7 (twice in verse) (in || Num 33:32 הַגִּדְגָּ֑ד חֹר‎ see below חֹר‎).

גדד.def:
H1413. gadad

[גָּדַד‎] verb penetrate, cut (Late Hebrew id., cut, cut out, Aramaic גְּדַד‎, , Arabic cut, cut off; Ethiopic in derivatives) —

Qal Imperfect Psa 94:21 צַדִּיִק עַלנֶֿפֶשׁ יָג֯וֺדּוּ‎ they attack (penetrate, make inroads upon) the life of a righteous man (Ol proposes יָגוּרוּ‎ compare 56:7; 59:4 where, however, Che יגודו‎; si vera lectio, perhaps denominative from גְּדוּד‎ compare Hosea 6:9 & below; compare also גוד‎ & Köi. 356).

Hithpo`el Imperfect יִתְגֹּדַד‎ Jer 16:6; 2feminine singular תִּתְגֹּדֲדִי‎ Micah 4:14, תִּתְגּוֺדָ֑דִי‎ 47:5; plural וַיִּתְגֹּדְדוּ‎ 1Kin 18:28, יִתְגּוֺדָ֑דוּ‎ Jer 5:7 + Hosea 7:11 see below, תִּתְגֹּדְדוּ‎ Deut 14:1; Participle plural מִתְגֹּדְדִים‎ Jer 41:5; —

1 cut oneself, as religious (heathen) practice 1Kin 18:28; practised also by men of Schechem, etc. in worship of ׳י‎ (late) Jer 41:5; for the dead, forbidden Deut 14:1 לָמֵת עֵינֵיכֶם בֵּין קָרְחָה תָשִׂימוּ וְלאֹ תִתְגֹּדְדוּ לֹא‎, Jer 16:6; compare 47:5 (subject Philistia personified); also for יִתְגּוֺרָ֖רוּ ᵑ0‎ Hosea 7:14 Codd, they cut themselves, ᵐ5‎ Gr Che RVm, We Now Marti Harper (compare I, II. גּוּר‎).

2 gather in troops, or bands; go in troops or throngs, throng; (denominative from גְּדוּד‎ q. v.) compare בַתגְּֿדוּד תִּתְגֹּדֲדִי‎ Micah 4:14 (addressed to Jerusalem); Jer 5:7 יִתְגּ זוֺנָה ׳וּבֵית‎ and to a harlot's house they throng. **read probably ᵐ5 יִתְגֹּרָ֑רוּ‎ Gie Du and others.

גדוד.def:
H1416. gedud

I. גְּדוּד‎ noun masculineGen 49:19 band, troop (as making inroads; others, as a division, detachment (as severed), but this usually later in Hebrew) — ׳ג‎ absolute 1Sam 30:8 19t.; construct 2Chr 25:9; plural גְּדוּדִים‎ 2Sam 4:2 2t.; construct גְּדוּדֵי‎ 2Kin 6:23 6t.; suffix גְּדוּדָיו‎ Job 19:12; 25:3; —

1 marauding band (making incursions, inroads, compare גדד‎) 1Sam 30:8, 15 (twice in verse); 30:23 compare 1Chr 12:22, also 2Chr 22:1; 1Kin 11:24; 2Kin 5:2; 6:23; 13:20-21, 24:2 (4 t. in verse) compare 2Sam 22:30 = Psa 18:30, & Gen 49:19 (see גַּד‎ 30:11) Hosea 6:9; 7:1; Jer 18:22; גִּדוּדִים שָׂרֵי‎ 2Sam 4:2, compare הַגְּדוּד בְּרָאשֵׁי וַיִּתְּנֵם‎ 1Chr 12:19; figurative of God's attacking forces, his chastisements Job 19:12 (compare 25:3 below)

2 troop, of divisions of army of Israel (late) מִלְחָמָה צְבָא גְּדוּדֵי‎ 1Chr 7:4, compare 2Chr 26:11; band of Israel, i.e. troop of mercenaries hired from Israel by Amaziah 25:9-10, הַגְּדוּד בְּנֵי‎ i.e. soldiers of the band25:13; of army in General בַּגְּדוּד כְּמֶלֶךְ‎ Job 29:25, in simile; also Micah 4:14 בַּתגְּֿדוּד‎ of Zion.

3 foray, raid 2Sam 3:22.

גדודה.def:
H1417. gedud

or gedudah II. [גְּדוּד‎, or גְּדוּדָה‎] noun [masculine or feminine] furrow, cutting —

1 furrow, plural defective גְּדוּדֶ֑הָ‎ Psa 65:11 (|| תְּלָמֶיהָ‎). 2 plural גְּדֻדֹת‎, cuttings upon hands, compare גדד‎ Hithpo`el

2 sign of mourning Jer 48:37 (|| שׂק‎).

גדול.def:
H1419. gadol

גָּדוֺל‎522 adjective great — ׳ג‎Gen 4:13 279t.; גָּדֹל‎ Deut 26:8 22t.; construct גְּדוֺל‎ Ezek 17:3, 7; Jer 32:19, גְּדָלֿ‎ Prov 19:19, גְּדָו֯לֿ‎ Psa 145:8; Nahum 1:3; suffix גְּדוֺלָם‎ Jer 6:13 2t.; plural גְּדוֺלִים‎ Exod 7:4 11t., גְּדֹלִים‎ Gen 12:17 22t.; construct גְּדֹלֵי‎ 2Kin 10:6; suffix גְּדֹלָיו‎ 10:11; Jonah 3:7; גְּדוֺלֶיהָ‎Nahum 3:10; feminine גְּדוֺלָה‎ Num 22:18 96t.; גְּדֹלָה‎ Gen 15:12 31t.; plural גְּדוֺלֹת‎ Neh 9:26; 12:31, גְּדֹלוֺת‎ Deut 27:2 30t., גְּדֹלֹת‎ Num 13:28 7t.; — great,

1 in magnitude and extent, e.g. sea Num 34:6, river Gen 15:18, wilderness Deut 1:19, rain 1Kin 18:45, mountain Zech 4:7, city Gen 10:12, house Jer 52:13, altar Josh 22:10, throne 2Chr 9:17, sea-monsters Gen 1:21, fish Jonah 2:1, eagle Ezek 17:3, terebinth 2Sam 18:9, substance Gen 15:14, wealth Dan 11:2, victory 1Sam 19:5, 22 הַגָּדוֺל בּוֺר‎ read ׳ב הַגֹּרֶן‎ according to ᵐ5‎ We Dr.

2 in number, e.g. nation Gen 12:2, congregation Jer 31:8, camp 1Chr 12:22, army Ezek 17:17, sacrifice 2Kin 10:19, slaughter Deut 28:59; 1Sam 4:17.

3 in intensity, fear Deut 4:34, weeping Isa 38:3, power כּחַ‎ Exod 32:11, joy Jonah 4:6, anger Deut 29:23, indignation Jer 21:5, sin Gen 20:9, iniquity 4:13, evil 39:9, trespass Ezek 9:7.

4 in sound, loud voice Gen 39:14, cry Exod 11:6, shout Josh 6:5.

5 in age, elder, eldest, son Gen 27:1, daughter 29:16, brother 10:21, sister Ezek 16:46.

6 in importance,

a. things (הַ)גָּדֹל (הַ)דָּבָר‎ an important thing or affair Exod 18:22; Deut 4:32; 1Sam 12:16; 2Kin 5:12; 8:13; יהוה יום‎ Jer 30:7; Hosea 2:2; Joel 2:11; 3:4; Zeph 1:14; Malachi 3:23.

b. of men, great, distinguished, Moses Exod 11:3, David 2Sam 5:10, Job Job 1:3, Mordecai Est 9:4, kings Eccl 9:14; Jer 27:7; especially of king of Assyr. הַגָּדוֺל הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ 2Kin 18:19, 28 = Isa 36:4, 18, = Assyrian šarru rabbu, šarru dannu, e.g. KBi. 94, 1. 1; הַגָּדוֺל הַכֹּהֵן‎ the h.p. Lev 21:10 20t.; גָּדוֺל (הָ)אִישׁ‎ 1Sam 25:2; 2Sam 19:33; 2Kin 5:1; גְדוֺלָה אִשָּׁה‎ 4:8; גָּדוֺל‎ a great man 2Sam 3:38; Micah 7:3; גָדוֺל מְּנֵי תֶהְדַּר לֹא‎ thou shalt not honour (favour) the person of a great man (opposed to דָּל‎) Lev 19:15 (H); (הַ)גְּדוֺלִים‎ the great 2Sam 7:9 = 1Chr 17:8; Neh 11:14 (see below) Prov 18:16; 25:6; Jer 5:5 (2Kin 10:11 ᵐ5‎L ἀγχιστεύοντας, Klo גֹּאֲלָיו‎); further הָעִיר גְּדֹלֵי‎ 10:6; (כָּלֿ)גְּדֹלָיו‎ 10:11; Jonah 3:7; גְּדוֺלֶיהָ כָּלֿ‎ Nahum 3:10.

c. of God, himself2Chr 2:4; Neh 4:8; 8:6; Psa 86:10; 99:2; 135:5; 147:5; Isa 12:6; Jer 10:6; (הַ)גָּדוֺל (הָ)אֵל‎ Deut 7:21; 10:17; Neh 1:5; 9:32; Psa 77:14; 95:3; Jer 32:18; Dan 9:4; האלהים מכל גדול‎ Exod 18:11; מאד ומהלל גדול‎ 1Chr 16:25; Psa 48:2; 96:4; 145:3; גדול מלך‎ 47:3; 95:3; Mal 1:14; his works Deut 11:7; Judg 2:7; Psa 111:2, glory 21:6; 138:5, name Josh 7:9; 1Sam 12:22; 1Kin 8:42; 2Chr 6:32; Psa 76:2; 99:3; Jer 10:6; 44:26; Ezek 36:23; Mal 1:11 (twice in verse), mercy 1Kin 3:6; 2Chr 1:8; Psa 57:11; 86:13; 108:5, goodness Neh 9:25, compassion Isa 54:7.

גדיש.def:
H853. eth

I. אֵת‎, with makk. אֶתֿ‎, with suffix אֹתִי‎; אֹתְכָה אֹתְךָ,‎ Num 22:33, אֹתָ֑כָה אֹתָ֑ךְ,‎ Exod 29:35, feminine אֹתָךְ‎; אֹתוֺ‎ etc.; 2 plural אֶתְכֶם‎, once אוֺתְכֶם‎ Josh 23:15; 3masculine plural regularly אֹתָם‎, rarely אֶתְהֶם‎ Gen 32:1; Exod 18:20; Num 21:3; Ezek 34:12; 1Chr 6:50, once אוֺתְהֶם‎ Ezek 23:45; 3feminine plural, on the contrary, regularly אֶתְהֶן‎ (13 t.), once אֹתָן‎ 16:54 (also אוֺתְהֶן‎ 23:47, אֹתָ֖נָה‎ Exod 35:26, אוֺתָ֖נָה‎ Ezek 34:21); forms with cholem also often written plene: — the

mark of the accusative, prefixed as a rule only to nouns that are definite (Moabite id., Phoenician אית‎ i.e. אִיַּת‎ (Schrödp. 213 f.); Aramaic יָת‎ frequently in ᵑ7‎; Syriac very rare as mark of accusative (for which is preferred), but used often in the sense of substance οὐσία, also in that of self, e.g. per se, reapse, sibi ipsi, PS1640f., Samaritan ; Arabic , only used with suffix, when it is desired to emphasize the pronoun, e.g. Qor 1:4 WAG i. § 189. [Ethiopic uses k£y¹ similarly, Di§ 150 a; but it is dubious if this is etymologically akin.] The primitive form will have been 'iwyath, originally a substantive with following Genitive, Olp. 432; whether ultimately a parallel development with אוֺת‎ sign from √ אוה‎ is uncertain: Ol WAG i. § 188 LagM i. 226 affirm, NöZMG 1886, 738 doubts. In Hebrew the ground-form is אוֺת‎; the forms with ¢, e being abbreviated. In post Biblical Hebrew, used in combination with another preposition: thus הַיּוֺם בְּאוֺתוֺ‎ = Bibl. הַשָּׁעָה בְּאוֺתָהּ הַהוּא, בַּיּוֺם‎; or as a nomin., e.g. הָאִישׁ אוֺתוֺ‎ = Bibl. הַהוּא הָאִישׁ‎).

1 As mark of the accusative prefixed to substantives defined either by the article (or כֹּל‎), or by a Genitive or pronominal affix, or in virtue of being proper names:

a. with transitive verbs, Gen 1:1, 16, 29, 30; 2:11; 4:1-2, 9:3 (אֶתֿכֹּל׃‎) etc. Similarly אֶתמִֿי‎ whom (in particular), Josh 24:15; 1Sam 12:3; 28:11; Isa 6:8 and elsewhere (but never אֶתמָֿה‎); also with זֶה‎ Gen 29:33; 44:29; 1 Samuel 21:16; 1Kin 22:27 +, זֹאת‎ Gen 29:27; 2Sam 13:27 +, אֵלֶּה‎ Gen 46:18; Lev 11:18; Isa 49:21 +. So pretty uniformly in prose; but in poetry את‎ is commonly dispensed with. By the use of את‎ with the pronominal affix, a pronoun can at once, if required, be placed in a position of emphasis; let the order of words from this point of view be carefully noticed in the following passages: Gen 7:1; 24:14; 37:4; Lev 10:17; 11:33; Num 22:32 thee I had slain, and her I had kept alive, Deut 4:14; 6:13, 23; 13:5; Judg 14:3 לִי קַח אוֺתָהּ‎ take for me her, 1Sam 14:35; 15:1; 18:17; 21:10 קָ֔ח תִּקַּחלְֿךָ אִםאֹֿתָהּ‎ if thou wilt take that, take it, 1Kin 1:35; 14:9; Isa 43:22; 57:11; Jer 9:2. So הַאוֺתִי‎ 5:22; 7:19. It also sometimes enables the reflexive sense to be expressed (elsewhere נַפְשָׁם‎) 7:19; Ezek 34:2. Rarely with a substantive which is undefined (Ew§ 277 d 2 Ges§ 117, 1, R. 2), as Exod 21:28; Num 21:9; Lev 20:14; 1Sam 24:6 (but see Dr) 2Sam 4:11; 18:18; 23:21; or which, though definite, is without the article, Gen 21:30; 2Sam 15:16; Lev 26:5; 1Sam 9:3 (so Num 16:15) Isa 33:19; 41:7; Ezek 43:10 (for further examples see Ew 1.c.)

b. with a passive verb (Ges§ 121. 1 Ew§ 295 b) conceived as expressing neutrally the action in question, and construed accordingly with an accusative of that which is its real object: examples occur with tolerable frequency from Gen 4:18 (J) אֶתעֿירָד לַחֲנוֺךְ וַיִּוָּלֵד‎, 17:5 (P), אַברָם אֶתשִֿׁמְךָ עוֺד יִקָּרֵא לֹא‎ there shall not be called (=one shall not call) thy name Abram, 21:5 (E), 27:42; 2Sam 21:11; 1Kin 18:13; Hosea 10:6 etc., to Jer 35:18; 38:4; 50:20; Ezek 16:4-5, Est 2:13 (compare DrJPh xi. 227 f.): also with passive verbs of filling (Ew§ 281 b), as Exod 1:7 +.

c. with neuter verbs or expressions, especially such as involve the idea of regarding, or treating, appy. by a construction κατὰ σύνεσιν (rare), Josh 22:17; 2Sam 11:25; Neh 9:32 (compare 1Sam 20:13 Dr). Once after אֵין‎, Hag 2:17; אֵלַיָֽ אֶתְכֶם אֵין‎.

d. poet. (si vera lectio), after an abstract noun used with a verbal force, Hab 3:13 (Amos 4:11; Isa 13:19; Jer 50:40 מַהְמֵּכָה‎ exerts a verbal force, like the Arabic nom. verbi [see WAG i. § 196, 43]; and Num 10:2; Ezek 17:9 לְמַשְׂאוֺת לְמַסַּע,‎ are Aramaizing infinitives: compare Ew§ 239 a).

2 את‎ marks an accusative in other relations than that of direct object to a verb: a. with verbs of motion (very rare) Num 13:17; Deut 1:19; 2:7 (to 'walk the wilderness'); denoting the goal Judg 19:18; Ezek 21:25 (Ew§ 281 d, n., 282 a 1). b. denoting time (duration), also very rare: Exod 13:7; Lev 25:22; Deut 9:25. c. expressing the accus. of limitation (rare): Gen 17:11, 14; 1Kin 15:23.

3 Chiefly in an inferior or later style, אֵת‎ (or וְאֵת‎) is used irregularly, partly (α), as it would seem, to give greater definiteness (so especially וְאֵת‎) at the mention of a new subject (when it may sometimes be rendered as regards), or through the influence of a neighbouring verb (a construct κατὰ σύνεσιν), or by an anacoluthon, partly (β) as resuming loosely some other preposition Thus (α) Exod 1:14; Num 3:26, 46; 5:10 (with הָיָה‎: so Ezek 35:10) Num 18:21b Deut 11:2 (anacoluthon), 14:13; Josh 17:11; Judg 20:44, 46 (contr. 20:25; 20:35) 1Sam 17:34 (see Dr) 26:16; 2Sam 21:22; 2Kin 6:5; Isa 53:8 (probably), 57:12; Jer 23:33 (but read rather with הַמַּשָּׂא אַתֶּם ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎) 27:8; 36:22; 38:16 Kt, 45:4 b Ezek 16:22; 17:21; 20:16; 29:4; b 43:7 (ᵐ5‎ Co prefix הֲרָאִיתָ‎) 44:3; Zech 8:17; Eccl 4:3; Dan 9:13; Neh 9:19, 34; 1Chr 2:9; 2Chr 31:17. In 1Sam 30:23; Hag 2:5 probably some such word as remember is to be understood. (β) Jer 38:9; Ezek 14:22; b 37:19 b Zech 12:10; אֵת סָבִיב‎ 1Kin 6:5; Ezek 43:17 strangely (in 1Kings ᵐ5‎ omits the clause: so StaZAW 1883, 135). — In 1Kin 11:1 וְ‎ is merely and also, and especially (see וְ‎); 11:25 is corrupt (read with הֲדָד עָשָׂה אֲשֶׁר הָרָעָה זֹאת ᵐ5‎); Ezek 47:17-18, 19 read similarly for זֹאת ואת,‎: see 47:20. — For some particulars as to the use of את‎, see A. M. WilsonHebraica. vi. 139 ff. 212 ff. (who, however, confuses it sometimes with II. אֵת‎). For denoting the pronominal object of a verb, את‎ with suffix preponderates relatively much above the verbal affix in P, as compared with J E Deuteronomy Judges Samuel Kings (see GieZAW 1881, 258 f.), — partly, probably, on account of the greater distinctness and precision which P loves.

יָת‎ mark of accusative (= Biblical Hebrew I. אֵת‎; Palmyrene ית‎; ZinjirliHad. 28 with suffix ותה‎; Nabataean, Palmyrene with suffix יתה‎ (Lzb263 Cooke170; compare RÉS468); ᵑ7‎ Samaritan יָת‎; Syriac (rare)); — Dan 3:12 יָָֽתְהוֺן מַנִּיתָ דִּי‎ whom thou hast appointed.

Qal Perfect גָּדַע‎ Lam 2:3; וְגָדַעְתִּ֫י‎ 1Sam 2:31; Imperfect וָאָגְדַּע‎ Zech 11:10, 14; Participle passive גְּדוּעָה‎ Isa 15:2 (so many editions but) Baer גְּרוּעָה‎; compare below, גְּדֻעִים‎ 10:33; — hew, cut in two, a staff Zech 11:10, 14; metaphor hew off, an arm 1Sam 2:31; horns Lam 2:3; hew down, trees Isa 10:33; if in 15:2 then = shave off (object זקן‎, beard), but no other indication of this meaning, and true גְּרוּעָה ᵑ0‎, compare Baer's note & Jer 48:37; see גרע‎.

Niph`al Perfect נִגְדַּע‎ Judg 21:6 נֶגְדַּע‎ Jer 50:23; 3feminine singular נִגְדְּעָה‎ 48:25; וְנִגְדְּעָה‎ consecutive Isa 22:25; 2masculine singular נִגְדַּעְתָּ‎ 14:12; 3plural וְנִגְדְּעוּ‎ consecutive Ezek 6:6; Amos 3:14; — be hewn off, of altar-horns 3:14, of idols Ezek 6:6 (|| נשׁבר‎); of severance of a tribe from nation Judg 21:6; figurative of king of Babylon Isa 14:12; of Babylon as hammer Jer 50:23 (|| נשׁבר‎); of a minister, under figure of secure peg or pin Isa 22:25; of horn of Moab Jer 48:25 (|| נשׁבר‎).

Pi`el revile, blaspheme (Late Hebrew גָּדַף‎ cut, wound, then (especially Pi) revile; Arabic cut, cut off, II. deny a favour, be ungrateful, etc.; Aramaic Pa`el גַּדֵּף‎, , revile) — Perfect2masculine singular וְגִדַּפְתָּ‎ 2Kin 19:22 = Isa 37:23; 3plural גִּדְּפוּ‎ 2Kin 19:6 = Isa 37:6; Participle מְגַדֵּף‎ Num 15:30; Psa 44:17; —

1 revile, between man and man, (absolute) וּמְגַדֵּף מְחָרֵף קוֺל‎ Psa 44:17 the voice of (him that) reproacheth and revileth.

2 blaspheme, followed by accusative ׳י‎ Num 15:30 (P); 2Kin 19:22 = Isa 37:23 (|| חֵרֵף‎; object אֶתמִֿי‎, reference to ׳י‎ as above); Ezek 20:27; 2accusative ג ׳אֲשֶׁר אֹתִי אַשּׁוּר מֶלֶךְ נַעֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים‎ ... 2Kin 19:6 = Isa 37:6 the words with which the servants of the king of Assyria blaspheme me.

1 house, a. as dwelling habitation Gen 19:2-3, 4, 11; 27:15; 33:17 (object of בָּנָה‎) Exod 12:7 + often; ׳בּ מוֺשַׁב‎ Lev 25:29 (compare לְשִׁבְתִּי בַּיִת‎ 2Sam 7:5); בֵּית‎ = in the house of, when modifying word follows, compare DrSm 29, n. 2 (after stative construct חוּץ מוֺלֶדֶת אוֺ בַּיִת מוֺלֶדֶת‎ Lev 19:9); e.g. ׳בּ אָבִיךָ‎ Gen 24:23; ׳בּ אִישָׁהּ‎ Num 30:11 ׳בּ יהוה‎ 2Kin 23:24; so in proper name ביתאל‎ Amos 7:13; (ה)בַּ֫יְתָה‎ into the house, home Exod 9:19 (of man & beast) compare, Judg 19:18; 1Sam 6:7 (compare 6:10) 1Kin 13:7, 15; Psa 68:7; Isa 14:17 etc.; compare below 7 below; partic (α) in J occasionally of tent Gen 27:15; compare 33:17 (with בנה‎; here of nomad's hut); usually (β) house of solid materials, with doorposts, etc. Exod 12:7; Deut 6:9; 11:20, walls Lev 14:37, 39, of stones, timber & mortar 14:45 (compare 14:40; 14:42; 14:43); so also Josh 2:15; supported by pillars Judg 16:26f.; with roof on which one could walk 2Sam 11:12 etc.; see especially temple and king's house in Jerusalem 1 Kings 5-7 etc.; compare Song 1:7; Jer 22:14; of Ezekiel's temple Ezekiel 40f.; סְפוּנִים בָּֽתֵּכֶם‎ of luxurious houses Hag 1:4; טֹבִים בָּֽתִּים בנה‎ Deut 8:12; בַּיִתחָֿדָשׁ בּנה‎ 20:5; compare 22:8; also with בנה‎ 28:30 + often; (γ) construct before word of material, ׳בּ אֲרָזִים‎ 2Sam 7:2, 7 = 1Chr 17:1 (׳בּ ׳הַא‎) 17:6; ׳בּ הַשֵּׁן‎ 1Kin 22:39 compare Amos 3:15; ׳בּ גָּזִית‎ house of hewn stone 5:11; compare הַלְּבָנוֺן יַעַר בֵּית‎ 1Kin 7:2; 2Chr 9:20, הַיַּעַר בֵּית‎ Isa 22:8; (δ) also before word of quality or characteristic, אֵבֶל בֵּית‎ Eccl 7:2 || ׳בּ מִשְׁתֶּה‎ 7:4 || ׳בּ שִׂמְחָה‎; ׳בּ מַרְזֵחַ‎ Jer 16:5; ׳בּ מִשְׁתֶּה‎ 16:8; חֶמְדָּתֵךְ בָּֽתֵּי‎ Ezek 26:12; תַּעֲנֻגֶי֑הָ בֵּית‎ Micah 2:9; compare ׳בּ מְרִי‎ rebellious house below 5. d below; (ε) in combinations, of structures for various purposes: — (1) הַמֶּלֶךְ בֵּית‎ = palace 1Kin 9:1, 10; 10:12 +, etc.; מַמְלָכָה בֵּית‎ Amos 7:13 compare below

2 below; ׳בּ הַמַּלְכוּת‎ Est 5:1; compare 2:16; ׳בּ לְמַלְכוּתוֺ‎2Chron 1:18; (2) הַסֹּהַר בֵּית‎ = the prison Gen 39:20 (twice in verse); 39:21-22, (twice in verse); 39:23; 40:3, 5; compare ׳בּ מִשְׁמַרְכֶם‎ 42:19; ׳בּ מִשְׁמֶרֶת‎ 2Sam 20:3; הָאָסוּר ׳בּ‎ Jer 37:15; ׳בּ הָאֲסיּרים‎ Judg 16:21, 25; ׳בּ הָסֿוּרִים‎ Eccl 4:14; ׳בּ הַכֶּלֶא‎ 1Kin 22:27; 2Kin 17:4; 2Chr 18:26; Jer 37:15, 18 compare Isa 42:7; ׳בּ כֶּלֶא‎ 2Kin 25:27; ׳בּ הַמַּהְמֶּכֶת‎2Chr 16:10; ׳בּ הַכְּליּ֯א‎ Jer 37:4; 52:31; כְלָאִים בָּֽתֵּי‎ Isa 42:22; בֵּיתהַֿבּוֺר‎ Jer 37:16; ׳בּ הַמְּקֻדּוֺת‎ 52:31; -3הַנָּשִׁים בֵּית‎ house of the women, harem Est 2:9, 11, 13, 14; -4׳בּ הַיַּיִן מִשְׁתֵּה‎ 7:8; ׳בּ הַיָּ֑יִן‎ Song 2:4; compare מָשׂוֺשׂ בָּֽתֵּי‎ Isa 32:13; -5הַחֹרֶף בֵּית‎ Amos 3:15; Jer 36:22; בּ ׳הַקָּ֑יִץ‎ Amos 3:15; -6נְכֹתֹה בֵּית‎ & כֵּלָיו בֵּית‎ 2Kin 20:13 = Isa 39:2; -7הַגָּן בֵּית‎ garden-h. Ezekiel + 9:9 above; also ׳בּ וּבִנְיָמִן יְהוּדָה‎ 1Kin 12:23; ׳בּ יְהוּדָה מֶלֶךְ‎ Jer 21:11; 22:6; (ζ) ׳בּ יוֺסֵף‎ Gen 50:8; Josh 17:17; 18:5 (all J E) Judg 1:22-23, 35; 2Sam 19:21; 1Kin 11:28; Amos 5:6; Obadiah 18; Zech 10:6; (η) ׳בּ אֶפְרַיִם‎ Judg 10:9; (θ) ׳בּ בִּנְיָמִן‎ 2Sam 3:19 compare 1Kin 12:23 above; (ι) ׳בּ יִשָּׂשכָר‎ 15:27; (κ) ׳בּ לֵוִי‎ Exod 2:1 (E) Numbers 17:23 (P) Zech 12:13 (ב ׳משׁפחת ׳ל‎), Psa 135:20; & (λ) ׳בּ אַהֲרֹן‎ 115:10; 115:12; 118:3; 135:19.

Numbers; Josh 22:14 (twice in verse); 1Chr 4:38; 5:13 25t. Chronicles; Ezra 2:59; 10:16; Neh 7:61; 10:35; = tribe Numbers 17:17 (twice in verse); Numbers 17:18; Numbers 17:21; = main division of tribe Num 3:20, 24 +, compare 34:14 (twice in verse) etc.; futher sub-division Exod 12:3; 1Chr 7:2, 7 +; compare especially 23:11 Jeush and Beriah had not many sons, therefore they became אֶחָ֑ת לִפְקֻדָּה אָב לְבֵית‎ (compare אבות ראשׁי‎, below אב‎).

6 house, including household affairs, persons, property, etc. עַלבֵּֿיתוֺ וַיַּפְקִדֵהוּ‎ Gen 39:4 compare בְּבֵיתוֺ‎ 39:5; עַלבֵּֿיתוֺ אֲשֶׁר‎ 44:1, 4; hence הבית על אשׁר‎ as title of governor of the palace (EwH iii. 269) Isa 22:15; 36:3 compare 1Kin 4:6; 2Kin 15:5; in Israel 1Kin 16:9; 18:3; 2Kin 10:5: further 2Sam 17:23; 2Kin 20:1 = Isa 38:1; hence of personal property 1Kin 13:8 בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ אֶתחֲֿצִי אִםתִּֿתֶּןלִֿי‎; family and property (everything on which one depends) Job 8:15.

7 בָּ֑יְתָה בַּ֫יְתָה,‎, literally housewards, hence metaphor inwards, Exod 28:26 = 39:19 (that is, of the ephod), 1Kin 7:25 2Chr 4:4 (that is, of the circle of oxen supporting the molten sea); 2Sam 5:9 וָבָ֑יְתָה מִןהַֿמִּלּוֺא‎ from the Millo and inward, Ezek 44:17.

8 מִבַּיִת‎

a. adverb on the inside (of a building, chest, etc.: opposed to מִחוּץ‎) Gen 6:14; Exod 25:11 = 37:2; Lev 14:41; 1Kin 6:15-16, 7:9; 2Kin 6:30 (of a person's clothes); Ezek 7:15; so with ה‎ locative מִבֲַּ֫יְתָה‎ 1Kin 6:15
