גדרתי.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

גדרתים.def:
H1453. Gederothayim

גְּדֵרֹתָ֫יִם‎ proper name, of a location in Judah Josh 15:36; perhaps strike out, so ᵐ5‎; whole number too large, compare Di.

גהה.def:
H1456. gehah

גֵּהָה‎ noun feminine healing, cure — גֵּהָ֑ה‎ Prov 17:22 ג יֵיטִיב שָׂמֵחַ ׳לֵב‎ compare Now.

גהר.def:
H1457. gahar

[גָּהַר‎] verb bend, crouch (so Vrss) —

Qal Imperfect וַיִּגְהַר‎ 1Kin 18:42 followed by אַרְצָה‎ Elijah, with face between knees; 2Kin 4:34-35, Elisha, over dead boy, followed by עליו‎ (|| וישׁכב‎ 4:34, compare שׁכב‎).

גֵּו גַּו,‎ see below גוה‎.

גּוֺב‎,גּוֺבַי‎ see below גבה‎

גו.def:
H1460. gev

I. גֵּו‎ noun [masculine] back — גֵּו‎ absolute unused, construct Prov 10:13 2t., suffix גֵּוִי‎ Isa 50:6, גֵּוְךָ‎ 38:17, גֵּוֵךְ‎ 51:23; — back, as beaten, lashed Prov 10:13; 19:29; 26:3 compare Isa 50:6; in phrase ג אַחֲרֵי ׳הִשְׁלִיךְ‎ (as גַּו‎) 38:17, of Yahweh's casting sins of penitent behind his back, putting them out of mind; as trodden upon 51:23, figurative of extreme humiliation.

II. גֵּו‎ noun [masculine] midst, Aramaism (compare Aramaic גֵּו גַּוָּא,‎ middle, Late Hebrew גֵּו‎ midst, interior; id., belly, Arabic midst) Job 30:5 יְגֹרָ֑שׁוּ מִןגֵּֿו‎ from the midst (of men) they are driven; Rosenm and others compare CiceroOff. iii. 8: e medio pelluntur.

גוא.def:
H1459. gav

[גַּו‎] noun masculine midst (Egyptian Aramaic, Nabataean, Palmyrene גו‎; גָּיו ᵑ7‎; especially construct מִגּוֺ לְגוֺ, בְּגוֺ,‎; so Syriac ; compare Biblical Hebrew נֵּו‎); — construct גּוֺא‎ (so Nabataen CookeNo. 94) Dan 3:26 +, 7:15 editions, Gi גּוֺ‎ (Baer גּוֺא‎, see on 3:6); suffix 3masculine singular גַּוֵּהּ‎ Ezra 5:7, 3feminine singular גַּוַּהּ‎ 4:15; 6:2; — midst, always with prepositions:

a. בְּגוֺא‎ (= Hebrew בְּתוֺךְ‎), Dan 3:25 גוּרָא בְּגוֺא‎, 4:7; 7:15; Ezra 4:15; 5:7 בְּגַוֵהּ כְּתִיב וְכִדְנָה‎, 6:2.

b. לְגוֺא‎ Dan 3:6, 11, 15, 21, 23, 24.

c. מִןגּֿוֺא‎ Dan 3:26.

גֵּרָה‎ see גאה‎.

גוב.def:
H1359. Gob

גּוֺב גֹּב,‎ proper name, of a location see below גבב‎.

גבא‎ (compare Arabic , restrain or withhold oneself; perhaps = collect (water in a cistern, also tribute), so Lane 1. near the end, Fl NHWBi. 431; see also Late Hebrew גָּבָה גבי,‎, Aramaic גְּבָא‎, collect debts, taxes, etc.)

גֹּב‎ 2Sam 21:18, גּוֺב‎ 21:19 proper name, of a location (compare Aramaic גֻּבָּא‎ den, and , Arabic , Ethiopic Assyrian gubbu, well, cistern, see גבב‎) — field of battle with Philistines 21:18 = גֶּזֶר‎ in || 1Chr 20:4 (so here Th Ew; compare Josh 10:33), but = ᵑ6 ᵐ5 גַּת‎ 2Sam 21:18 (ᵐ5‎L Γαζεθ); 21:19 (omit || 1Chr 20:5), ᵐ5‎ Ρομ, Ροβ; Klo Gath; in 1 Chronicles 20:16 We Dr (q. v.) read בְּגֹב‎ for בְּנֹב‎; site of Gob (si vera lectio) unknown.

גוג.def:
H1463. Gog

גּוֺג‎ proper name, masculine (√ unknown) —

1 1Chr 5:4 a Reubenite.

2 Gog of the land of Magog, prince of Rosh, Meshak, and Tubal, וְתֻבָ֑ל מֶשֶׁךְ ראֹשׁ נְשִׂיא מָגוֺג אֶרֶץ גּוֺג‎ Ezek 38:2-3,(omit ׳א מגוֺג‎) 39:1 (omit id.) compare 38:14, 16 (strike out ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Co) 38:18; 39:1, 11 (3 t. in verse) (ג הֲמוֺן ׳גֵּיא‎) 39:15 (id.); compare Assyrian Gâgu, chief of a mountain tribe north of Assyria DlPa 247 COT on 38:2.

גוד.def:
H1464. gud

[גּוּד‎] verb invade, attack (compare גדד‎, whence יָגֻד‎ etc. actually derived by Ki Bö Köi. 356 q. v.; SS, perhaps better, denominative from גדוד‎) —

Qal Imperfect יָגֻד‎ Gen 49:19, יְגוּדֶ֑נּוּ‎ 49:19, יְגֻדֶנּ֑וּ‎ Hab 3:16; יגודו‎ Psa 94:21 Kt (see גדד‎); — attack Gen 49:19, alliteration with גָּד‎ proper name & ׃ עֵָקב יָגֻד וְהוּא יְגוּדֶנּ֑וּ גְּדוּד גָּד גְּדוּד,‎ Gad, a troop shall troop upon him, but he shall troop upon the heel (i.e. pursue them in their retreat) VB; Hab 3:16 יְגֻדֶ֑נּוּ לְעַם לַעֲלוֺת‎ compare VB & Comm.

גוה.def:
H1466. gevah

גֵּוָה‎ noun feminine pride (contracted for גַּאֲוָה‎ Ew§ 62 b, 73 b compare Aramaic Dan 4:34 & ᵑ7‎) —

1 pride Job 33:17; Jer 13:17.

2 lifting up Job 22:29 an exclamation, up! Ew Di De and others; but pride Hi Dr§ 154 n. (ed. 3).

גֵּאָיוֺת‎ see גַּיְא‎.

I. גֵּוָה‎ see below גאה‎.

גוה‎ (project, be convex?).

H1468. guz

Qal Perfect גָּז‎ Psa 90:10; Imperfect וַיָּ֫גָז‎ Num 11:31; — pass away, of the life of the aged, Psa 90:10 חִישׁ גָּז‎; transitive bring over, subject wind, object quails from sea, Num 11:31 (read perhaps Hiph`il וַיָּגֶז‎ compare Köi. 442 Di).

גוזן.def:
H1470. Gozan

גּוֺזָן‎ proper name, of a location (Assyrian Guzana COT 2Kin 17:6 DlPa 184) city and district of Mesopotamia, on or near the middle course of the Euphrates, through which the river Chabur (חָבוֺר‎) flowed; thither some of the exiled Israelites were brought [by Sargon B.C. 722-21]: גּוֺזָן‎ 19:12 = Isa 37:12; גּוֺזָן נְהַר חָבוֺר‎ 2Kin 17:6; 18:11; גּוֺזָן הַר וּנְ וְהָרָא וְחָבוֺר‎ 1Chr 5:26 where Chabur is separated entirely from the river of Gozan (see חבור‎).

גוי.def:
H1471. goy

גּוֺי‎561 noun masculineGen 12:2 nation, people (Late Hebrew id. Gentiles, Phoenician גו‎ community, , Sabean גו‎ id., DHMZMG 1883, 348) — ׳ג‎ 12:2 121t.; suffix 1 singular גּוֺיִ‎ Zeph 2:9, גּוֺיֶ֑ךָ‎ Psa 106:5, גּוֺיֵךְ‎ Kt Ezek 36:13-14, 15 (Qr wrongly גּוֺיַיִךְ‎ compare Co, who strike out 36:15); plural גּוֺיִם‎ Gen 10:5 410t. + Qr 25:23; Psa 79:10 (Kt גיים‎) + 6 t. Ezekiel (variant reading emended Co); construct גּוֺיֵי‎ Gen 18:18 8t., גּוֺיֵ‎2Chr 32:13; Ezra 6:21 (compare Baer's notes); suffix גּוֺיֵהֶם‎ Gen 10:5, 20, 31, 32; —

1 nation, people Gen 10:5 (twice in verse); 10:20, 31, 32 (twice in verse) (all P) +; Isa 2:2, 4 (twice in verse) = Micah 4:2-3,(twice in verse); Job 12:23 (twice in verse); 34:29 ; Prov 14:34; הָאָרֶץ גּוֺיֵי כֹּל‎ Gen 18:18; 22:18; 26:4 (all J); Deut 28:1.

a. specifically of descendants of Abraham, גָּדוֺל גּוֺי‎ Gen 12:2; compare 18:18 (both J), גּוֺיִם‎ 17:6, גּוֺיִם הֲמוֺן‎ 17:4, 15 (all P); of Sarah גּוֺיִם‎ 17:16 (P); of Ishmael גּוֺי‎ 21:13, גָּדוֺל גָּוֺי‎ 21:18 (both E), גָּדוֺל גּוֺי‎ 17:20 (P); of Jacob גּוֺיִם וּקְהַל גּוֺי‎ 35:11 (P), גָּדוֺל גּוֺי‎ 46:3 (E); of Ephraim הַגּ ׳מְלֹא‎ 48:19 (J); of Moses גָּדוֺל גּוֺי‎ Exod 32:10 (J) compare Num 14:12 (J) Deut 9:14; of Jacob and Esau as two nations Gen 25:23 (J).

b. definitely of Israel Exod 19:6 (׳גּ קָדוֺשׁ‎) 33:13 (both J E), Deut 4:6 (הַזֶּה הַגָּדוֺל הַגּוֺי‎, said by heathen compare 4:7; 4:8) see also 4:34, 26:5 compare Psa 33:12; 83:5 (said by enemies) Jer 31:36; 33:24; Ezek 37:22; in narrative Josh 3:17; 4:1; 5:8 (JE), 5:6 (D), 10:13 (in poetry, no article); of Israel and Judah as two nations Ezek 35:10 (said by heathen) 37:22; of Judah Isa 26:2, 15 (twice in verse); compare 58:2; 60:22; Micah 4:7; once my people Zeph 2:9 (|| עַם‎); thy people Psa 106:5 (i.e. of ׳י‎), compare also Ezek 36:13-14, (read Kt); especially of Israel and (or) Judah as sinful, rebellious Deut 32:28; Judg 2:20; Isa 1:4; 10:6; Jer 5:9, 29; 7:28; 9:8; 12:17; Ezek 2:3 (strike out ᵐ5‎ Co) Hag 2:14; Mal 3:9. — Note. This definite reference to Israel and (or) Judah is comparatively rare; in Hexateuch not P (yet see Gen 17:4-5, 6, 16; 35:11 P); seldom in exile & post-exile prophets; not Chronicles —

c. usually of non-Hebrew peoples Exod 9:24; 34:10 (JE) Lev 25:44 (H) Num 14:15 (J) Deut 15:6 (twice in verse); 1Kin 5:11; 1Chr 14:17; 16:20; Isa 11:10, 12 + often; opposed to Israel as י ׳עם‎ 2Sam 7:23; 1Chr 17:21 (twice in verse) etc., see עם‎, compare also Num 23:9; note especially הַגּוֺיִם גְּלִיל‎ Isaiah 8:23 circle or district of the nations (see גָּלִיל‎); also הַגּ ׳חֲרשֶׁת‎ Judg 4:2, 13, 16 Charosheth of the nations, & לְגִלְגָּ֖ל גּוֺיִם מֶלֶךְ‎ Josh 12:23 king of nations (peoples, tribes) belonging to Gilgal (ᵐ5‎ Di to the district, i.e 'Galilee'); especially of these peoples as heathen: idolatrous Lev 8:24, 28 (P) 20:23 (H) 1Kin 14:24; 2Kin 17:8, 11, 15, 26, 29 (twice in verse); 2Chr 28:3; 32:13 +, Ezra 6:21; Ezek 5:6 +; hostile Gen 15:14 (J) Lev 26:33, 38, 45 (H) Deut 4:27; 9:4-5, 18:9; 1Chr 16:35; Jer 5:15; Ezek 4:13 +? Jeremiah Ezekiel, etc.; in simile 20:32; 25:8; sometimes || עַם‎ Psa 33:10; 33:12; Isa 11:10; Jer 6:18, see also Isa 2:2, 4 compare with Micah 4:1, 3.

2 figurative of swarm of locusts Joel 1:6; of all species of beasts Zeph 2:14.

3 גּוֺיִם‎ Gen 14:1, 9 probably mutilated proper name see below

גּוֺיִם‎ proper name, of a people Gen 14:1, 9, in phrase גּוֺיִם מֶלֶךְ תִּדְעָל‎ Tid`al king of Goim; probably a Babylonian (Elamitic, etc.) name corrupted; H. Rawlinson proposes Gutî a people northeast of Babylonia COT on 14:1; also KGF258and elsewhere; compare also DlPa 233 f.

גול‎ see גיל‎.

גְּוִיָּה‎ noun feminine body, corpse — absolute ׳ג‎ Nahum 3:3; construct גְּוִיַּת‎ Judg 14:8 2t.; suffix גְּוִיָּתוֺ‎ 1Sam 31:10; Dan 10:6, גְּוִיָּתֵנוּ‎ Gen 47:18, גְּוִיָּתָם‎ Nahum 3:3; plural absolute גְּוִיּוֺת‎ Psa 110:6; suffix גְּוִיֹּתֵנוּ‎ Neh 9:37, גְּוִיֹּתֵיהֶם‎ Ezek 1:23, גְּוִיֹּתֵיהֶ֑נָֿה‎ 1:11; —

1 living human body Gen 47:18 (singular, of many persons), compare plural Neh 9:37; of man in Daniel's vision Dan 10:6 (body apart from extremities); also of the living creatures in Ezekiel's vision Ezek 1:11, 28.

2 dead body, corpse, carcass:

a. of man 1Sam 31:10 (so originally in || 1Chr 10:10 see WeSm compare Dr) 10:12; 10:12 (singular of several persons), Psa 110:6; collective Nahum 3:3 (twice in verse);

b. of lion Judg 14:8-9,.

גּוֺלָן‎ proper name, of a location (? connected with √ גול‎ Arabic go about, around; circuit; compare Phoenician גול‎ proper name insul.; also גְּלִילָה גָּלִיל,‎) city of Manasseh in Bashan, named as a city of refuge Deut 4:43 compare Josh 20:9; 21:27 both Qr (Kt גלון‎); given to sons of Gershom son of Levi according to 1Chr 6:56; Euseb. knew it as a very large village Γαυλὼν ἢ Γωλάν LagOnom. 242, 2nd ed. 253; district of same name ib., JosephusAnt. viii. 2, 3 etc Gaulanitis, modern Jaulân RobBR ii, 432 BdPal 270 SchumacherZPV 1886 = Jaulân 1888, according to most, name applied first to city, thence to district, but perhaps otherwise if above derivatives be correct.

Qal Perfect גָּוַע‎ Num 20:29; Josh 22:20 גָּוָ֑עוּ‎ Lam 1:19 גָּוַעְנוּ‎ Numbers 17:27; Num 20:3; Imperfect יִגְוַע‎ Job 34:15, יִגְוָ֑ע‎ Gen 6:17, יִגְוְעוּ‎ Job 36:12, יִגְוָע֑וּ‎ Zech 13:8, יִגְוָע֑וּן‎ Psa 104:28 etc.; Infinitive construct גְּוַע‎ Num 20:3 גְּוֺעַ‎ Numbers 17:28; Participle גֹּוֵעַ‎ Psa 88:16; — expire and die, only P & poetry; ׳ג וימת‎ Gen 25:8, 17; 35:29 (all P); || מות‎ Job 3:11; 14:10 compare Numbers 17:28 (P); || אבד‎ Numbers 17:27 we expire, we perish (P); || עָנִי‎ Psa 88:15 (progressive parall.) distressed and about to die; || אבותיו אל יאסף‎ Gen 49:33; || ישׁוב עלעֿפר‎ Job 34:15 compare Psa 104:29; || יִכָּֽרְתוּ‎ Zech 13:8; absolute, both prose and (especially) poetry Num 20:3 (twice in verse); 20:29; Josh 22:20; Gen 6:17; 7:21 (all P) Job 10:13; 13:19; 27:5; 36:12; Lam 1:19; Job 29:18 אגוע עִםקִֿנִּי‎ with my nest shall I die, i.e. in full possession of what is mine, compare Di.

גורל.def:
H1486. goral

גּוֺרָל‎77 noun masculineLev 16:8 & ( Josh 21:10, but see below) feminine lot: (Late Hebrew id. & denominative Hiph`il הִגְרִיל‎ cast lots) — absolute ׳ג‎ 16:1 51t.; construct גּוֺרַל‎ 18:11 2t., גֹּרַל‎ Num 36:3; suffix גּוֺרָלִי‎ Psa 16:5, גֹּרָלִי‎ Judg 1:3, גּוֺרָֽלְךָ‎ Prov 1:14, גֹּרָֽלְךָ‎ Dan 12:13, גּוֺרָלֶ֑ךָ‎ Judg 1:3, גּוֺרָלֵךְ‎ Jer 13:25; Isa 57:6, גּוֺרָלוֺ‎ 1Chr 26:14, גּוֺרָלָם‎ Josh 18:11 2t.; plural גּוֺרָלוֺת‎ Jonah 1:7-8t., גֹּרָלוֺת‎ Lev 16:8; — a lot cast for the decision of questions Prov 18:18, designation of persons, etc., for service or punishment, assignment of property, etc.; probably stones put into the bosom-fold of a garment, 16:33 (אֶתהַֿגּ יוּטַל ׳בַּחֵיק‎), or into a vessel, and shaken until one springs out (יָצָא עָלָה,‎ or — late — נָפַל‎); this was regarded originally as divine decision (compare on Urim & Thummim p. 22, above); for the agent, the usual verbs are נָתַן יָרָה, הִשְׁלִיךְ,‎, and הִמִּיל‎. Particularly: —

1 lot for dividing land, especially that which Joshua cast at Shiloh י ׳לִפְנֵי‎ Josh 18:6 (יָרָה‎) 18:8; 18:10 (both הִשְׁלִיךְ‎; all three followed by לְ‎ of person for whom; all J E); compare 19:51 (P); so of lot coming up, or forth, עָלָה‎ 18:11 (construct; P), also followed by לְ‎ person 19:10 (P), & following with יָצָא‎ Joshua 16:11 (JE), Num 33:54; Josh 19:1, 17, 24, 32, 40; 21:4 (all P); be divided by lot בְּג ׳יֵחָלֵק‎ Num 26:55, or according to lot הַגּ ׳עַלמִּֿי תֵּחָלֵק‎ 26:56; apportion by lot ׳בְּג הִתְנַחֲלוּ‎ 33:54; 34:13, בְּג ׳נִחַל‎ Josh 19:51; give by lot בְּג ׳נָתַן‎ Num 36:2 בַּגּ ׳נָתַן‎ Josh 21:8 (all P) 1Chr 6:50; have by lot ל ׳הָיָה ׳בַּגּ‎ Josh 21:4, & (היה‎ omitted) 21:5; 21:6 (all P) compare 1Chr 6:46; 6:48; also Josh 21:10 (P; ׳הַגּ רִאישֹׁנָה‎, only here feminine; ᵐ5‎ — not ᵐ5‎L — omits ראישׁנה‎, & so) || 1Chr 6:39; compare further Isa 34:17 (לְ הִמִּיל‎).

2 lot for assigning to service, duty or punishment,

a. concerning the goats on day of atonement, Lev 16:8 (עַל נָתַן‎) 16:8; 16:8 (followed by לְ‎); compare 16:9; 16:10 (עַל עָלָה‎; all P).

b. assigning priests to their courses, singers, musicians & porters to their duties, by lot בְּג ׳חָלַק‎ 1Chr 24:5; ג ׳הִמִּיל‎ 24:31; 25:8; 26:13 (followed by לְ‎ of position) 26:14; of lot coming forth (לְ יָצָא‎ person) 24:7 (compare 24:7; 24:18) 25:9 (compare 25:9-31) 26:14 compare גּוֺרָלוֺ וַיֵּצֵא‎ 26:14.

c. cast lots for dwelling in Jerusalem (ג ׳הִמִּיל‎) Neh 1:11 (followed by infinitive)

d. for supplying wood for altar-fire Neh 10:35 (עַל הִמִּיל‎); here belongs probably also

e. Judg 20:9 בְּג ׳עָלֶיהָ‎, reference to 20:10 (determining who shall go up, and who supply provision) ᵐ5‎ ἀναβησόμεθα ἐπ’ αὐτὴν ἐν κλήρῳ, so Stu (insert perhaps נעלה‎), compare AV RV, BuRS 151 (who reads בְּג ׳נַמִּילָה‎); > ᵑ6‎ Be Ke who reference ׳ג‎ here to division of land of captured city.

f. to determine guilty persons Jonah 1:7 (twice in verse) (both הִמִּיל‎) 1:17 (עַל נָפַל‎); so apparently Ezek 24:6 of inhabitants of Jerusalem under figure of flesh in pot ג עָלֶיהָ ׳לֹאנָֿפַל‎ no lot is fallen over it, i.e. no discrimination is made, destruction is to include the whole city; (compare also Josh 7:14ff.; 1Sam 14:41ff. where divine agency in detection is prominent but word גּוֺרָל‎ not used).

g. in allotting slaves Joel 4:3גּ ׳יַדּוּ אֶלעַֿמִּי‎; Nahum 3:10 (עַל יַדּוּ‎); so Obadiah 11 ג יַדּוּ ׳וְעַליְֿרוּשָׁלִַם‎ — all with verb ידד‎ q. v.

h. in distributing plundered garments Psa 22:19 (על הִמִּיל‎).

i. to determine favourable day for a scheme, הִמִּיל‎ Est 3:7 (הָמָן לִפְנֵי‎) 9:24 (followed by infinitive; see also מּוּר‎).

3 thing assigned, apportioned, allotted especially of land assigned by lot, allotment Josh 15:1; 17:1; 21:38 (all P), 17:14, 17 = portion, share (|| נַחֲלָה‎ J E); compare נַחֲלָתֵנוּ גֹּרַל‎ Num 36:3 (P), נַחֲלָתָם גּוֺרַל‎ Josh 14:2 (P; but perhaps read absolute גּוֺרָל‎ compare Di); also גּוֺרָלָם גְּבוּל‎ 18:11 (P) the boundary of their allotment; גוֺרָלָם עָרֵי‎ 21:20 (P); see further Judg 1:3 (twice in verse); so probably Micah 2:5 בְּג חֶבֶל ׳הִשְׁלִיךְ‎ (Hi Che; compare also Ew); Psa 125:3, land, exposed to oppressive exaction; also figurative of ׳י‎ as portion, allotment of his people 16:5 (so Che, & on תָּמִיד‎ for תּוֺמִיךְ‎ compare his critical note; see also Ew; otherwise De and others; — || חֶלְקִי מְנָת‎); on the other hand, of idols Isa 57:6 (|| חֵלֶק‎); also לְג ׳עָמַד‎ Dan 12:13, of allotted portion, share, in the Messianic consummation; more Generally, one's portion, lot, fortune בְּתוֺכֵנוּ תַּמִּיל גּוֺרָֽלְךָ‎ Prov 1:14 cast thy fortune into the midst of us, in with us (|| לְכֻלָּנוּ יִהְיֶה אֶחָד כִּיס‎).

4 portion = recompence, retribution Isa 17:14 (|| חֵלֶק‎), Jer 13:25 (|| מִדַּיִךְ מְנָת‎), both implying divine agency.

גחה.def:
H4480. min

or minni or minne מִןֿ‎ and מִּ ‎, before יְ‎ (except Dan 12:2; 2Chr 20:11) contracted to מִי‎ (as מִידֵי‎ from מִיְּדֵי‎), before guttural and ר‎, mostly מֵ‎, occasionally מִ‎ (Ges§ 102, l R.; more fully Köii. 291ff), מִן‎ before article in all books much commoner than -מֵ‎; מִן‎; before other words most frequently in Chronicles [51 t.: elsewhere 47 t. (Kö292)]; in poetry also מִנִּי‎, with the old י‎ of the Genitive (Ges§ 90.3a) Judg 5:14 (twice in verse); Isa 46:3 (twice in verse); Psa 44:11; 44:19; 68:32; 74:22; 78:2; 78:42; 88:10 19t. Job, and in לְמִנִּי‎ Micah 7:12 (twice in verse) and מִנֵּיֿ‎ (on analogue of עֲלֵי עֲדֵי,‎) Isa 30:11 (twice in verse), preposition expressing the idea of separation, hence out of, from, on account of, off, on the side of, since, above, than, so that not (Phoenician מ‎; Aramaic ; Arabic >; Ethiopic ; Sabean בן‎ (DHMZMG xxix.606 ff.; xxxvii.375)); with suff, מִמֶּנִּי‎ (the מִן‎ reduplicated, Ol§ 223c, and others, Köii. 289 f.), in poetry מִנִּי‎ 22:4; 30:1; 38:12; Job 16:6, מֶ֫נִּי‎ Psa 18:23; 65:4; 139:19; Job 21:16; 22:18; 30:10; מִמֵּךְ מִמֶּ֑ךָּ, מִמְּךָ,‎; מִמֶּ֫נּוּ‎ ( 4:12 מֶ֫נְהוּ‎), מִמֶּ֫נָּה‎; 1 plural מִמֶּ֫נּוּ‎ (according to Orientals מִמֵּ֫נֿוּ‎: see BaerJob. p. 57 Kö290); מִכֶּם‎; מֵהֶם‎ (מִנְּהֶם‎ 11:20), מֵהֵ֫מָּה‎ Jer 10:2; Eccl 12:12; מֵהֵ֫נָּה‎7t. (see הֵ֫מָּה‎ 8c), מֵהֶן‎ (editions מֵהֵן‎) Ezek 16:47, 52 (see ZerweckHeb, Präp. Min, 1894): — 1. with verbs expressing (or implying) separation or removal, whether from a person or place, or in any direction, also from guilt, calamity, etc.: — thus

a. to descend from a mountain Exod 19:14, to fall from a roof Deut 22:8, from heaven Isa 14:12, to go up from a valley Josh 10:7, to raise up from the dunghill 1Sam 2:8, or the ground 2Sam 12:17. So constantly with verbs of going, as ברח שׁב, הלך, בא,‎ (followed by a person, usually מפני‎), of calling, as Isa 24:14 מִיָּם צָֽהֲלוּ‎, 42:10-11, Psa 148:1 of asking or exacting as נָקַם דרשׁ, בקשׁ, שׁאל,‎,הִנָּקֵם‎, of delivering, as הציל הושׁיע,‎, etc., of hiding as העלים נעלם,‎, etc., of taking or withholding, as מנע חשׂך, לקח,‎, of keeping (from), as שׁמר נצר,‎, of being far, or desisting, as רחק‎ Exod 23:7, מִמֶּנּוּ חֲדַל‎ desist from us,14:2, so הֶרֶף‎ Deut 9:14,הֵנִיחַ‎ 12:10, השׁקיט‎ > Psa 94:13, שׁבת‎ Gen 2:2, compare 5:29; note especially the pregnant constructions, שׁפט‎ to judge (and save) from Psa 43:1, followed by מִיַּד‎ 1Sam 24:16 +, ענה‎ to answer (and save) from Psa 22:22, חרשׁ‎ and חשׁה‎ to be silent (turning) from 28:1 (twice in verse), ממני החרישׁו‎ Job 13:13; Jer 38:27; Psa 18:22 מאלהי רשׁעתי ולא‎ not did wickedly (turning) from my God, 30:4 Kt., 73:27, ממך כלזֿוֺנֶה‎, Jer 3:20 מִן בָּגַד‎ (ᵐ5‎ εἰς = ב‎), 31:13 with שִׂמַּח‎ (2Chr 20:27), Ezek 27:34; Prov 25:17; רֵעֶ֫ךָ מִבֵּית רַגְלְךָ הֹקַר‎, Isa 29:4; 63:17; Joel 1:12; Jer 51:5 מֵאֱלֹהָיו אַלְמָן‎ widowed (and severed) from etc., Ezek 44:22; also Judg 7:17 תַּעֲשׂוּ וְכֵן תִרְאוּ מִמֶּנִּי‎ ye shall see from me, i.e. learn what to do by observing me. Some of the verbs mentioned above are construed more precisely with מֵעַל מֵעִם, מֵאֵת,‎, q. v.: and others, especially מִּלֵּט מּדה, הצּיל, הושׁיע, דרשׁ, לקח,‎, idiomatic with מִיַּד‎. Here also belong 40:15 מִדְּלִי מַר‎ a drop from (hanging from) a bucket; Song 4:1 goats גלעד מהר שֶׁגָָּֽלְשׁוּ‎ that sit up (seeming to hang) from the hills of Gilead (compare Od. 21. 420 ἐκ διφροιο καθήμενος: also the Arabic idiom , literally to be near from a thing): probably also the difficult passage Dan 8:9, and from one of them there came forth אַחַת קֶרֶן מִצְּעִירָה‎ a horn from (being) a little one, i.e. gradually increasing from small beginnings (but ? read צְעִירָה אַחֶרֶת‎ Bev compare 7:8).

With a following לְ‎ (or suffix), most of these words are frequently in the sense of on the east (west, etc.) of . . ., as Josh 8:13 מִיָּם לָעִיר‎ on the west of the city, לְ מִקֶּדֶם‎ Gen 3:24, לְ מִצְּפוֺן‎ (construct Ges§ 130 a, n.) (c) with verbs of fearing, to express the source of the emotion, as ירא‎ Psa 3:7 + often (also with מִמְּנֵי‎), מָּחַד‎ 27:1, נִבְהַל‎ Ezek 26:18, גּוּר‎ Deut 18:22; Job 41:17; Est 5:9 ממנו זָע ולא ולאקֿם‎; with בּוֺשׁ‎ to be disconcerted or disappointed, to express the source of the disappointment, Isa 1:29 + often; with שָׂמֵחַ‎ Prov 5:18; Eccl 2:10. feminine of the remoter cause, the ultimate ground on account of which something happens or is done. (N.B. The line between

e and

f. is not always clearly defined): Exod 2:23 they sighed מןהֿעבדה‎ on account of the bondage, 6:9; 15:23; Deut 7:7 not מֵרֻבְּכֶם‎ through, by reason of, your numbers did J. set his love upon you, Josh 22:24 to do a thing מִדְּאָנָה‎ out of carefulness, 2Sam 23:4 מִנֹּגַהּ‎, 1Kin 14:4; Isa 53:5 wounded מִמְּשָׁעֵינוּ‎ on account of our transgressions, bruised מֵעֲוֺנוֺתֵינוּ‎, 53:8; Job 4:19; Obadiah 10; Hab 2:17; Psa 6:8 מִכַּעַס עיני עשׁשׁה‎ from vexation (compare Job 17:7: Psa 31:10 ׳ב‎), 31:12; 38:19 I am concerned on account of my sin, Prov 20:4 יחרשׁ לא עצל מֵחֹרֶף‎ by reason of the winter, Job 22:4 יֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ הֲמִיִּרְאָ֑תְךָ‎ on account of thy fear of him? Song 3:8; Ruth 1:13 מִכֶּם מְאֹד כִּימַֿרלִֿי‎ because of you: see also Deut 28:34, 67; 32:19; Judg 2:18; Isa 65:14; Jer 12:4; 24:2 מֵרֹעַ‎, 50:13; 51:5 b (Ew Ke), Ezek 7:27 (but read probably with ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Co כְּדרכם‎), 16:61; 35:11 (AV out of), 45:20; Micah 2:12; 7:13; Psa 5:11; 12:6; 107:17; 119:53; Gen 49:12 red of eyes מִיָּ֑יִן‎, and white of teeth מֵחָלָב‎. Often also in מֵרֹב‎ from the abundance of, absolute for abundance, with many different verbs, as 16:10 מֵרֹב יִסָּפֵר לֹא‎ Josh 9:13; 1Sam 1:16, etc. Similarly in מִבִּלְתִּי מִבְּלִי, מֵאֵין,‎ (pp. 35, 115, 117); and before an infinitive (7a), and in מֵאֲשֶׁר‎ (p. 84).

g. the cause being conceived as regulative, מן‎ occasionally approaches in sense to according to (compare Latin ex more, ex lege), Jonah 3:7 proclaimed in Nineveh וגדליו המלך מטעם‎ at, by, in accordance with, the decree of the king (compare Aramaic Ezra 6:14; Dan 2:8): so Job 39:26 (2e (b)) according to Ges Hi.

3 Partitively (a sense connecting with

2a (c), above): —

a. Gen 6:19 מִכֹּל שְׁנַיִם‎ two out of, from, all, 7:8; 39:11 ֗֗֗ מן אישׁ‎ a man (or one) of . . . (so Num 25:6; 1 Samuel 24:28 +, ֗֗֗ מן אנשׁים‎ 16:2; Josh 2:2 +, 2Kin 2:7, etc.); Gen 42:16 send אֶחָד מִכֶּם‎ Lev 1:2a 17:12 מִכֶּם כלנֿפשׁ‎, 19:34; 26:8, Judg 8:14 סֻכּוֺת מֵאַנְשֵׁי נַעַר‎, 1Sam 22:8, etc.; Judg 14:19; 2Kin 2:24; Isa 66:19; ֗֗֗ מִן אֶחָד‎ 1Sam 16:18 +, ֗֗֗ מִן אַחַד‎ (Ges§ 130, 1) Deut 25:5 +; מֵהֵ֫נָּה אַחַת‎ Psa 34:21; Isa 34:16; ֗֗֗ מִן מִי‎ Job 5:1; Isa 50:1, ֗֗֗ מִן אֵין‎ 1Sam 14:39; Isa 51:18; 21:11 מלילה מהֿ‎ how much of the night? 2Chr 31:3 מִןרְֿכוּשׁוֺ הַמֶּלָח וּמְנָת‎.

b. the number being omitted, מִן‎ is used indefinitely: — (a) = some of, — as subject Exod 16:27 מןהֿעם יצאו‎ there went out (some) of the people, Lev 25:49; 2Sam 11:17, 24, especially in late Hebrew Ezra 2:68, 70; 7:7; Neh 11:4, 25; 1Chr 4:42; 9:30, 32; 2Chr 17:11; 32:21; Dan 11:35; more frequently as object, especially with לקח‎, Gen 4:3 האדמה מִמְּרִי וַיָּבֵא‎ brought of the fruit of the ground, 30:14 give me בְנֵךְ מִדּוּדָאֵי‎ (some) of thy son's love-apples, 33:15; Exod 12:7; 17:5; Lev 18:30; 20:2; Num 11:17; 13:23; 1Kin 12:4; Isa 39:7; 47:13; Amos 2:11; Dan 8:10 +, Song 1:2 מִּיו מִנְּשִׁיקוֺת ישׁקני‎ let him kiss me (with) some of the kisses etc., Psa 72:15; 137:3 צִיּוֺן מִשִּׁיר‎ (some) of the songs of Zion, Job 11:6 (Ges RVm) + often; in late Hebrew note also ֗֗֗ מִן יֵשׁ‎ there are some of . . . Neh 5:5; ֗֗֗ מֵהֶם ֗֗֗ מֵהֶם‎ some. . . others. . . 1Chr 9:28f. (as in Aramaic Dan 2:33, and PS2155); ֗֗֗ מִקְצָת‎ some of. . . (as in Late Hebrew) 1:2; Neh 7:69. (b) to designate an individual (rare), Gen 28:11 and he took הַמָּקוֺם מֵאַבְנֵי‎ (one) of the stones of the place (see 28:18), Exod 6:25 פוטיאל מבּנות‎ (one) of the daughters of P., Ezek 17:5, 13; Neh 13:28; Psa 132:11; as subject Lev 25:33; Dan 11:5 the king of the south וּמִןֿ שָׂרָיו‎ and (one) of his captains, 11:7, compare Jer 41:1; Est 4:5; 2Chr 26:11; Ruth 2:20 הוא מִגֹּאֲלֵנוּ‎ he is (one) of our kinsmen, Exod 2:6. (c) in a negative or hypothetical sentence (whether subject or object) = any, aught, Deut 16:4 מןהֿבשׂר ילין ולא‎ and there shall not remain any of the flesh, 1Kin 18:5 מןהֿבהמה נכרית ולא‎ and we shall not destroy any of the beasts, 2Kin 10:10 (compare Josh 21:43; 23:14; 1Sam 3:19; 1Kin 8:56; Est 6:10), Esther 6:23 י מֵעַבְדֵי ׳מֶּןיֶֿשׁמֹּֿה‎ Job 27:6 מִיָּמָ֑י לְבָבִי יֶחֱרַף לֹא‎ my heart reproacheth not one of my days: with אִם‎, etc. Exod 29:34; Lev 4:2a (compare 4:22; 4:27), 11:32 (מהם‎), 11:33; 11:35; 11:37-39; 18:29; 25:25; Num 5:6; מִכֹּל‎ anything whatever, Leviticus 5:24; Lev 11:34; compare 1Sam 23:23 (?). (d) peculiarly, with a noun of unity, especially אֶחָד‎, to express forcibly the idea of a single one: Deut 15:7 if there be a poor man in thy midst, אַחֶיךָ מֵאַחַר‎ any one of thy brethren, Lev 4:2b if he doeth מֵהֵ֫נָּה מֵאַחַת‎ any one of these things, 5:13; Ezek 18:10 אָח וְעָשָׂה מֵאֵלֶּה מֵאַחַד‎ (where אח‎ is a vox nihili) and doeth aught of these things; 1Sam 14:45 if there shall fall אַרְצָה ראֹשׁוֺ מִשַּׂעֲרַת‎ a single hair of his head to the ground! (for שְׂעָרָה‎ as a noun of individual meaning see Ges§ 122t Dr), compare 2Sam 14:11; 1Kin 1:52. (Probably a rhetorical application of the partitive sense, though the explanation 'starting from one' = 'even one' would also be possible. is used similarly after negative and interrogative particles, not merely with collective nouns, as nought have they of knowledge (Qor 18:4), but also with nouns of unity, as Qor 3:55 Ye have not aught of (= any) god, except Him; 19:19 dost thou perceive even one of them? 6:59 there falleth not even a single leaf (noun of individual meaning) without His knowing it. See further Thes, and WAG. ii. § 48 f. b), (e) (rare) specifying the objects, or elements, of which a Genus consists (the Arabic , min of explication, WAG. ii. § 48 g): Gen 6:2 מכל בחרו אשׁר‎ consisting of all whom they chose, 7:22; 9:10; Lev 11:32 (מכל‎), 1Chr 5:18; Jer 40:7 (מאשׁר‎); 44:28 and they shall know וּמֵהֶם מִמֶּנִּי יָקוּם דְּבַרמִֿי‎ whose word shall stand, consisting of me and of them (defining the Genus embraced by ׃מי‎ compare both (of them), Abel as well as Cain, and Qor 3:193: Wl.c.). — On מֵאַיִן‎ 10:6-7, see אַיִן‎ near the end.

4 of time — namely

a. as marking the terminus a quo, the anterior limit of a continuous period, from, since Deut 9:24 אֶתְכֶם דַּעְתִּי מִיּוֺם‎ from the day of my (first) knowing you (so 1Sam 7:2; 8:8 + ); 18:9 וָהָֽלְאָה ההוא מהיום‎ from that day and onwards, simil. Lev 22:27; Num 15:23; Ezek 39:22; Isa 18:2, 7 (where מִןהֿוּא‎ = הוּא מֵאֲשֶׁר‎; compare Nahum 2:9 הִיא מִימֵי‎ = הִיא אֲשֶׁר מִימֵי‎); וָמָֽעְלָה ההוא מהיום‎ 1Sam 16:13; 30:25 (Hag 2:15, 18 apparently of time backwards); מֵאָז‎ from the time of . . . .; מִןהַֿבֶּטֶן‎ from the womb Judg 13:5, 7, אִמִּי מִבֶּטֶן‎ 16:17 +; ֗֗֗ מִימֵי‎ Hosea 10:9; Isa 23:7; Jer 36:2 +; מִיָּמֶיךָ‎ idiomatic = since thou wast born 1Sam 25:28; 1Kin 1:6 (מִיָּמָיו‎), Job 38:12; מִקֶּדֶם‎ from antiquity Hab 1:12; Psa 74:12; Isa 42:14 מֵעוֺלָם הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי‎ I have been silent since old time; מֵעַתָּה‎ from now, hence-forth Jer 3:4 +, מִיּוֺם‎ from to-day 43:13; Ezek 48:35, הזה מןהֿיום‎ Hag 2:19. See also 5c, 7 c. compare Exod 33:6 חוֺרֵב מֵהַר‎ from Horeb, Hosea 13:4 I am ׳י‎ thy God מִצְרַיִם מֵאֶרֶץ‎.

b. as marking the period immediately succeeding the limit, after: Gen 38:24 חֳדָשִׁים כְּמִשְׁלשׁ‎ after about three months it was told Judah, רַבִּים מִיָּמִים‎ Josh 23:1; Ezek 38:8, מִיָּמִים‎ after (some) days, Judg 11:4; 14:8; 15:1, מִיֹּמַיִם‎ after two days Hosea 6:2; יָמִים מֵרֹב‎ Isa 24:22: more frequently with קֵץ‎ or קָצֶה‎, Gen 4:3 יָמִים מִקֵּץ‎, 8:3; Josh 3:2 + often; Deut 14:28 שָׁנִים שָׁלשׁ מִקְצֵה‎, 15:1 שֶׁבַע מִקְצֵה שָׁנִים‎ (by which is meant not the actual end of the three or seven years, but the period when the third or seventh year has arrived); מִמָּחֳרָת‎ after the morrow (had arrived) = on the morrow, Gen 19:34 + often; מֵהַבֹּקֶר‎ 2Sam 2:27. — 23:4 מִמָּטָר‎; Isa 53:11 נַפְשׁוֺ מֵעֲמַל‎; perhaps 29:18 (Kö581). compare 2Sam 20:5 and he delayed מןהֿמועד‎ beyond the appointed time.

c. in such phrases, however, מִן‎ sometimes (compare 1c) loses its significance: thus מֵאָז‎ 2Sam 15:34; Isa 16:13 not from former time, but in former time, formerly, Gen 6:4 מֵעוֺלָם אֲשֶׁר הַגִּבּוֺרִים‎ which were of old, Josh 24:2 dwelt of old, Psa 77:6 days מִקֶּדֶם‎ aforetime, מֵאַחֲרֵי‎ Deut 29:21 (p. 30). — מִקָּרוֺב‎ literally from near, i.e. recently 32:17, of short duration Job 20:5, shortly Ezek 7:8; at hand (in a local sense, 1c) Jer 23:23.

5 (וְעַד‎) עַד ֗֗֗ מִן‎ from . . . even, to : very oft .: —

a. in geography or local sense, Gen 10:19; 15:18 הגדול הנהר עד מצרים מנהר‎, 25:18; Exod 23:31; Deut 2:36; 1Sam 3:20; 2Sam 5:25; Jer 31:38; Psa 72:8 + often; so with מִלְּבוֺא‎ 1Kin 8:65 (2Chr 7:8), 2Kin 14:25; Amos 6:14; Deut 13:8 הָאָרֶץ קְצֵה וְעַד הָאָרֶץ מִקְצֵה‎, 28:64; Jer 12:12; Gen 47:21 וְעַדקָֿצֵהוּ גְּבוּלמִֿצְרַיִם מִקְצֵה‎, 1Kin 6:24; 7:23 וְעַד מִשְּׂפָתוֺ שְׂפָתוֺ‎; Lev 13:12 רגליו ועד מראשׁו‎, Deut 28:35 רגלך מכף קדקדך ועד‎ (similarly 2Sam 14:25; Job 2:7; Isa 1:6). compare 1Sam 9:2 וָמַ֫עְלָה מִשִּׁכְמוֺ‎, 2Sam 5:9; Josh 15:46.

b. metaphor not of actual space, but of classes of objects, to express idiomatically the idea ofcomprehension, so that the two prepositions may be often represented by both . . . and: Gen 19:4 וְעַדזָֿקֵן מִנַּעַר‎ from young to old (i.e. both included) = both young and old, 19:11; 1Sam 5:9 + וְעַדגָּֿדוֺל מִקָּטֹן‎ = both great and small, Jer 6:13 וְעַדגְּֿדוֺלָם מִקְּטַנָּם‎ from the least of them even to the greatest of them, ib. מִנָּבִיא וְעַדכֹּֿהֵן‎ from the prophet even to the priest every one dealeth falsely, Exod 9:25 + בהמה ועד מאדם‎ both man and beast, 11:5 וגו השׁפחה ׳בכור פרעהע֗֗֗ד מבכור‎, 13:15; Num 6:4; Deut 29:10 עציך מחֹטב מימיך שֹׁאב עד‎, Josh 8:25 + אשׁה ועד מאישׁ‎, 1Sam 15:3 (4 pairs), 22:19; 1Kin 5:13; 2Kin 17:9 = 18:8, Isa 10:18 בשׂר ועד מנפשׁ‎ = both soul and body, Jer 9:9; after a word implying a negative = either . . . or Gen 14:23; 31:24, 29 רע עד מטוב‎ either good or evil. The עַד‎ may be repeated, if required: 6:7 מאדם השׁמים ועדעֿוף רמשׂ עד עדבֿהמה‎ (so 7:23), Exod 22:3; Josh 6:21; Judg 15:5 זָ֑יִת וְעַדכֶּֿרֶם וְעַדקָֿמָה מִגָּדִישׁ‎, 20:48; 1Sam 30:19: without מן‎, Lev 11:42; Num 8:4. Similar is the use of מן‎ in the idiom (וָמָֽטָּה‎) וָמָֽעְלָה מִבֶּןשָׁ֗֗֗נָה‎ (also שָׁנָה ֗֗֗ וְעַדבֶּֿן‎); and compare 2Kin 3:21

c. of time, Gen 46:34 עַתָּה וְעַד מִנְּעֻרֵינוּ‎ from our youth even until now, 1Sam 12:2; Jer 3:25; Num 14:19; Exod 10:6; 18:13 עדהֿערב מןהֿבֹקר‎, 1Sam 30:17; 1Kin 18:26; Isa 9:6; Psa 90:2; + often: with two inff. Hosea 7:4: and implying intervals (not duration) Ezek 4:10-11, (compare with לְ‎ Est 3:7 (twice in verse)).

d. there occur further (1) אֶלֿ ֗֗֗ מִן‎, Josh 15:21; Exod 26:28 = 36:33 אֶלהַֿקָּצֶה מִןהַֿקָּצֶה‎ from end to end, Ezek 40:23, 27; Ezra 9:11 מִמֶּהאֶֿלמֶּֿה‎; Psa 144:13 זַן אֶל מִזַּן‎ from kind to kind = kinds of every sort; with a verb of motion, Jer 48:11; Psa 105:13; 1Chr 17:5, and expressing a climax, Psa 84:8 אֶלחַֿיִל מֵחַיִל יֵָֽלְכוּ‎, Jer 9:2 (compare Rom 1:17): of time, מיוםאֿליֿום‎ Num 30:15, compare 1Chr 16:23 (|| Psa 96:2 לְ‎); implying intervals, אֶלעֵֿת מֵעֵת‎ 1Chr 9:25. (2) לְ ֗֗֗ מִן‎ Exod 32:27; Ezek 40:13; Zech 14:10: of time Psa 96:2; Job 4:20: with intervals, 2Sam 14:26. (3) הָ֯ ֗֗֗ מִן‎ Num 34:10; Ezek 6:14; רִבְלָ֫תָה מִמִּדְבָּר‎ (so Ges Ew Hi etc.) from the wilderness to Riblah, 21:3; 25:13 וּדְדָ֫נֶה מִתֵּימָן‎ (Co Kö Berthol); without ָ֯‎ 1Kin 5:1. And of time in the phrase (implying intervals) יָמִ֫ימָה מִיָּמִים‎ Exod 13:10 4t.

6 In comparisons, beyond, above, hence in English than: so constantly: namely

a. when an object is compared with another distinct from itself, Judg 14:18 מִדְּבַשׁ מַהמָּֿתוֺק‎ what is sweet away from, beyond in excess of, honey ? i.e. in our idiom, what is sweeter than honey ? Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל הַכֹּהֵן‎ the priest that is great above his brethren, Num 14:12; Ezek 28:3 מִדָּנִאֵל חָכָם‎ wiser than Daniel, Psa 119:72 + very often; Hosea 2:9 מֵעָ֑תָּה אָז לִי טוֺב כִּי‎; with an infinitive (sometimes with לְ‎) as subject, Gen 29:10 וגו אֹתָהּ מִתִּתִּי לְךָ אֹתָהּ תִּתִּי ׳טוֺב‎ better is my giving her to thee than my giving her to another, Exod 14:12; 1Sam 15:22; Prov 21:9, 19; 25:7; Psa 118:8; 118:9 +; with verbs, Gen 19:9 מֵהֶם לְךָ נָרַע עתה‎ now we will harm thee beyond them, more than them, 25:23 יֶאֱמַץ מִלְאֹם לְאֹם‎, 26:16; 29:30 גםֿ ויאהב מִלֵּאָה אתרֿחל‎, 38:26 מִמֶּנִּי צָֽדְקָה‎, 48:19 מִמֶּנּוּ יִגְדַּל‎, Judg 2:19 מאבותם השׁחיתו‎ they have done corruptly more than their fathers, 1Sam 2:29; 2Sam 20:6; 1Kin 1:37; 14:9; Jer 5:3; Ezek 5:6 + often; = in, preference to, above, Psa 45:8; 52:5 (twice in verse); Hosea 6:6; Hab 2:16, after בחר‎ Jer 8:3; Job 7:15; 36:21; Psa 84:11 (מִדּוּר‎) +: note also מִן נֹפֵל‎ Job 12:3; 13:2 +?to (Ew Ges and others Hi; al. De); מִן שֹׁנֶה‎ different from Est 1:7; 3:8.

b. when an object is compared with a group or multitude of which it forms one, especially with מִכֹּל‎, Gen 3:1 עָרוּם הַשָּׂדֶה חַיַּת מִכֹּל‎ subtil out of all beasts of the field, or beyond, above all (other) beasts, 3:14 cursed above all cattle (but without implying any judgment whether other cattle are cursed likewise), 37:3 Israel loved Joseph מִכָּלבָּֿנָיו‎ out of all his sons, or above all his (other) sons, Deut 7:7; 33:24 אָשֵׁר מִבָּנִים בָּרוּךְ‎ blessed above sons be Asher, Judg 5:24 מִנָּשִׁים תְּבֹרַח‎ blessed above women be Jael, 1Sam 9:2b 15:33 אִמֶּ֑ךָ מִנָּשִׁים תִּשְׁכַּל כֵּן‎, 18:30; Jer 17:9 מִכֹּל עָקֹב‎ deceitful above all things, Psa 45:3; Song 5:10 מֵרְבָבָה דָּגוּל‎ (compare מִן בָּחַר‎ above

2a c: ex in eximius, egregius; Iliad 18:431 ὅς σ’, ἐμοὶ ἐκ πάσεων Κρονίδης Ζεὺς ἄλγἐ ἔδωκεν, 3:227 ἔξοχος Ἀργείων . . . κεφαλήν).

c. sometimes in poetry the idea on which מן‎ is logically dependent, is unexpressed, and must be understood by the reader, Isa 10:10 מירושׁלם ופסיליהם‎ and their idols are (more) than (those of) Jerusalem, Micah 7:4 מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר‎ the uprightest is (sharper) than a thorn-hedge (but We from), Job 11:7; 28:18; Psa 4:8 מֵעֵת‎ beyond (that of) the time when etc. Ecclesiastes 4:17; Eccl 9:17; compare Ezek 15:2.

d. מן‎ not unfrequently expresses the idea of a thing being too much for a person, or surpassing his powers: Gen 18:14 ׳מי הֲיִמָּלֵא דָּבָר‎ can a thing be too hard for J.? (so Deut 17:8 +; compare Psa 131:1; 139:6 + ), 32:11 מִן קָטֹנְתִּי‎, Deut 14:24 הַדֶּרֶךְ מִמְּךָ יִרְבֶּה כִּי‎ = is too great for thee (1Kin 19:7), 1Ki 32:47 מִכֶּם רֵק‎: so with עָצַם‎ Gen 26:16, כָּבֵד‎ be too heavy for Exod 18:18; Psa 38:5, מָךְ‎ Lev 27:8 (too poor to pay), קָשָׁה‎ Deut 1:7, צַר‎ be too narrow for, 2Kin 6:1; Isa 49:19, קצר‎ 50:2, אָמַץ‎ Psa 18:18, נמני ירום‎ is too high for me 61:3, גָּבַר‎ 65:4; מִמְּךָ ַהמְעַט‎ Job 15:11 too little for thee ? מִכֶּם ַהמְעַט‎ Num 16:9; Isa 7:13; Ezek 34:18 (see מְעַט‎; also on 16:20); often with an infinitive, as Gen 4:13 מִנְּשׂוֺא עֲוֺנִי גָּדוֺל‎ is greater than I can bear, 30:7 their substance was יַחְדָּו מִשֶּׁבֶת רַב‎ literally great beyond dwelling together = too great for (their) dwelling together, Exod 12:4; Judg 7:2 רַב מִתִּתִּי‎ = too great for me to give, 1Sam 25:17b 1Kin 8:64 מֵהָכִיל רַב‎, Isa 28:20; 33:19; 59:1; Hab 1:13; Psa 40:6; Ruth 1:12: note especially מִן רַב‎ it is more than that . . . (= there is enough of), Exod 9:28; 1Kin 12:28, followed by substantive Ezek 44:6 (see רַב‎); and Isa 49:6 וגו לְהָקִים ׳עֶבֶד לִי מִהְיוֺתְךָ נָקֵל‎ too light for thy being my servant was it to raise up, etc., Ezek 8:17 וגו ׳מֵעֲשׂוֺת יִשְׂר לְבֵית ׳הֲנָקֵל‎ was it too trifling to the house of Israel for the doing etc. (less than the doing etc. deserved) ? (but ? read עֲשׂוֺת‎ on analogue of 1Kin 16:31).

7 מן‎ is prefixed to an infin.:

a. with a causal force (rare), from, on account of, through (compare 2f): Deut 7:7-8, י ׳מֵאַהֲבַת אֶתְכֶם‎ through J.'s loving you = because J. loved you, 9:28 (compare 1:27 בְּ‎) 2Sam 3:11 אֹתוֺ מִיִּרְאָתוֺ‎ = because he feared him, Isa 48:4 ֗֗֗ מִדַּעְתִּי‎ = because I knew. . . So in מִבִּלְתִּי , ֗֗֗ מִבְּלִי‎.

b. after verbs implying restraint, prevention, cessation, etc., as עֲצָרַנִי מִלֶּדֶת‎ Gen 16:2 hath restrained me from bearing, מִלֶּדֶת וַתַּעֲמֹד‎ 29:35; 30:9: so with חשׂך‎ 20:6 +, חדל‎ + Exod 23:5 +, כִּלָּה‎ + 34:33 +, נִכְלָא‎ 36:6, מָנַע‎ 1Sam 25:26 +, שׁבת‎ Jer 31:36 +, מֵהַבִּיט יָרֵא‎ Exod 3:6 +, מִןהַֿחֵרֶם שִׁמְרוּ‎ Josh 6:18; 2Chr 25:13 מִלֶּכֶת הֵשִׁיב‎. Especially (a) after similar verbs, expressing concisely a negative consequence, literally away from . . ., i.e. so as not to, so that not: Gen 23:6; b 27:1 Jacob's eyes were dim, ֵמרְאֹת‎ away from seeing = so that he could not see, 31:29 מִן נִשְׁמַר‎ (|| 31:24 מֶּן‎), Exod 14:5; Lev 26:13; Num 32:7; Deut 28:55 (his eye shall be envious etc.) מִתֵּת‎ from giving = so that he will not give, Judg 6:27; 1 Samuel 21:31; 1Sam 7:8 do not be silent from us מִזְּעֹק‎ so as not to call (compare 1Kin 22:3), 1Sam 8:7 me have they rejected עליהם מִמְּלֹךְ‎, 16:1 (Hosea 4:6), 2Sam 14:11 (read מֵהַרְבּוֺת‎), Isa 5:6; 8:11; 21:3; 23:1 is destroyed מִבּוֺא‎ so that none can enter in, 24:10; 33:15; 44:18; 49:15; 54:9; 56:6; 58:13; Jer 10:14 מִדַּעַת ֗֗֗ נִבְעַר‎ is stupefied so that he has no knowledge, 13:14; 33:21, 24, 26; Ezek 20:17; Micah 3:6; Zech 7:11; 7:12; Psa 30:4 Qr, 39:2; 69:24; 102:5 (after שָׁכַח‎, peculiarly), 106:23; Lam 3:44; 4:18; Job 34:30a 2Chr 36:13. So in מֵעֲשׂוֺת חָלִילָהלִֿי‎ that I should not do Gen 44:17 +. (b) still more concisely, especially in poetry, with a noun alone: 1Sam 15:23 has rejected thee מִמֶּלֶךְ‎ from (being) king (15:26 מִהְיוֺת מֶלֶךְ‎), Lev 26:43 מֵהֶם‎, Isa 7:8 מֵעָם יֵחַת‎ shall be shattered from (being) a people, that it be no more a people, 17:1 מֵעִיר מוּסָר‎, 25:2b; 52:14 מִשְׁחַת כֵּן מַרְאֵהוּ מֵאִישׁ‎ marred away from (being) a man('s), Jer 2:25 מִיָּחֵף‎, 17:16 מֵרֹעֶה‎, 48:2 מִגּוֺי וְנַכְרִיתֶנָּה‎, 48:42 מֵעָם‎, Psa 8:6 hast made him lack but little מאלהים‎ ut non esset Deus, 83:5 מִגּוֺי‎, Prov 30:2 בַּעַר מֵאִישׁ אָנֹכִי‎ too boorish to be a man: compare Dan 4:13; 1Kin 15:13 מִגְּבִירָה וַיְסִרֶהָ‎ removed her from (being) queen-mother, Ezek 16:41 מִזּוֺנָה וִהִשְׁבַּתִּיךְ‎; and even to express absolutely the non-existence of a thing not named in the principal clause, as Isa 23:1 כִּי מִבַּיִת שֻׁדַּד‎ so that there is no house, Ezek 12:19 (32:15), 25:9 מֵהֶעָרִים‎, Hosea 9:11 (3 t. in verse); 9:12; Micah 3:6; Hag 1:10 מִטָּ֑ל‎, Zech 7:14; 9:8; Psa 39:3; 49:15 מִזְּבֻללֿוֺ‎ so that it has no dwelling, 52:7 מֵאֹהֶל יִסָּֽחֲךָ‎ pluck thee up tentless, 109:24 is lean מִשָּׁ֑מֶן‎ so that there is no fatness, Job 28:11; 33:21; 34:30b. Oft. strengthened by pleonastic אֵין‎ or בְּלִי‎, as יוֺשֵׁב מֵאֵין‎ Isa 5:9, יוֺשֵׁב מִבְּלִי‎ see pp. 35:a, 115:b. compare Köiii. 592 ff.

c. with a temporal force, since, after (compare

4), chiefly late: Num 24:23 אֵל מִשֻּׂמוֺ‎ after God's establishing him, Isa 44:7 עֿוֺלָם עַם מִשֻּׂמִי‎ since I appointed the ancient people, Hosea 7:4; Hag 2:16 (?) Ruth 2:18; Neh 5:14; 1Chr 8:8 אוֺתָם מִןשִֿׁלְחוֺ‎ (compare 6:16) 2Chr 31:10; Dan 11:23; 12:1 (compare 9:25), Psa 73:20 מֵהָקִיץ כַּחֲלוֺם‎ after (one's) awaking, Job 20:4.

8 Once Deut 33:11 as a

conjunction before a finite verb. Smite . . . his haters מִןיְֿקוּמוּן‎ that they rise not again, in poetry for מִקּוּם‎ (7b): compare Dr§ 41. — On מֵאֲשֵׁר‎

adverb and

conjunction.

9 In compounds: —

a. מִלְּ מִבַּ֫עַד, מִבַּלְעֲדֵי, מִבֵּין, מֵאֵת, מֵאַחֲרֵי,‎ (common in Late Hebrew, **for מִלְּ‎ in Mishna see e.g. Babylonian Mez 7:10; Kil 8:1; Ter 8:11; Pes 1:6; Taan 2:7; Yeb 8:2; Ecclesiastes 4:17 מִלַּעֲשׂוֺת‎ (have no knowledge so as not to do evil) is read by Siegf Wild; especially before infinitive; in O.T. only in מִלְּבוֺא מִלְּבַד,‎ (above 5a), מִלִּפְנֵי מִלְּפָנִים, מִלְּעֻמַּת, מִלְמַ֫טָּה, מִלְמַ֫עְלָה,‎, and, si vera lectio, הֶחָ֑רֶס מִלְמַעֲלֵה‎ Judg 8:13, see מַעֲלֶה‎), מִתַּ֫חַת מֵעִם, מֵעַל, מִנֶּגֶד,‎; see אֵת אַחֲרֵי,‎, etc.

b. לְמִן‎ (לְמִנִּי‎ Micah 7:12 (twice in verse)), with לְ‎ pleonastic, from = מִן‎, but used almost exclusively of the terminus a quo, whether of space or time (compare מִן‎

5); — (I) of space, Deut 4:32; Judg 20:1 שֶׁבַע וְעַדבְּֿאֵר לְמִדַּן‎, Micah 7:12.7:12 (both לְמִנִּי‎), Zech 14:10; 1Chr 5:9; לְמֵרָחוֺק‎ from afar Job 36:3; 39:29 (on Ezra 3:13; 2Chr 26:15, see below לְ עַד‎); לְ לְמִתַּחַת‎ = underneath 1Kin 7:32. Idiomatic, especially followed by וְעַד‎, to denote comprehensively an entire class, בְּהֵמָה וְעַד לְמֵאִישׁ‎ Exod 11:7; Jer 51:62 (לְמֵאָדָם‎), אִשָּׁה וְעַד לְמֵאִישׁ‎ 2Sam 6:19; 2Chr 15:13, גָּדוֺל וְעַד לְמִקָּטֹן‎ 2Kin 23:2; Jer 42:8, simil. 2Chr 15:13; Jer 31:34; Est 1:5, 20, וְעַדטֿוֺב לְמֵרָע‎ 2Sam 13:22, שָׁנָה עֶשְׂרִים לְמִבֶּן וּלְמָ֑טָּה‎ 1Chr 27:23, compare 2Chr 25:5. — On לְמִבֵּית‎ Num 18:7. (2) of time (often following by עַד‎), ֗֗֗ אֲשֶׁר הַיּוֺם לְמִן‎ from the day when . . ., Deut 4:32; 9:7; 2Sam 7:11 (|| 1Chr 17:10 אֲשֶׁר וּלְמִיָּמִים‎) Jer 7:25; 32:31; Hag 2:18; ֗֗֗ אֲשֶׁר הַיָּמִים לְמִקְצָת‎ Dan 1:18; הַיּוֺם לְמִן‎ followed by infinitive (in apposition) Exod 9:18; 2Sam 19:25; לְמִיּוֺם‎ followed by infinitive (genitive) Judg 19:30; 2Sam 7:6; Isa 7:17; ֗֗֗ לְמִימֵי‎ 2Kin 19:25 (|| Isa 37:26 מימי‎) Mal 3:7; למןֿ עולם ועד עולם‎ Jer 7:7; 25:5; לְמֵרָחוֺק‎ from afar = long before, 2Sam 7:19 = 1Chr 17:17; 2Kin 19:25 = Isa 37:26.

מְנָאוֺת‎ see מְנָת‎ below מנה‎. below

[מַנְגִּינָה‎] see נגן‎.

II. מִנֵּי מִנִּי,‎ see מִן‎. מִנִּי‎ Psa 45:9 see I. [ מֵן‎].

מִנָיוֺת‎ see מְנָת‎ below מנה‎.

מִנְיָמִן מִנְיָמִין,‎ see מִיָּמִן‎.

מִנְלָם‎ see [ מִנְלֶה‎] below נלה‎.

מנן‎ (of following; Arabic is praecidit funem, diminuit numerum,debilitavit; also be bounteous, Qor 3:158 and elsewhere, a gift; whence ZerweckPräp. Min 4 assumes a primary meaning to separate — either from or for ("zutheilen"), as the case might be).

גחר‎ (? compare Arabic retire, retreat, etc.)

גיא.def:
H1516. gay

גַּיְא‎ noun masculineIsa 40:4 (feminineZech 14:4) valley — absolute גַּיְא‎ Num 21:20 8t. + 1Sam 17:52 (compare below), גָּ֑יְא‎ 1Chr 4:39, גֵּיא‎ Zech 14:4, גֶּיא‎ Isa 40:4, גַּי‎ Deut 34:6 2t.; construct גֵּיא‎ Isa 22:1 21t.; גֵּי‎ Josh 15:8 13t.; plural absolute גֵּאָיוֺת‎ Ezek 31:12; 36:4, 6 + 7:16; 32:5 (strike out Co) + 6:3; 2Kin 2:16 Qr (so Co Ezek 6:3; Kt גיאות‎); suffix גֵּיאוֺתֶיךָ‎ 35:8; — valley Josh 8:11 (E) Micah 1:6; 1Sam 17:3; 2Kin 2:16 (opposed to הַר‎) Isa 40:4 (opposed to הַר גִּבְעָה,‎), Ezek 6:3; 35:8; 36:4, 6 (in all with הרים אפיקים, גבעות‎), 31:12 (opposed to הַר‎), compare 7:16 (strike out B Co) 32:5; specifically, valley in Moab, a station of Israel Num 21:20 (E); over against Beth-Peor Deut 3:29; 4:46; 34:6; a valley near גְּדוֺר‎ 1Chr 4:39; ׳ג חִזָּיוֺן‎ Isa 22:1, 5 near Jerusalem; ׳ג שְׁמָנִים‎ 28:1, 4 valley of fatness, fertility, the valley surrounding Samaria; הַגּ ׳שַׁעַר‎2Chr 26:9; Neh 2:13, 15; 3:13; apocalyptic valley Zech 14:4, made by cleaving Mt. of Olives, compare ׳ג הרים‎ 14:5; 14:5; valley of slaughter ׳ג ההרגה‎, a future name of valley of Hinnom Jer 7:32; 19:6; 1Sam 17:52 (גַּיְא‎) ᵐ5‎ reads גַּת‎ compare We Dr; Jer 2:23 of valley of Hinnom, see below; figurative Psa 23:4 ׳ג צלמות‎ compare צלמות‎; Ezek 39:11 ׳ג הָעֹבְרִים‎, Co הָעֲבָרִים‎ proper name compare below; elsewhere in combination with proper names: —

a. ׳ג יִפְתַּחאֵֿל‎ Josh 19:14, 27 perhaps = Jotapata JosBJ iii. 7, 7; Rabbin. גופתתא‎ RelandPal 816; — Tell Jefât RobBR iii. 107. GuérinGal. i. 476 f. compare BdPal 243.

b. ׳ג הַצְּבֹעִים‎ 1Sam 13:18.

c. הַֿמֶּלַךְ׳ג‎ 2Kin 14:7 (Kt; Qr omits article) 1Chr 18:12; 2Chr 25:11 = מֶֿלַךְ׳ג‎ 2Sam 8:13; Psa 60:2 (title); south of Dead Sea, in or bordering on Edom; el-Ghôr RobBR ii. 109.

d. ׳ג הֶחָרָשִׁים‎ 1Chr 4:14; Neh 11:35, apparently near Lod & Ono, northwest of Jerusalem, not far from the sea.

e. ׳ג לְמָרֵשָׁה צְפַ֖תָֿה‎2Chr 14:9 (? read ᵐ5 צָפֹנַה,‎ κατὰ βορρᾶν, to the north of M.) probably near the great plain of Judah, west of Jerusalem, toward the sea; ׳ג הָעֹבְרִים‎ Ezek 39:11, east of Dead Sea (Hi Sm), Co reads ׳ג הָעֲבָרִים‎

f. name to be changed to ׳ג הֲמוֺןגּֿוֺג‎ Ezek 39:11, 15. Most frequently

g. הִנֹּם גֵּי‎ Josh 15:8; 18:16; Neh 11:30, בֶןהִֿנֹּם גֵּי‎ Josh 15:8; 18:16; 2Kin 23:10 Qr (Kt ה בני ׳גי‎) 2Chr 28:3; 33:6; Jer 7:31-32, 19:2, 6; 32:35; valley southwest & south of Jerusalem (RobBR ii. 273 f.), where incense was burned, and children were offered in sacrifice to 'Molech.' Others identify with the TyropÊon valley, compare RSSemitic i. 353; see further תֹּפֶת הִנֹּם,‎.

גיח.def:
H1520. Giach

גִּיחַ‎ proper name, of a location (from a spring?) near Gibeon in Benjamin 2Sam 2:24.

גיחון.def:
H1521. Gichon

גִּיחוֺן‎ proper name, of a river (a bursting forth) —

1 one of the rivers of Eden Gen 2:13 (on theories of identity see Commentaries; also SmithDict. Bible Schaff-HerzogArt. Eden SpurrellText of Gen. on the passage RiHWB).

2 spring of water near Jerusalem: גִּחוֺן‎ 1Kin 1:33, 38, 45, הָעֶלְיוֺן גִיחוֺן מֵימֵי‎2Chr 32:30, בַּנַּחַל לְגִיחוֺן‎33:14; — there are two main theories as to locality:

a. west of Jerusalem, connected with Birket Mamilla, and aqueduct into city RobBR i. 239, 345 ff. SurveyJerusalem and others;

b. east of Jerusalem = Fountain of the Virgin, FurrerSchenkel BL ii. 483 BdPal 101, or Siloah water-system GutheZPV, v., 1882, 359 ff.

גֵּיחֲזִי‎ see below גַּיְא‎.

גיחזי.def:
H1522. Gechazi

גֵּחֲזִי גֵּיחֲזִי,‎ proper name, masculine (valley of vision?) servant of Elisha, גֵּיחֲזִי‎ 2Kin 4:12, 14, 25, 27, 29, 36; 5:20-21, גֵּחֲזִי‎ 4:31; 5:25; 8:4-5,.

גיד‎ (√ of following; meaning dubious; ? compare As gâdu, bind, fetter, JägerBAS i. 589f.)

גיל.def:
H1524. giyl

I. גִּיל‎ noun [masculine] rejoicing — Job 3:22 6t., גִּו֯ל‎ Prov 23:24; suffix גִּילִי‎ Psa 43:4; — rejoicing 65:13; Prov 23:24; || שׂמחה‎ Psa 45:16; Isa 16:10; Jer 48:33; Joel 1:16, גִילִי שִׂמְחַת‎ Psa 43:4, גיל אל שׂמח‎ glad unto rejoicing Hosea 9:1; Job 3:22.

II. [גִּיל‎] noun [masculine] circle, age, גִלְכֶם כְּ אשׁר הילדים מן‎ of the youths which are of your age Dan 1:10 (compare Arabic Samaritan גיל‎ = Hebrew דור‎ = γενεά, Talmud גילו בן‎ one born at the same time, a contemporary).

גילה.def:
H1525. gilah

גִּילָה‎ noun feminine rejoicing Isa 65:18, וְרַנֵּן גִּילַת‎ 35:2 (verbal noun for Infinitive absolute compare De Di; construct before וְ‎ Ges§ 130. 2; but read probably גִּילָה‎); הַגִּילָה‎ read 9:2 for לֹא הַגּוֺי‎ by Krochm Che RS Di.

גילני.def:
H1526. Giloni

גִּילֹנִי‎ adjective, of a people 2Sam 15:12, 23:34 = 1Chr 11:36, where also read ׳הַגּ‎ (for הַמְּלֹנִי ᵑ0‎).

גִּיגַת‎ see below גנן‎.

גיר‎ (boil, boil up? compare Aramaic גִּיר‎ wave, Late Hebrew id. foam; Arabic quicklime, also heat in chest from rage or hunger (Lane); admodum aestuans according to Fl NHWBi. 433 b; but compare below)

גינת.def:
H1527. Ginath

גִּינַ֑ת‎ proper name, masculine father of Tibni 1Kin 16:21-22,.

גיר.def:
H1528. gir

[גִּיר‎] noun [masculine] chalk, plaster (so ᵑ7‎; Biblical Hebrew once, p. 162); — emphatic גִּירָא‎ Dan 5:5.

[גַּלְגַּל‎] see גלל‎. below

גישן.def:
H1529. Geshan

גֵּישָׁן‎ proper name, masculine a descendant of Judah through Caleb 1Chr 2:47.

גֹּל גֵּל, גַּל,‎ see below גלל‎

גלב‎ ( = shear, shave, Assyrian [galâbu] HptSFG; Aramaic גְּלַב‎ id., גְּלָב‎ razor; compare 2Sam 20:8 see PS).

גל.def:
H1561. gelel

or gel [גֵּל‎] noun [masculine] dung (ball of dung, Arabic etc., dung of camels etc., compare Aramaic גַּלָּא‎; on form see Ew§ 255 b Ol§ 150. 163) — suffix גֶּלֲלוֺ‎ Job 20:7, plural construct הָאָדָם‎ (צֵאַת‎) גֶּלֲלֵי‎ Ezek 4:12, 15; — human dung used as fuel 4:12, 15 ׳ג הָאָדָם (צֵאַת)‎; perhaps also Job 20:7, but compare Di, who thinks no reference to fuel, & De who thinks of cattle-dung; (see on Arabic word Wetzst in De). — See also II.גָּלָל‎.

גֻּלָּהּ גֹּל,‎ see גֻּלָּה‎. below

גלב.def:
H1532. gallab

[גַּלָּב‎] noun [masculine] barber (Phoenician גלב‎ CISi, 257 ff.) — Ezek 5:1 הַגַּלָּבִים תַּעַר‎.

גלבע.def:
H1533. Gilboa

גִּלְבֹּעַ‎ proper name, of a location Gilboa` (derivation unknown), mountain-ridge at southeast end of plain of Jezreel, where Saul & Jonathan were killed; usually with article הַגּ ׳הַר‎ 1Sam 31:1, 8; 2Sam 1:6; בַּגִּלְבֹּעַ הָרֵי‎ 1:21 (David's lament); ׳בַּגּ‎ alone 1Sam 28:4; 2Sam 21:12; without article גִּלְבֹּעַ הַר‎ 1Chr 10:1, 8 (|| 1Sam 31:1, 8 above); — modern Jebel Fu‡û±a BdPal 244.

גֻּלְֹגּלֶת גִּלְגָּל, גַּלְגַּל,‎ see below גלל‎.

גלד‎ (√ of following meaning dubious perhaps compare Ethiopic obducere, inducere; Arabic scourge).

גלגל.def:
H1534. galgal

גַּלְגַּל‎ noun masculineEccl 12:6 wheel, whirl, whirlwind (on formation compare BaNB 204) — absolute ׳ג‎ Ezek 10:2 7t.; גַּלְגַּ֑ל‎ Psa 83:14; plural with suffix גַּלְגִּלָּיו‎ Isa 5:28; Jer 47:3; —

1 wheel,

a. of war-chariot Isa 5:28; Jer 47:3, also collective Ezek 23:24; 26:10; perhaps also in Ezekiel's vision 10:2, 6, 13 (compare wheelwork) but compare below

b. for drawing water Eccl 12:6.

2. a. whirl (of dust or chaff) Psa 83:14; Isa 17:13, simile of foes put to flight by God.

b. perhaps whirling of wheels Ezek 10:2, 6, 13 Sm RV, but compare above

c. whirlwind Psa 77:19.

גלגלת.def:
H1538. gulgoleth

גֻּלְגֹּ֫לֶת‎ noun feminine skull, head, poll (person) (on formation compare BaNB 205; Aramaic גּוּלְגַּלְתָּא‎) — absolute ׳ג‎ 2Kin 9:35 3t.; suffix גֻּלְגָּלְתּוֺ‎ Judg 9:53; 1Chr 10:10; plural suffix גֻּלְגְּלֹתָם‎ Num 1:2 5t.; —

1 skull, as broken by a stone Judg 9:53; as severed from body 2Kin 9:35; 1Chr 10:10.

2 head, poll (in counting, taxing, etc.; only P and late) לַגּ ׳עֹמֶר‎ Exod 16:16 an omer for every man; compare 38:26; Num 1:2, 18, 20, 22; 3:47; 1Chr 23:3, 24.

גלד.def:
H1539. geled

[גֶּ֫לֶד‎] noun masculine skin (Arabic , Aramaic גִּלְדָּא‎, ) of man Job 16:15 גִלְדִּ֑י עֲלֵי תָּפַרְתִּי שַׂק‎.

גלה.def:
H1542. Giloh

גִּלֹה‎ proper name, of a location city in mountains of Judah Josh 15:51; 2Sam 15:12; (on v compare Dr 15:12.)

גִּלֹה‎ proper name, of a location see below גיל‎.

גֻּלָּה‎ see below גלל‎.

גלו.def:
H1547. galuth

or galu [גָּלוּ‎ K§ 61. 4] noun feminine exile; — emphatic גָלוּתָא בְּגֵי‎ i.e. exiles, Ezra 6:16; Dan 2:25; 5:13; 6:14 (compare Biblical Hebrew גּוֺלָה‎).

גלולים.def:
H1544. gillul

[גִּלּוּל‎] noun masculineJer 50:27 only plural idols (= logs, blocks, shapeless things Ges BaudRel i. 95; Ew doll-images > dungy things Sm Ezek 6:4 SS after Rabb) **See BaudZMG, 1904, 395 ff. (compares Biblical Aramaic גְּלָל‎ (אֶבֶן‎), Palmyrene גללא‎Tariff i. 9 = στήλη λιθινη; and concludes that it was originally a designation of the primitive stone menhir or מַצֵּבָה‎). — גִּלּוּלִים‎ 22:8 3t. + 30:13 (strike out B Co); גִּלֻּלִים‎ 1Kin 15:12 2t.; construct גִּלּוּלֵי‎ Ezek 8:10 6t.; גִּלּוּלַיִךְ‎ 22:4; גִּלּוּלָיו‎ 2Kin 21:11 4t.; גִּלּוּלֶיהָ‎ Jer 50:2; יֵ֯כֶם‎ Lev 26:30 7t.; יֵ֯כֶן‎ Ezek 23:49; יֵ֯הֶם‎ 6:9 14t. + 6:5 (del BA al Co); יֵ֯הֶן‎ 23:37; — idols (39 t. Ezekiel); — 1Kin 15:12; 2Kin 17:12; 21:21; Ezek 6:5 (del Co) 6:9; 6:13 (twice in verse); 14:4-5, 18:6, 15; 20:16, 24, 39; 23:37, 39, 49; 33:25; 44:10, 12; || שִׁקּוּצִים‎ Deut 29:16; 2Kin 23:24 (|| also תְּרָפִים‎), Ezek 20:7, 18 (both with verb טמא‎) 20:8; 37:23, compare also 8:10 (שֶׁקֶץ‎, but שִׁקּוּצִים‎ apparently ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ & so Co); || תּוֺעֵבָה‎ 14:6; 2Kin 21:11, compare Ezek 18:12; 16:36 (תוֺעֲבוֺתַיִךְ גִּלּוּלֵי‎), & 1Kin 21:26 (where verb תָּעַב‎); || טֻמְאוֺת‎ Ezek 36:25; || עֲוֺנוֺ מִכְשׁוֺל‎ 14:3-4, 7; || עֲצַבִּים‎ Jer 50:2; || אֱלִילִים‎ Ezek 30:13 (Co אילים‎; compare also above); || חַמָּן‎ 6:4, 6; Lev 26:30 (compare below); || תְּרָפִים‎ 2Kin 23:24 (above); in phrase בְּגִלּ ׳טִמֵּא‎ etc. Ezek 20:7, 18, 31; 22:3-4, 23:7, 30; 36:18 (del Co); בְגִלּ ׳תְּחַלְּלוּ‎ 20:39; — note especially the expression גִלּוּלֵיכֶם עַלמִּֿגְרֵי מִּגְרֵיכֶם וְנָתַתִּי‎ Lev 26:30 and I will lay your carcases upon the carcases of your idols.

גלום.def:
H1545. gelom

[גְּלוֺם‎] noun [masculine] wrapping, garment (Aramaic גְּלִימָא‎, = Persian according to Fl ChWBi. 143 SFräLOPh i. (1883-4) 410), תְּכֵלֶת בִּגְלוֺמֵי‎ Ezek 27:24.

גלות.def:
H1546. galuth

גָּלוּת‎ noun feminine exile — Isa 20:4 9t.; גָּלֻת‎ Obadiah 20 (twice in verse); suffix גָּלוּתִי‎ 45:13, גָּלוּתֵינוּ‎ Ezek 33:21; 40:1 (Qames unchangeable); —

1 absolute exile, 2Kin 25:27; Jer 52:31; Ezek 1:2; 33:21; 40:1; Amos 1:6, 9; Obadiah 20 (twice in verse).

2 collective exiles, כושׁ גלות‎ Isa 20:4, יהודה גלות‎ Jer 24:5; 28:4; 29:22; 40:1, ישׁלח גלותי‎ he shall let my exiles (Yahweh's) go free Isa 45:13; see LagArm. Stud. § 445. **Amos 1:6; 1:9 compare Obad 20 (twice in verse) and Jer 13:19 (ᵐ5‎ Du Co and others).

גלח.def:
H1548. galach

[גָּלַח‎] verb be bald (Arabic );

Pi`el shave, shave off (so Late Hebrew, Aramaic) — Perfect וְגִלַּח‎ consecutive Lev 14:8 2t.; suffix וְגִלְּחוֺ‎ consecutive 2Sam 14:26; 3feminine singular וְגִלְּחָה‎ consecutive Deut 21:12; Imperfect יְגַלַּח‎ Lev 14:9; Isa 7:20, יְגַלֵּחַ֑‎ Lev 13:33 2t., וַיְגַלַּח‎ Gen 41:14; 2Sam 10:4; suffix (3masculine singular) וַיְגַלְּחֵם יְגַלְּחֶגּוּ,‎1Chr 19:4; 3 feminine singular וַתְּנַלַּךְ‎ Judg 16:19; 3masculine plural יְגַלֵּ֑חוּ‎ Lev 21:5; Ezek 44:20; Infinitive suffix of subject גַּלְּחוֺ‎ 2Sam 14:26; —

1 shave, object the head, ראֹשׁ‎ Num 6:9 (twice in verse); 6:18 (P) Deut 21:12 (hair as containing impurity, compare RSSem i. 407), 2Sam 14:26 (twice in verse) compare; 14:26; Ezek 44:20; Lev 13:33 (P), object הַנֶתֶק‎; object persons 1Chr 19:4.

2 shave off, the hair שֵׂעָר‎ Lev 14:8-9, (twice in verse) (P) compare Judg 16:19; the beard זָקָן‎ Lev 21:5 (H) 2Sam 10:4.

3 figurative of devastation by Assyrians Isa 7:20 (object הָרַגְלָ֑יִם שַׂעַר הָראֹשׁ,‎ and הַזָּקָן‎).

4 intransitive he shaved (himself) Gen 41:14 (E).

Pu`al Perfect גֻּלָּ֑ח‎ Judg 16:22, גֻּלַּחְתִּי‎ 16:17; Participle construct מְגֻלְּחֵי‎ Jer 41:5; — be shaven, subject person (of Samson) Judg 16:17, 22; זָקָן מְגֻלְּחֵי‎ Jer 41:5.

Hithpa`el Perfect וְהִתְגַּלָּ֑ח‎ consecutive Lev 13:33; Infinitive suffix הִתְגַּלְּחוֺ‎ Num 6:19; — shave oneself Lev 13:33; with accusative אֶתנִֿזְרוֺ‎ Num 6:19 (both P).

I. גלל‎ ( be great in rank or dignity (often of God)).

גליון.def:
H1549. gillayon

גִּלָּיוֺן‎ noun masculine table, tablet (Talmud גִּלְיוֺן‎, the empty margin of page or roll, see LagGN 1881, 403, compare BN 199) — עָלָיו וּכְתֹב גָּדוֺל גִּלָּיוֺן קַחלְֿךָ‎ take thee a great tablet and write upon it Isa 8:1; plural הַגִּלְֹינִים‎ tablets of polished metal, mirrors 3:23 ᵑ9 ᵑ7‎ Ges Che Di De; but transparent garments, gauzes, ᵐ5‎ Ew (compare Arabic fine garment).

גליל.def:
H1551. galil

II. גָּלִיל‎ noun masculine cylinder, rod, circuit, district; —

1 cylinder, rod, only plural construct כֶסֶף גְּלִילֵי‎ Est 1:6 of support of rich hangings (|| שֵׁשׁ עַמּוּדֵי‎); & בַּתַּרְשִׁישׁ מְמֻלָּאִים זָהָב גְּלִילֵי‎ Song 5:14, simile of (? fingers of) hands: cylinders of gold set with topaz.

2 circuit, district, on northern border of Israel in Naphtali (see below), population largely heathen (Late Hebrew id. Aramaic גְּלִילָא‎, ) — הַגּוֺיִם גְּלִיל‎ Isaiah 8:23; elsewhere =

proper name, of a location always with article Josh 20:7; 21:32; 1Chr 6:61 all בַּגּ ׳קֶדֶשׁ‎; הַגּ ׳אֶרֶץ‎ 1Kin 9:11, so also ᵐ5‎ Josh 12:23 (compare Di) for גִּלְגַּל‎ q. v.; הַגָּלִ֫ילָה‎ Galilee, 2Kin 15:29 (|| נַפְתָּלִי אֶרֶ֖‎) Ew§ 173 h n Sta§ 308 a 2 Ges§ 90 f.

גלילה.def:

גם.def:
H1571. gam

גַּם‎768 adverb denoting addition, also, moreover, yea (Moabite id., also Zinjirli (Lzb250 Cooke166); probably akin to √ ; compare (accusative) in a mass, altogether) —

1 also, moreover, emphasizing sometimes the thought of an entire sentence, but more usually the word immediately following, as Gen 3:6 לְאִישָׁהּ גַּם וַתִּתֵּן‎ and gave also to her husband, Genesis 3:27 and take also of the tree of life, 7:3; 19:21; 24:19; 26:21; 29:27; 30:15; 32:21 (֗֗֗ הִגֵּה גַּם‎: so Est 7:9) Gen 48:11; Exod 8:28; 12:32b Deut 1:37; 1Sam 28:20; 2Sam 11:12; 2Kin 9:27; Isa 7:13 +. Often before pronouns, Gen 4:4 הוּא גַם הֵבִיא וְהֶבֶל‎ and Abel, he also brought, 20:5 וְהִיאגַֿםהִֿוא‎ (so only here) and she herself also, 20:6; 27:31 הוּא גַּם וַיַּעַשׂ‎, 30:8; Deut 3:20; Judg 3:31; 6:35; 9:19; 1Sam 19:20-24 Jer 12:6; 48:26 etc. (compare MI6 הא גם ויאמר‎): especially in Genealogies of J (BuUrg. 220) Gen 4:22, 26; 10:21; 19:38; 22:20, 24 compare Judg 8:31. גַּם‎ followed by pronoun also begins a sentence with emphasis in an elevated style, thou (they) also, Isa 14:10; Jer 12:6 (twice in verse); 48:7; Ezek 16:52; Nahum 3:11 (twice in verse). After a pronoun in an oblique case (Ges§ 135, 2) Gen 27:34; 1Sam 19:23; 2Sam 17:5; Jer 25:14; 27:7 +. וְגַם‎ and also (more often than גַּם‎ alone attaching a sentence) Gen 6:4; 14:16; 15:14; 17:16; 20:12; 24:14, 46; 30:6; 37:7; 38:24; 42:28; Exod 2:19; 3:9; 4:14; Josh 7:11 (5 t.) 1Sam 4:17; 1Kin 21:19 + often; with a negative = neither Exod 5:2; 34:3 and elsewhere — גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎ (like et ... et) both ... and Gen 44:16; 47:3, 19; Num 18:3; Jer 51:12; Psa 49:3 +: גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎ Gen 24:25; Judg 8:22; Eccl 9:6: with a negative neither ... nor Num 23:25; 1Sam 20:27; 1Kin 3:26, and (3t.) Gen 43:8; Exod 4:10; 1Sam 28:6. So (but seldom) גַּםוְ֗֗֗גַם‎ Gen 24:44; Exod 10:25f.; 1Sam 2:26; 12:14; 26:25: with negative 21:9. — N.B. In poetry independence and emphasis is sometimes given by גַּם‎ to a new idea, where in English we should be satisfied with and: Psa 107:5; 137:1; Job 24:19; Cant 7:14; Lam 4:15.

2 with stress on a particular word, even, Exod 4:9; Num 22:33 אוֺתְךָ גַּם‎ even thee I had slain, and kept her alive, 2Sam 17:10; Jer 2:33; Psa 132:12; Prov 14:13 even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, 14:20; 17:28; 20:11; Ruth 2:15; Nehemiah 3:35; and so often after כִּי‎, Deut 12:31 for even their sons they burn in the fire to their gods, 1Sam 22:17; Isa 26:12; Jer 6:11; 12:6; 14:5; Hosea 9:12 לָהֶם כִּיגַֿםאֿוֺי‎ for even woe is it to them when I depart from them; הֲגַם‎ Gen 16:13; 1Sam 10:11-12, = 19:24; 1Kin 17:20; Psa 78:20; Job 41:1; Est 7:8. Other cases: — 1Sam 24:12 רְאֵה גַּם רְאֵה‎ see, yea see ! (but HupQu. Job vi. רָאֹה גַּם‎: compare below) Psa 118:11; Job 2:10 נְקַבֵּל אֶתהַֿטּוֺב גַּם‎ shall we receive good (emphatic) from God and not evil ? 21:7; interposed once between a substantive and adjective Gen 20:4 Gentemne etiam justam interficies? emphasizing כֹּל‎, Deut 28:61; Judg 9:49b 1Sam 22:7 לְכֻלְּכֶם גַּםֿ‎ to all (emphatic) of you will he give ...? 2Sam 19:31 יִקָּ֑ח אֶתהַֿכֹּל גַּם‎ yea, the whole let him take! Isa 26:12; אֶחָד‎ 2Sam 17:12b and we will not leave ֗֗֗ אֶחָד גַּם‎ even one (similarly 17:13 b), Psa 14:3 (= 53:4) אֶחָד גַּם אֵין‎; an infinitive or cognate accusative attached to a verb, Gen 31:15; 46:4; Num 11:15; 16:13; 1Sam 1:6. שְׁנֵיהֶם גַּם‎ literally even both i.e. the one as well as the other (German alle beide) is said idiomatically, Gen 27:45 (שְׁנֵיכֶם‎), Deut 22:22; 23:19; 1Sam 25:43 (שְׁתֵּיהֶן‎), Prov 17:15; 20:10, 12; Ruth 1:5.

3 introducing a climax, yea, especially in a rhetorical style, Gen 27:33; Deut 23:3; 23:4; Judg 5:4 (twice in verse); Isa 13:3; 14:8; 43:13 yea, from to-day I am the same, 44:12 רָעֵב גַּם‎ yea, he is hungry, and has no strength, 47:3; 48:8 (3 t. in verse); 57:7; Jer 46:16; 48:2; 51:44; Hosea 7:9; Psa 41:10; 84:7; 139:12; Isa 66:8 אֶתבָּֿנֶיהָ צִיּוֺן גַּםיָָֽֿלְדָה, כִּיחָֿ֫לָה‎, Jer 5:28; 12:2; Ezek 24:5; Job 21:7; Song 8:1: emphasizing an extreme, or aggravated, case, yea, even, Isa 49:15 yea, these may forgot, Jer 8:17 yea, the stork knoweth, etc., Isa 23:12 שָׁם גַּם‎ even there no rest shall be for thee (so Psa 139:10), Isa 49:25; 57:6; Jer 23:11b; Mal 3:15; Psa 84:4.

4 expressing correspondence, especially in the matter of retribution (the גַּם‎ correlativum), so frequently אָנֹכִי גַּם אֲנִי, גַּם‎ I also (on my part): — Gen 20:6 I also [as well as thyself] know that thou hast done this innocently, Josh 24:18; Judg 2:21; 1Sam 1:28 (compare Dr) 28:22 אַתָּה גַּם‎ thou also (as I have done 28:21), 2Sam 12:13 ׳י‎ also [responding to thy confession] hath removed thy sin, 2Kin 2:3, 5; Isa 31:2; 66:3-4 (גם ֗֗֗ גם‎, emphasizing the action of both parties), Jer 2:36; 4:12 now will I also [in correspondence with their deeds] speak judgments with them, 7:11; 51:49 (גם ֗֗֗ גם‎), Ezek 5:8, 11; 16:43 (וְגַם‎ = therefore also), 23:35; Hosea 4:6 because thou hast forgotten the direction of thy God, I also (on my part) will forget thy children, Psa 52:7 (thou lovest evil, etc.) יִתָּצְךָ אֵל גַּם‎ God also (on his part) will pluck thee up, 71:22; 133:1; Prov 1:26; Job 7:11; 12:3; 16:4; so וְגַם‎ Judg 2:3; Amos 4:6-7, Micah 6:13; Mal 2:9. In the apodosis (uncommon): Gen 13:16 if a man could number the dust of the earth, יִמָּנֶה זַרְעֲךָ גַּם‎ thy seed also should be numbered, Jer 31:36-37, 33:21, 26; Zech 8:6. The correspondence is sometimes of the nature of a climax: Gen 27:33; 30:8 I have wrestled, יָכֹלְתִּי גַּם‎ (compare 1Kin 22:22 תּוּכָ֔ל וְגַם‎, Jer 50:24), Isa 66:8.

5 connecting two ideas which express (or imply) a contradiction, גַּם‎ acquires sometimes an adversative force (compare אַף‎ 1 end), yet, but, though: Psa 95:9 they tried me, but also (Che) saw my work (namely of judgment), 129:2; Jer 6:15 = 8:12; Ezek 20:23; Eccl 4:8, 16; 5:18; Neh 6:1. So וְגַם‎ Ezek 16:28; 20:15; Eccl 3:13; 6:7; Neh 5:8.

6 כִּי גַּם‎ (with imperfect) yea, when Lam 3:8, even when Prov 22:6; yea though (stating an imagined case) Isa 1:15; Hosea 8:10; 9:16; Psa 23:4 (so אִם גַּם‎ Eccl 8:17); also (is it) that Ruth 2:21 (see כִּי‎ 1d). גַם כִּי‎ = for even (see above 2); = though even, although (conceding a fact) Eccl 4:14 (see De) 8:12.

גמא.def:
H1573. gome

גֹּ֫מֶא‎ noun masculineJob 8:11 rush, reed, papyrus (compare Löwp. 55) (Late Hebrew גּוֺמֶא‎, Ethiopic loan-word, according to Di; — name from swallowing, sucking up, water? so Thes, compare Che Isa 18:2 and elsewhere; = Coptic gome, see Di Exod 2:3 whence others derive as loan-word) — גֹּ֫מֶא‎ 2:3 3t.; — rush, paper-reed, (Egyptian) Job 8:11 (|| אָחוּ‎); collective Isa 35:7 (|| קָנֶה‎); as material, ג ׳תֵּבַת‎ Exod 2:3 chest of paper-reed; ׳כְּלֵיגֿ‎ Isa 18:2 vessels of paper-reed.
