גמולה.def:
H5674. abar

עָבַר‎548 verb pass over, through, by, pass on (Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew; Zinjirli עבר‎ Haph`el Lzb336 Cook88, perhaps also Nabataean עבר‎ Idib.; עֲבַר ᵑ7‎, Syriac id.; Assyrian ebêru, id. DlHWB 10, and derivatives; Arabic id., and derivatives; Sabean עבר‎ = Hebrew עִבַּר‎

1 MordtSabDenkm 49; עברת‎ passage, march through DHMZMG xxix (1875), 614 also bank or neighbourhood of a stream SabDenkm49); —

Qal465 Perfect3masculine singular ׳ע‎ Gen 15:17 +, suffix עֲבָרוֺ‎ Jer 23:9; 1singular עָבַ֫רְתִּי‎ 1Sam 15:24 +; 2 masculine plural עֲבַרְתֶּם‎ Gen 18:5 +; 1 plural עָבַ֫רְנוּ‎ Josh 24:17 +, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יַעֲבֹר‎ Amos 8:5 +, יַעֲבָרֿ‎ Gen 33:14 +, suffix 3 masculine singular יַעַבְרֶ֫נּוּ‎ Isa 33:21; 35:8, יַעַבְרֶ֫נְהוּ‎ Jer 5:22, וַיַּעֲבֹר‎ Gen 12:6 +; 1 singular אֶעֱבֹר‎ Amos 5:17 +, cohortative אֶעְבְּרָה‎ Num 21:22 +, אֶעֱבֹ֑רָה‎ 20:19; Judg 12:5, etc.; Imperative masculine singular עֲבֹר‎ Exod 17:5 +; feminine singular עִבְרִי‎ Micah 1:11 2t.; עֲבֹ֑רִי‎ Isa 23:12; masculine plural עִבְרוּ‎ Amos 6:2 +; Infinitive absolute עָבוֺר‎ 2Sam 17:16; construct עֲבֹר‎ Amos 7:8 +, לַעֲבָרֿ‎ 1Kin 18:6 + Nahum 2:1 Qr (Kt לעבור‎); suffix עָבְרִי‎ Exod 33:22; Deut 4:21, etc.; Participle עֹבֵר‎ Judg 8:4 +, etc.; —

1 pass over:

a. = cross (stream, wady, sea, etc.), (1) with accusative Gen 31:21 (E), 32:11 (J), Josh 3:14, 17; 4:1 (all J E), Deut 2:14 (D), Num 32:29 (P), 2Sam 17:20, 22, 24; Isa 16:8, + 37 t., + Gen 32:23 (E; accusative מַעֲבַר‎), לַעֲבִיר הָֽעֲבָרָה וְעָֽבְרָה‎ 2Sam 19:19 (read וַיַּעַבְרוּ‎ We Dr Kit Löhr, and they crossed the ford, or וְעָֽבְרוּ‎ frequent., HPS; > ᵐ5‎ Klo Bu הָעֲבֹדָה וַיַּעַבְדוּ‎ and they performed the service); also with accusative + accusative of location 1Sam 13:7, + ה‎ locative Deut 4:26; 31:13; 32:47. (2) accusative omitted Judg 3:28; 2Sam 17:16 (twice in verse) + 32 t., + עֹבֵר‎ Judg 8:4 (read וַיַּעֲבֹר‎ Vrss, or strike out as gloss GFM Bu), 2Sam 15:23 a (where read עֹמֵד‎ for עֹבֵר ᵑ0‎ We Dr Bu Kit Löhr HPS, but strike out עֹבְרִים‎, plausibly, Klo HPS); with אֶלֿ‎ Num 32:7 (JE), Deut 27:2 (D), Josh 4:13; 22:19 (both P), with אֶלעֵֿבֶר‎ Deut 30:13, with הָעֵבֶר‎ 1Sam 26:13; with ה‎ locative Deut 3:21; 4:14; 6:1; 11:8, 11; 34:4; Isa 23:6; with accusative of location 23:12; Jer 2:10; Num 32:32 (P).

b. cross border, boundary, with accusative Num 20:17; b 21:22 b (both J E), + אֶלֿ‎ 1Sam 27:2; of invasion, accusative omitted, with אֶלֿ‎ Judg 11:32; 12:3; 1Sam 14:1, 6, 8, with ה‎ locative 2Kin 8:21, absolute 2Chr 21:9.

c. cross over (that is, intervening space) against (עַלֿ‎) 1Sam 14:4, unto 2Sam 24:20 (read אֶלֿ‎ for עַלֿ‎ Bu HPS, compare ᵐ5‎L), so perhaps also Isa 45:14 (עַל‎; read אֶל‎ ?); with accusative of goal Amos 5:5; 6:2.

d. pass, march over (that is, bodies of captives), Isa 51:23 (twice in verse).

e. = overflow, figurative, Isa 23:10, absolute of invasion (like a flood) 8:8, hence Dan 11:10, 40; Nahum 1:8 (compare 4c); of evil thoughts Psa 73:7; compare דִבְרֵירָֿ֑ע עָֽבְרוּ‎ Jer 5:28 they overflow with evil matters.

f. pass, go, over, of waves, over one's head, usually with עַלֿ‎ Isa 54:9; Psa 42:8; 88:17; 124:4; 124:5 (all figurative), Jonah 2:4; with accusative Psa 38:5, compare Jer 23:9 over whom wine hath gone (= overcome with wine).

g. of razor passing over head, with עַל‎ Numbers 6:50; figurative of time passing over one, with עַלֿ‎ 1Chr 29:30 (compare Biblical Aramaic על חלף‎ Dan 4:13 +).

h. pass over upon (עַלֿ‎), in weakened sense, nearly = come or light upon; of spirit Num 5:14 (twice in verse); 5:30; absolute + מֵאֵת‎ 1Kin 22:24 2Chr 18:23; with עַלֿ‎ also light upon in chastisement or judgment, Hosea 10:11; Job 13:13, compare Nahum 3:19; Deut 24:5 no affair shall pass over upon (עַלֿ‎) him, i.e. no duty be laid upon him.

(also construct Deut 33:29; Nahum 2:4); suffix מָגִנִּי‎ Psa 7:11 5t.; מָגִנֵּנוּ‎ 33:20 3t.; מָגִנָּם‎ 115:9; 115:10; 115:11; plural מָגִנִּים‎ 1Kin 10:17 6t.; מָגִנּוֺת‎2Chr 23:9; construct מָגִנֵּי‎ 1Kin 14:26 4t.; suffix מָגִנָּיו‎ Job 15:26; מָגִנֶּיהָ‎ Hosea 4:18; — shield, buckler, carried by warrior for defence Judg 5:8; 2Sam 1:21 (twice in verse); 2Kin 19:32 = Isa 37:33, 1Chr 5:18; 14:7; 17:17; 23:9; 26:14; 1Chron 32:5; Neh 4:10; Psa 76:4; Jer 46:3, 9; Ezek 23:24; 38:4-5, 39:9; Nahum 2:4; Isa 22:6; compare 21:5 (anoint the shield, to make it slippery), so also Psa 35:2 (where ׳י‎ figurative as warrior); מָגֵן אִישׁ‎ = armed man Prov 6:11; 24:34; laid up for show, or as treasure 1Kin 10:17 (twice in verse); 14:26-27, (= 2Chr 9:16 (twice in verse); 12:9-10,) 32:27 compare Song 4:4; Ezek 27:10; of scales of crocodile (leviathan) מָגִנִּים אֲפִיקֵי‎ Job 41:7; figurative of wicked's defence against judgments of מָגִנָּיו גַבֵּי עֲבִי ׳י,‎ 15:26; fig, of king Psa 89:19 (compare Che); figurative of rulers of Ephraim Hosea 4:18; figurative of rulers of earth Psalm 47:10; figurative (very often) of ׳י‎, as defence of his servants, Psa 3:4; 7:11 (read אל עָלַי ׳מָגִנִּי‎ compare Che critical note) 18:3; 18:31; 18:36 (= 2Sam 22:3, 31, 36) Psa 28:7; 33:20; 59:12; 84:10; 84:12; 115:9; 115:10; 115:11; 119:114; 144:2; Prov 2:7; 30:5, and see especially Gen 15:1 (E).

גן.def:
H1588. gan

גַּן‎ noun masculineSong of Solomon 4:12 & (Gen 2:15) feminine enclosure, garden (Late Hebrew id., גַּנָּה‎ Arabic , Ethiopic Assyrian ginû COTGloss, also gannatu DlPr 84; Aramaic גִּנְתָּא גִּנָּא,‎, ; Phoenician צץ אם אגנן פר‎[צ‎] CISi, 165, 11 & p. 232 f. birds of enclosure (domestic fowls) or of wing) — absolute גַּן‎ 2:8 3t.; construct id. 2:15 19t.; with article הַגָּן‎ 2:9 9t., but כַּגַּן‎ Lam 2:6; suffix גַּנִּי‎ Song 4:16; 5:1, גַּנּוֺ‎ 4:16; 6:2; Plural גַּנִּים‎ 4:15 2t. — garden as enclosure Lam 2:6 (simile); בַּגַּנִּים הַיּוֺשֶׁבֶת‎ Song 8:13; compare 4:12 (figurative of, bride נָעוּל גַּן‎); g. of herbs (יָרָק‎) Deut 11:10; 1Kin 21:2; figurative of bride, g. of plants, fruits, and spices Song 4:16 (twice in verse); 5:1; 6:2 (twice in verse) compare גנים מַעְיַן‎ 4:15; g. of (king's) house) 2Kin 21:18 = גַּןעֻֿזָּא‎ 21:18, 26; הַמֶּלֶךְ גַּן‎ 25:4; Jer 39:4; 52:7; Neh 3:15, compare הַגָּן בֵּית‎) 2Kin 9:27 (at Jez-reel ? but this perhaps

proper name, of a location see below בית‎ p. III ); most often of garden (orchard ?) in Eden (Hexateuch only Gen & only J) Gen 2:8-9, 10, 16; 3:1-2, 3, 8 (twice in verse); 3:10, called גַּןעֵֿדֶן‎ 2:15; 3:23-24, Ezek 36:35; Joel 2:3, compare ׳גןיֿ‎ Gen 13:10; Isa 51:3 (both in simile); גןאֿלהים‎ Ezek 28:13 (גןאֿל ׳עֵדֶן‎), 31:8 (twice in verse); 31:9 (|| עֵדֶן‎); in last three the trees of the garden are compare with Assyrian under figure of cedar of Lebanon.

גנב.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

גנבת.def:
H1592. Genubath

גנז‎ (cover up, hide, compare Late Hebrew hide, Arabic cover up, Aramaic גְּנַז‎ Ithpa`al Ethpe`el be hidden, Ethiopic enwrap).

גנה.def:
H1593. gannah

גַּנָּה‎ noun feminine garden (compare foregoing) — גַּנָּה‎ Isa 1:30; 61:11; construct גִּנַּת‎ Song 6:11 3t.; suffix גַּנָּתוֺ‎ Job 8:16; plural גַּנֹּת‎ Num 24:6, גַּנּוֺת‎ Eccl 2:5-6t.; suffix גַּנּוֺתֵיכֶם‎ Amos 4:9; garden, orchard, 4:9 (|| זַיִת תְּאֵנָה, כֶּרֶם,‎), 9:14 (fruit-garden; || כֶּרֶם‎), Jer 29:5, 28; Eccl 2:5 (|| מַּרְדֵּס‎), אֱגוֺז גִּנַּת‎ Song 6:11 nut-garden; compare גִּנַּתבִּֿיתָן‎ Est 1:5; 7:7-8, in simile, of prosperous Israel Num 24:6 (poem in J E; עֲלַינָהָר׳ג‎), of chastised Israel Isa 1:30 (ג לָהּ אין מים ׳אשׁר‎), of Yahweh's blessing 61:11; in Job 8:16 עַלגַּֿנּוֺ‎ in figure of prosperity of wicked, as a luxuriant plant; gardens as places of idolatrous worship Isa 1:29 (|| אֵילִים‎), 65:3 (|| לְבֵנִים‎ ), 66:17 (i.e. groves).

גנז.def:
H1595. genez

[גְּנָזִים‎] noun [masculine] plural

1 chests (?);

2 treasury — only plural constructגִּנְזֵי‎; — 1 perhaps chests of variegated cloth ׳ג בְּרֹמִים‎ Ezek 27:24 so Thes AV RV; Sm Co and others cloths, carpets, Ew Taschen. 2 treasury (Late Hebrew גֶּנֶז‎, Aramaic גְּנִיז גִּנְזָא,‎, Biblical Aramaic construct plural גִּנְזֵי‎; Persian loan-word from treasure? compare Vullersii.1032 LagGes.Abh.27); הַמֶּלֶךְ גִּנְזֵי‎ Est 3:9; 4:7.

[גְּנַז‎] noun masculineEzra 6:1 treasure (ᵑ7‎; see Biblical Hebrew [ גְּנָזִים‎], below גנז‎); — plural emphatic גִּנְזִיָּא‎ treasures 6:1, ׳ג בֵּית מַלְכָּא דִּי‎ 5:17, construct מִלְכָּא גִּנְזֵי בֵּית‎ 7:20.

גנזך.def:
H1597. ganzak

גַּנְזַךְ‎ noun [masculine] treasury (Late Hebrew גנזכה‎ treasure; loan-word from or through Persian compare above & LagGes. Abh. 28); וְגַנְזַכָּיו‎ 1Chr 28:11. ᵐ5‎ τῶν ζακχὼ αὐτοῦ; but ᵐ5‎L τῶν ἀποθηκῶν αὐτοῦ.

גנן.def:
H1598. ganan

[גָּנַן‎] verb cover, surround, defend (Arabic , Aramaic אַגֵּן‎ (Aph`el), Palmyrene אגן‎ VogPalm.132 ff.) —

Qal Perfect וְגַנּוֺתִי‎ Isa 37:35 3t.; Infinitive absolute גָּנוֺן‎ 31:5 (c. Hiph`il q. v.) — defend, subject always ׳י‎; object the city Jerusalem with על‎ 37:35; 38:6 = 2Kin 20:6; 19:34 with אֶלֿ‎ (|| הוֺשִׁיעַ‎).

Hiph`il Imperfect — or

Qal according to BaZMG 1889, 178, who compare Arabic — יָגֵן‎ Isa 31:5 2t. — defend (= Qal), Jerusalem 31:5 גָּ֗֗֗נוֺן יגן‎ with על‎ (|| הִצִּיל‎); object Yahweh's people Zech 9:15 with על‎, 12:8 with בְּעַד‎.

גנתון.def:
H29. Abiyyah

2 2nd son of Samuel 1Sam 8:2; 1Chr 6:13.

3 son of Jerob. I 1Kin 14:1.

4 son of Becher, a Benjamite 1Chr 7:8.

גער.def:
H1605. gaar

גָּעַר‎ verb rebuke (Aramaic גְּעַר‎ id., Ethiopic cry out, Sabean יגער‎ proper name, SabDenkmp. 29.30) — Isa 17:13; גָּעַרְתָּ‎ Psa 9:6 2t., etc.; Imperfect יִגְעַר‎ Zech 3:2-3t., תִּגְעֲרוּ‎ Ruth 2:16; Imperative גְּעַר‎ Psa 68:31; Infinitive מִגְּעָרֿ‎ Isa 54:9; Participle גּוֺעֵר‎ Nahum 1:4, גֹּעֵר‎ Mal 2:3; — with בְּ‎ except Psa 9:6; 68:31; 119:21; Mal 2:3 where accusative; —

1 rebuke, father his son Gen 37:10 (E), reapers Ruth Ruth 2:16, priest Jeremiah Jer 29:27.

2 of God rebuking nations Psa 9:6; Isa 17:13, proud Psa 119:21, Satan Zech 3:2 (twice in verse), קנה חית‎ Psa 68:31, בָּאֹכֵל‎ (the devouring swarm of locusts, restraining them) Mal 3:11, the sea drying it up Psa 106:9; Nahum 1:4, Zion Isa 54:9; הַזֶּרַע‎ the seed (prevent the usual harvest) Mal 2:3 (ᵐ5‎ Aq הַזְּרֹעַ ᵑ9‎, the arm, namely, of priests, that they may not extend it to bless).

גערה.def:
H1606. gearah

גְּעָרָה‎ noun feminine rebuke — Prov 13:1-2t.; גַּעֲרַת‎ Eccl 7:5 5t.; suffix גַּעֲרָֽתְךָ‎ Psa 18:16 + (suffixes 6 t.); —

1 of man Prov 13:1, 8; 17:10; Eccl 7:5; Isa 30:17 (twice in verse).

געש.def:
H1607. gaash

[גָּעַשׁ‎] verb shake, quake (Late Hebrew id.) —

Qal Imperfect וַתִּגְעַשׁ‎ Psa 18:8 a = 2Sam 22:8 a Kt (Qr Hithpa`el); — quake of earth at theoph., Psa 18:8 = 2Sam 22:8 (read Kt; || רעשׁ‎).

Pu`al Imperfect be shaken up, convulsed יְגֹעֲשׁוּעַֿם‎ Job 34:20 a people are convulsed.

Hithpa`el shake back and forth, toss or reel to and fro וַיִּתְגָּעַשׁ‎ Qr 2Sam 22:8 a (< Kt Qal); יִתְגָָּֽעֲשׁוּ‎ Jer 46:7, וַיִּתְגָָּֽעֲשׁוּ‎ Psa 18:8b + 2t.; — of mountains 18:8b = 2Sam 22:8 b; of waves of sea, Jer 5:22; of waters of Nile 46:7 (compare 46:8).

Hithpo`el Perfect וְהִתְגֹּעֲשׁוּ‎ consecutive Jer 25:16; Imperfect יִתְגֹּעֲשׁוּ‎ 46:8; id. of waters of Nile 46:8; of drunken men, reel to and fro, 25:16 (figurative of nations confounded by ׳י‎).

גֶּ֫פֶן‎ noun feminineJudg 9:13 + (masculine only Hosea 10:1, perhaps influence of יִשְׂרָאֵל‎ 2Kin 4:39) vine (Late Hebrew id., Arabic (Yemen), Assyrian gapnu, compare ZehnpfBAS i. 633; Aramaic גֶּפֶן גּוֺפַן,‎, , plural ) — ׳ג‎ Gen 40:9 38t. (also construct, as Num 6:4; Deut 32:32; Isa 16:8-9,), גָּ֑פֶן‎ Judg 9:12 2t.; suffix גַּפְנִי‎ Joel 1:7, גַּפְנְךָ‎ Jer 5:17, גַּפְנוֺ‎ 1Kin 5:5 3t., גַּפְנָהּ‎ Hosea 2:14, גַּפְנָם‎ Deut 32:32 2t.; plural גְּפָנִים‎ Song 2:13; Hab 3:17 — vine (always grape-bearing except 2Kin 4:39) Gen 40:9-10, (in dream) 49:11; Num 20:5; Deut 8:8; Judg 9:12-13, (in allegory) 1Kin 5:5; 2Kin 18:31 = Isa 36:16; Psa 78:47; 105:33; Song 2:13; 6:11; 7:13; Isa 7:23; 24:7; 32:12; Jer 5:17; 8:13; Hosea 2:14; Joel 1:7, 12; 2:22; Micah 4:4; Hab 3:17; Hag 2:19; Zech 2:10; 8:12; Mal 3:11; שָׂדֶה גֶּפֶן‎ a vine bearing poisonous gourds 2Kin 4:39; הַיַּיִן גֶּפֶן‎ Num 6:4 (compare Gen 40:10; Judg 9:13) 13:14; הַגֶּפֶן אֶשְׁכְּלוֺת‎ Song 8:9; הַגֶּפֶן עֵץ‎ Ezek 15:2, 6; in simile of stars fading away at Yahweh's judgment Isa 34:4; in simile of wicked losing early promise Job 15:33; in simile of wife Psa 128:3; figurative of Israel 80:9; 80:15; Ezek 17:6 (twice in verse); 17:7-8, Hosea 10:1 compare Ezek 19:10; Jer 2:21; 6:9; also Hosea 14:8; figurative of Israel as easily destroyed Ezek 15:2, 6; figurative of godless enemies of Israel Deut 32:32 compare Di; שִׂבְמָה גֶּפֶן‎ figurative for prosperity of Moab Isa 16:8-9, Jer 48:32. — On the vine in Syria compare AnderlindZPV 1888, 160 ff.

גָּרֵב‎ 1. proper name, masculine (compare Palmyrene proper name, masculine גריבא‎ Vog141) one of David's heroes 2Sam 23:38 = 1Chr 11:40.

2. proper name, of a location (compare Sabean proper name, of a location גרבם‎ HalNo. 379, 382) only in גָּרֵב גִּבְעַת‎ Jer 31:39 hill of Gareb, apparently close to Jerusalem on the southwest compare Gf; see also Hi Che.

גַּרְגְּרוֺת גַּרְגַּר,‎ see below גרר‎.

גרגר.def:
H1620. gargar

[גַּרְגַּר‎] noun masculine berry (Late Hebrew id.), אָמ֑יר בְּראֹשׁ גַּרְגְּרִים‎ Isa 17:6.

גרגרת.def:
H1621. gargeroth

גַּרְגְּרוֺת‎ noun feminine plural neck (on formation compare BaNB 204) — גַּרְגְּרֹתֶ֑יךָ‎ Prov 1:9; 3:22, גַּרְגְרוֺתֶ֑ךָ‎ 3:3, גַּרְגְּרֹתֶ֑ךָ‎ 6:21 — always in figure, instruction of parents an ornament, a chain upon neck 1:9, bind them upon thy neck 6:21; so of mercy & truth 3:3, compare 3:22.

גרגשי.def:
H1622. Girgashi

גרד.def:
H1623. garad

[גָּרַד‎] verb scrape, scratch (Late Hebrew id., Aramaic גְּרַד‎, & Phoenician מגרדם‎ flesh-scrapers CIS338. 4; compare also Arabic peel or strip off bark, shave hair from a hide etc.) —

Hithpa`el Infinitive לְהִתְגָּרֵד‎ scrape one's self Job 2:8.

גרה.def:
H1624. garah

[גָּרָה‎] verb only

Pi`el stir up strife,

Hithpa`el engage in strife (compare Late Hebrew Pi`el stir up, excite, against (בְּ‎) Hithpa`el; Aramaic Pa`el גָּרֵא‎ ; especially Assyrian garû, Qal attack, be at war with, garû, girû, enemy, etc. AsrbAnnals iv. 49, 50 (KBii. 190) also SASmithAssurbanipal i. ii. Glossary; Arabic is run, especially of water, flow, etc.) —

Pi`el Imperfect3masculine singular יְגָרֶה‎ Prov 15:18; 28:25; 29:22, all with object מָדוֺן‎ excite, stir up, strife. — On גֵּרָה‎ Deut 14:8 see I. גֵּרָה‎ below גרר‎.

Hithpa`el Perfect2feminine singular הִתְגָּרִיתְ‎ Jer 50:24; Imperfect3masculine singular יִתְגָּרֶה‎ Dan 11:25, וְיִתְגָּרֶ֯ו‎ 11:10; 2masculine singular תִּתְגָּרֶה‎ 2Kin 14:19; 2Chr 25:19; jussive with apocope תִּתְגָּר‎ Deut 2:9, 19; 3masculine plural יִתְגָּרוּ‎ Prov 28:4; Dan 11:10, compare 11:10 Kt., see above; 2 masculine plural תִּתְגָּרוּ‎ Deut 2:5 (jussive); Imperative masculine singular הִתְגָּר‎ 2:24; —

1 excite oneself against (בְּ‎ person), engage in strife with, literally Deut 2:5, 19; 2Kin 14:19 2Chr 25:19 (followed by בְּרָעָה‎; — רעה‎ personified as challenged opponent); also + accusative of manner, מִלְחָמָה‎ Deut 2:9, 24; figurative בָם יִתְגָּרוּ תוֺרָה וְשֹׁמְרֵי‎ Prov 28:4 while they that keep the law are at strife with them, i.e. with those that forsake it.

2 absolute, excite oneself (against foe), wage war, only Daniel 11:רַבִּים חֲיָלִים הֲמוֺן וְאָֽסְפוּ יִתְגָּרוּ‎ Prov 28:10 they shall wage war, etc.; עַדמָֿעֻזֹּה וְיִתְגָּרֶ֯ו וְיָשֹׁב‎ 28:10 and he shall return and war, even to his stronghold; 28:25 followed by לַמִּלְחָמָה‎ + גָּדוֺל בְּחַיִל‎ (instrumental)

גרון.def:
H1627. garon

[גורן‎] Jer 2:25 גורנך‎ Kt see גָּרוֺן‎.

גושׁ‎ (be hard, compare Arabic be hard, of hands, from toil).

גָּרוֺן‎ noun masculinePsa 69:4 neck, throat (connection with above √ dubious; Thes Rob-Ges (compare MV) from גרה‎ in (assumed) sense of גרר‎ of a dragging, scraping sound; compare מְגֵרָה‎; yet √ perhaps גרן‎ q. v.; Arabic (sub Frey Lane) front part of neck of camel, etc.) — ׳ג‎ Isa 3:16; 58:1; suffix גְּרוֺנִי‎ Psa 69:4; גְּרוֺנֵךְ‎ Ezek 16:11 + Jer 2:25 Qr (Kt גורנך‎); גְּרוֺנָם‎ Psa 115:7; 149:6, גְּרֹנָם‎ 5:10; — throat;

1 of the visible exterior (front) of throat, neck ג ׳נְטֻו֯וֺת‎ Isa 3:16 outstretched of neck (= with outstretched neck); עַלגְּֿרוֺנֵךְ וְרָבִיד‎ Ezek 41:19 and a chain upon thy neck.

2 throat, as capable of thirst Jer 2:25; as organ of speech בְגָרוֺן קְרָא‎ Isa 58:1 (|| קוֺלֶ֑ךָ הָרֵם‎), בִּג יֶהְגּוּ ׳לֹא‎ Psa 115:7; also בִּגְרוֺנָם אֵל רוֺמֲמוֺת‎ 149:6 high songs to God (be) in their throat; compare גְּרוֺנִי נִחַר‎ 69:4 my throat is parched (|| בְקָרְאִי יָגַעְתִּי‎); so also גְּרֹנָם קֶבֶרמָּֿתוּחַ‎ 5:10 their throat is an opened sepulchre.

גרות.def:
H1628. Geruth

גּרוּת‎ noun feminine lodging (- place) — לחם בית אצל אשׁר כִּמְוהָם בְּגֵרוּת וישׁבו‎ Jer 41:17, inn, khan? so Ew Gf; Hi and others גִּדְרוֺת‎ folds, after Joseph. Aq

גרז.def:
H539. aman

I. [אָמַן‎] verb confirm, support (compare Arabic , etc., see below; Sabean אמן‎ in derivatives & proper names compare CISiv.1, 10 DHMZMG 1885, 598; Aramaic אֲמַן‎, in Haph`el, Ethiopic , Assyrian in derivatives) — only

Qal Participle אֹמֵן‎ —

1 as verb support, nourish 2Kin 10:1, 5; Est 2:7,

2 as substantive foster-father Num 11:12 (J) Isa 49:23.

3 אֹמֶנֶת‎ foster-mother, nurse Ruth 4:16; 2Sam 4:4.

4 אֹמְנוֺת‎ pillars, supporters of the door 2Kin 18:16. Participle passive a. הָאֱמֻנִים‎ those brought up (in scarlet) Lam 4:5.

b. אֱמוּנִים‎ intransitive faithful (as firm, stable) as substantive masculine faithful ones Psa 12:2 (> ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ and others faithfulness) 2Sam 20:19 (compare Arabic be faithful, trust in, be secure); Psa 31:24 faithful ones ׳י‎ Keepeth, י נֹצֵר ׳אֱמוּנִים‎; but ׳א‎ is here taken by ᵐ5‎ Ri De Che as abstract noun see אֵמֻן‎. Niph`al נֶאֱמַן‎ Prov 11:13 + (6 t); Imperfect יֵאָ֫מֶן יֵאָמֵן,‎ 1Kin 8:26 + (9 t.); Participle נֶאֱמָן‎ Prov 25:13 + ( 16 t.) נֶאֱמָנָה‎ Isa 1:21 + ( 4 t.); נֶאֱמֶנֶת‎ Psa 89:29; נֶאֱמָנִים‎ Prov 27:6 + (9 t.); נֶאֱמָנוֺת‎ Deut 28:59. 1.carried by a nurse Isa 60:4.

2 made firm, sure, lasting: place Isa 22:23, 25; name 1Chr 17:24; waters Isa 33:16; Jer 15:18; an event Hosea 5:9; sickness Deut 2:8:59; mercy Isa 55:3.

3 confirmed, established, sure: kingdom 2Sam 7:16; house, dynasty 1Sam 2:35; 25:28; 1Kin 11:38; 1Chr 17:23; prophet Samuel 1Sam 3:20; compare word-play תֵאָמֵנוּ לֹא תַאֲמִינוּ לֹא אִם‎ = if ye believe not (have not firm confidence) ye will not be confirmed Isa 7:9; בי ׳הַאֲמִינוּ וְתֵאָמֵנוּ‎ = believe in Yahweh and ye will be confirmed2Chr 20:20. 4. verified, confirmed: words of God 1Kin 8:26; 2Chr 1:9; 6:17; his precepts Psa 111:7; testimonies 19:8; 93:5; covenant 89:29; words of men Gen 42:20 (E). 5. reliable, faithful, trusty: persons 1Sam 2:35; 22:14; Job 12:20; Psa 89:38; 101:6; Prov 25:13; Isa 8:2; Neh 13:13; a city Isa 1:21; הנאמן האל‎ the faithful God Deut 7:9 compare Isa 49:7; רוּחַ נֶאֱמַן‎ faithful in spirit (disposition) Prov 11:13; נֶאֱמָן לְבָבוֺ‎ his heart faith-ful Neh 9:8; וְנֶאֱמָן אֱמֶת עֵד‎ true and faithful witness Jer 42:5; אוהב פצעי נאמנים‎ faithful the wounds of a loving one Prov 27:6; with נֵת‎ Psa 78:8; עִם‎ Hosea 12:1; בְּ‎ of thing Psa 78:37; בְּכָלבֵּֿיתִי‎ in all my house (of Moses) Num 12:7 (E). Hiph`il הֶאֱמִין‎ Gen 45:26 + (18 t.); Imperfect יַאֲמֵן יַאֲמִין,‎ Job 15:31 + (30 t.); Imperative הַאֲמִינוּ‎2Chr 20:20 + (2 t.); Participle מַאֲמִין‎ Deut 1:32; Josh 25:16.

4 stand firm Job 39:24 (with negative of the horse when the trumpet sounds Di De MV RVm; but neither believeth RV, hardly trusts Da). 2. trust, believe: (a) absolute Exod 4:31 (J) Isa 7:9; 28:16; Hab 1:5; Psa 116:10; Job 29:24; (b) with ל‎ of person, trust to, believe Gen 45:26 (E) Exod 4:1, 8 (J) Jer 40:14; 2Chr 32:15; with God Deut 9:23; Isa 43:10; ל‎ of thing Exod 4:8-9, (J) Psa 106:24; 1Kin 10:7; 2Chr 9:6; Isa 53:1; Prov 14:15; (c) with ב‎ of person, trust in, believe in Exod 19:9 (J) 1Sam 27:12; 2Chr 20:20; Job 4:18; 15:15; Prov 26:25; Jer 12:6; Micah 7:5; the usual construction with God Gen 15:6 (E) Exod 14:31; Num 14:11 (J) 20:12 (P) Deut 1:32; 2Kin 17:14; 2Chr 20:20; Psa 78:22; Jonah 3:5; with ב‎ of thing Deut 28:66; Job 15:31; 24:22; 39:12; Psa 78:32; 106:12; 119:66; (d) with כִּי‎ trust or believe that Exod 4:5 (J) Job 9:16; Lam 4:12; (e) so with infin. Job 15:22; Psa 27:13; also trust to do a thing, almost = allow, Judg 11:20.

[אֲמַן‎] verb Haph`el trust (Biblical Hebrew); — Perfect3masculine singular בֵּאלָחֵהּ חֵימִן‎ Dan 6:24; Passive participle מְחֵימַן‎ trusty, trustworthy, of person 6:5, interpretation 2:45.

גְּרִזִּים‎ proper name, of a location mountain in Northern Israel, south of Sichem (Nabulus), opposite Ebal (עֵיבָל‎), which was on north; only ג ׳הַר‎ Deut 11:29; 27:12; Josh 8:33; Judg 9:7; modern Jebel et‰-ˆôr RobBR ii. 274 ff. BdPal 220, 222.

[גָּרַם‎] verb lay aside, leave, save **meaning dubious; ? cut off, hence reserve (Late Hebrew גָּרַם‎ is shorten, occasion, bring about, to pass, Aramaic גְּרַם‎ Pa`el occasion, bring about, abscidit, decrevit, compare also Arabic cut off (fruit), shear (sheep); — on connection of ideas see Fl NHWBi. 437)

(construct e.g. 50:10-11, 2Sam 6:6); גָֹּֽרְנָָֽה׃‎ Micah 4:12; suffix גָּרְנִי‎ Isa 21:10; גָּרְנְךָ‎ Deut 15:14; 16:13; plural הַגְּרָנוֺת‎ 1Sam 23:1, הַגֳּרָנוֺת‎ Joel 2:24; construct גָּרְנוֺת‎ Hosea 9:1 — threshing-floor, (on form see RobBR i. 550 compare Fl NHWBi. 437) Gen 50:10-11, (׳ג האטד‎) Num 18:27 (מןהֿג ׳דָּגָן‎) Deut 15:14; 16:13; Judg 6:37; Ruth 3:2 (ג זֹרֶה ׳הוּא הַשְּׂעֹרִים‎) 3:3; 3:6; 3:14; 2Sam 6:6; 24:16, 18, 21, 24; 1Chr 13:9; 21:15, 18, 21, 22, 28; 2Chr 3:1; Hosea 9:1 (׳ג דָּגָן‎) 9:2; Micah 4:12; Job 39:12 compare Di; ג ׳תְּרוּמַת‎ Num 15:20; ג ׳תְּבוּאַת‎ 18:30; of these, three may be proper name, of a location: — הָאָטָד גֹּרֶן‎ Gen 50:10-11, נָכוֺן גֹּרֶן‎ 2Sam 6:6 (compare We Dr) = כִּידֹן גֹּרֶן‎ 1Chr 13:9; place of storing corn, etc. 1Sam 23:1; 2Kin 6:27; Joel 2:24; open place at city-gate שֹׁמְרוֺן מֶּתַחשַׁעַר גֹּרֶן‎ 1Kin 22:10 2Chr 18:9, where kings of Israel & Judah sat (but this peculiar & text dubious; ᵐ5‎ (in Kings) ἔνοπλοι; We omits; ᵑ6‎ Th Be בְּרֻדִּים‎, agreeing with בְּגָדִים‎ preceding; yet this elsewhere in Hebrew only of animals); in simile of daughter of Babylon, Jer 51:33 (trodden smooth) compare figurative of Israel בֶּןגָּֿרְנִי‎ || (מדֻשָׁתִיׅ‎) Isa 21:10; .... ׳מִגּ מֹץ‎ Hosea 13:3.

גרס.def:
H1638. garas

[גָּרַס‎] verb be crushed (Aramaic [be crushed,] perish) —

Qal Perfect3feminine singular גָָּֽרְסָה‎ Psa 119:20 figurative ׳ג לְ נַפְשִׁי‎ my soul is crushed (i.e. perisheth: compare Syriac) with longing for (compare לְ כָּלָה‎).

Hiph`il Imperfect שִׁנָּ֑י בֶּחָצָץ וַיַּגְרֵס‎ Lam 3:16 and he hath crushed my teeth with gravel, figurative of divine chastisement.

גרע.def:
H1639. gara

[גָּרַע‎] verb diminish, restrain, withdraw (Late Hebrew id., Aramaic גְּרַע‎ shave head, etc.; compare swallow) —

Qal Imperfect יִגְרַע‎ Job 36:7, יִגְרָ֑ע‎ Exod 21:10; 2masculine singular תִּגְרַע‎ Deut 13:1 3t.; אֶגְרַע‎ Ezek 5:11 (but compare below), וָאֶגְרַע‎ 16:27; תִּגְרְעוּ‎ Exod 5:8 2t.; Infinitive לִגְרֹעַ‎ Eccl 3:14; Participle גְּרוּעָה‎ Isa 15:2 (so Baer; v. d. H. גְּדוּעָה‎ see גדע‎), גְּרֻעָה‎ Jer 48:37; —

1 diminish, usually followed by מִן‎ Exod 5:8, 19 (the tale of bricks), Deut 4:2; 13:1 (in both, word of ׳י‎; opposed to הוסיף‎) compare Eccl 3:14, and also Jer 26:2 (with accusative); with accusative also Exod 21:10 (food etc.) compare Ezek 16:27; Passive participle diminished, clipped, of beard, Jer 48:37 and Isa 15:2 (so Baer, rightly, compare his note and see גדע‎).

2 restrain Job 15:4 (with accusative שִׂיחָה‎ meditation, devotion), 15:8 (with accusative חָכְמָה‎, followed by אֵלֶיךָ‎, i.e. unto, for thyself, monopolize; De Di Da render draw unto thyself, appropriate; Schult. compare Arabic swallow, compare Ew saugst zu dir ein Weisheit).

3 withdraw Job 36:7 (object עַיִן‎, eye, followed by מִן‎); Ezek 5:11 absolute (si vera lectio); Co. reads אֶתְגָּרֶה‎, for אֶגְרַע‎, on internal grounds; others: withdraw (thy needs) Sm (compare 16:27); withdraw (mine eye) Ges Ke.

Niph`al Perfect וְנִגְרַע‎ consecutive Lev 27:18; וְנִגְרְעָה‎ Num 36:3; Imperfect יִגָּרַע‎ 27:4; 36:4, יִגָּרֵ֑עַ‎ 36:3; 1plural נִגָּרַע‎ 9:7; Participle נִגְרָע‎ Exod 5:11; —

1 be withdrawn with מִן‎ Num 36:3 (twice in verse); 36:4 (inheritance, נחלה‎); 27:4 a name out of a family; Exod 5:11 (דָּבָר מֵעֲבֹדַתְכֶם‎); impersonal Lev 27:18 (abatement shall be made).

2 be restrained followed by infinitive Num 9:7. Pi`el Imperfect יְגָרַע‎ Job 36:27 withdraw = draw up with accusative נִטְפֵימָֿ֑יִם‎ compare Di (on other hand, De and others draw down, let down).

Niph`al (read

Qal ? Samaritan יָגוֺר‎ compare Di) Imperfect יִגָּ֑ר‎ Lev 11:7 with accusative of congnate meaning with verb לֹאיִֿגָּ֑ר גֵּרָה‎ = (the) cud he cheweth not, compare also Deut 14:8 ᵐ5 ⅏‎ (Di).

Hithpo`el מִתְגּוֺרֵ֑ר סַעַר‎ Jer 36:23 a (sweeping) roaring whirlwind (|| 23:19 has מִתְחוֺלֵל‎). On יִתְגּוֺרָרוּ‎ Hosea 7:14, see I.גדד גור,‎.

גרש.def:
H1643. geres

גֶּ֫רֶשׂ‎ noun [masculine] a crushing, but only concrete of that which is crushed, groats, grits (compare Arabic , Late Hebrew גְּרִיס‎, Aramaic (rare) גְּרוּסְיָא גִּרְשָׂא,‎ ) — כַּרְמֶל גֶּרֶשׂ בָּאֵשׁ קָלוּי אָבִיב‎ Lev 2:14 young ears parched with fire, groats (&) fresh fruit (see Sifra on the passage); (וּמִשַּׁמְנָהּׅ מִגִּרְשָׂהּ‎ 2:16.

גרשה.def:
H1646. gerushah

[גְּרוּשָׁה‎] noun feminine expulsion, violence. Only plural suffix גְּרֻשֹׁתֵיכֶם‎ Ezek 45:9 your acts of expulsion (compare Ew Da; 'Raubereien' Sm Co).

גרשון.def:
H1648. Gereshon

or Gereshom גֵּרְשׁוֺן‎ proper name, masculine son of Levi (= גרשׁם‎ 1Chr 6:1; 6:28; 15:7 גרשׁום‎ 6:2; 6:5; 6:47; 6:56) Gen 46:11; Exod 6:16-17, Num 3:17-18, 21, 25; 4:22, 38, 41; 7:7; 10:17; 26:57; Josh 21:6, 27; 1 Chronicles 5:27; 1Chr 23:6 (particularly in expression sons of Gershon, i.e. family, descendants of Gershon Num 3:25; 4:22, 38, 41; 7:7; 10:17; Josh 21:6, 27; compare sons of Gershom 1Chr 6:47; 6:56; 15:7).

גרשם.def:
H1647. Gereshom

גֵּרְשֹׁם‎ proper name, masculine

1 son of Moses & Sipporah Exod 2:22 (explanation as if from גור‎) = 18:3; גֵּרְשׁוֺם‎ 1Chr 23:15-16, 26:24; so also גֵּרְשֹׁם‎ Judg 18:30 מְנַשֶּׁה בֶּןֿ ᵑ0‎ compare VB.

2 a son of Levi גֵּרְשֹׁם‎ 1Chr 6:1; 6:28; 15:7 (compare גֵּרְשׁוֺן‎); גֵּרְשׁוֺם‎ 6:2; 6:5; 6:47; 6:56.

3 a son of Phinehas Ezra 8:2.

גרשני.def:
H1649. Gereshunni

גֵּרְשֻׁנִּי‎ adjective, of a people with article as substantive collective Num 3:21, 23, 24; 4:24, 27, 28; 26:57; Josh 21:33; 1Chr 23:7; 26:21; 2Chr 29:12; with article as adjective singular masculine 1Chr 26:21; 29:8.

גשור.def:
H1650. Geshur

גְּשׁוּר‎ proper name, masculine (bridge ? or land of bridges ? compare WetzstHauran, 82).

1 of people, = הַגְּשׁוּרִי‎ Josh 13:13 compare 1Chr 2:23.

2 of land גְּשׁוּר מֶלֶךְ‎ 2Sam 3:3; 13:37 compare 13:38 (but text in disorder compare ᵐ5‎ We Dr) 14:32; 15:8 ׳בִּגְ בַּאֲרָם‎ 1Chr 3:2, גְּשׁ֫וּרָה‎ 2Sam 14:23; a territory east of the upper Jordan, exact limits unknown; according to GutheZPV xii. 1889, 232 f. between Gilead and Hermon, in Jaulân; according to Furrerib. xiii. 1890, 198 = the Ledjah, district east of Jaulân, with town Jisre; against him Gutheib. 285 f.

גשורי.def:
H1651. Geshuri

גְּשׁוּרִי‎ adjective, of a people = substantive ׳הַגּ‎;

1 people dwelling in Geshûr (above) Deut 3:14; Josh 12:5; 13:11, 13.

2 a tribe of, or near, the Philistines Josh 13:2 read probably הֵגִּוְרִי‎ We and Dr (on 1Sam 27:8), MeyZAW i. 126 n GFMJudg 1:29 n., also 1Sam 27:8, but deleted ᵐ5‎ (not ᵐ5‎L) compare We Dr; read possibly אשׁורי‎ HomAufsätze i. (1892), 9; 2Sam 2:9 read ׳הגּ‎ for האשׁורי‎.

גשם.def:
H1656. goshem

[גּ֫שֶׁם‎] noun [masculine] גֻּשְֿׁמָהּ‎ Ezek 22:24 (or גִּשְׁמָהּ‎ from גֶּשֶׁם‎ ?) according to punctuation; but compare below גשׁם‎

verb

גשמו.def:
H1654. Geshem

or Gashmu I. גֶּ֫שֶׁם‎ proper name, masculine an opponent of Nehemiah Neh 2:19; 6:1 (in both called הָעַרְבִּי‎); 6:2; also גַּשְׁמוּ‎ 6:6; וּ‎ as in Nabataean proper name compare Nö in EutNab 73.

גַּשְׁמוּ‎ proper name, see I. גֶּשֶׁם‎. above

H1657. Goshen

גּ֫שֶׁן‎ proper name, of a location (on etymology compare Di Gen 45:10) —

1 district in Egypt east of lower Nile, see EbGS 500 ff.; NavilleGoshen, 1887, who reads hieroglyphics Kesem, but compare GroffJAs xiv. 527 (ᵐ5‎ Γεσεμ (Ἀραβιας)) — גּשֶׁן אֶרֶץ‎ Gen 45:10 (JE) 46:34; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exod 8:18; 9:26 (all J); גּשֶׁן אַ֫רְצָה‎ Gen 46:28 (J), גּ֑שְׁנָה‎ 46:28; 46:29 (both J), in both ᵐ5‎ καθ’ Ἡρώων πόλιν compare Di. (P has land רעמסס‎ 47:11 etc., compare Di 45:10.

2 הַגּשֶׁן ארץ‎ Josh 11:16 (D), גּשֶׁן אֶרֶץ‎ 10:41 (D), גּשֶׁן‎ 15:51 (P) (ᵐ5‎ in all Γοσομ) a city named with חֹלֹן‎ & גִּלֹה‎ compare Di. — not clearly located, but on southern border of Judah.

גשפא.def:
H1658. Gishpa

גִּשְׁמָּא‎ proper name, masculine named after צִיחָא‎ as an officer of Nethinim Neh 11:21; see om. B; ᵐ5‎L & Manuscripts Γεσφα; name not elsewhere in OT, not even || 1 Chronicles 9; possibly corrupted from חֲשֻׂפָא‎ 7:46 (following צִחָא‎; in || Ezra 2:43 צִיחָא חֲשׁוּפָא,‎), ᵐ5‎ Ἁσφα (B; Manuscripts Ασειφα, etc.); compare BeRy.

גשש.def:
H1659. gashash

[גשׁשׁ‎] verb feel with the hand, feel, stroke (Late Hebrew id., Arabic , Aramaic גְשַׁשׁ‎ Pa`el, ; Ethiopic or stroke, touch) —

Pi`el Imperfect1plural cohortative נְגַשֲׁשָׁ֫ה‎ Isa 59:10, נְגַשֵּׁ֑שָׁה‎ ib., grope, grope for compare Che.

גת.def:
H1661. Gath

II. גַּת‎ proper name, of a location (wine-press) — Philistine city ᵐ5‎ Γεθ, ᵑ9‎ Geth, JosAnt. vi. 12, 2 etc., Γιττα (ed. Niese), exact site unknown (see GASmGeog. 194 ff.), named with Gaza and Ashdod Josh 11:22 as home of remaining `Anakim; named with Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon and `Ekron 1Sam 6:17; with Ashkelon 1:20; with Ashkelon, yabne and Ashdod 2Chr 26:6; וְעַדגַּֿת מֵעֶקְרוֺן‎ 1Sam 7:14, compare 17:52b and also 17:52a (read גַּת‎ for ᵐ5 גַּיְא‎ We Dr); called מְּלִשְׁתִּים גַּת‎ Amos 6:2; built up by Rehoboam, according to 2Chr 11:8; taken by Hazael 2Kin 12:18; also 1Sam 5:8; 17:4, 23 (of Goliath), compare 2Sam 21:20, 22 = 1Chr 20:6, 8; 1Sam 21:11; 21:13; 27:2-3, 4, 11; 2Sam 15:18; 1Kin 2:39 (twice in verse); 2:40-41, Psa 56:1; Micah 1:10, 14; 1Chr 7:21; 8:13, also 18:1 (but || אַמָּה מֶתֶג‎ 2Sam 8:1; on change of this into reading in Chronicles see We); with ה‎ locative, גַּ֫תָּה‎ 1Kin 2:40.

גת החפר.def:
H1662. Gath

-hachepher הַחֵ֫פֶר גַּת‎ 2Kin 14:25 (wine-press of digging home of Jonah, prophet; חֵ֫פֶר גִּתָּ֖הֿ‎ Josh 19:13, perhaps modern El-Meshhed, approximately 3 miles east of north from Nazareth, RobBR ii. 350 BdPal 252.

גת רמון.def:
H1667. Gath

-rimmon גַּתרִֿמּוֺן‎ proper name, of a location in Dan Josh 19:45; Levitical city 21:24 = 1Chr 6:54; site unknown. — רִמּוֺן גַּת‎ in Manasseh Josh 21:25 is scribal error; read יִבְלְעָם‎, q. v.

גתי.def:
H1663. Gitti

גִּתִּי‎ adjective, of a people, of II.גַּת‎ 1; of Obed-edom 2Sam 6:10-11, = 1Chr 13:13; Ittai 2Sam 15:19, 22; 18:2; Goliath 21:19; 1Chr 20:5; plural with article as substantive, הַגִּתִּים‎ 1Sam 15:18 the Gittites (but read הַגִּתִּי אִתַּי‎ We Klo Kit Bu NowArchaeology i.308n.); singular with article as proper name collectiveהַגִּתִּי‎ Josh 13:3 (with men of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the Awwim).

adjective see below יגן‎. p. 387 f

גתית.def:
H1665. Gittith

גִּתִּית‎ feminine of foregoing (si vera lectio) only in phrase עַלהַֿגִּתִּית‎ in three Psalm titles: Psa 8:1; 81:1; 84:1; upon the Gittite (lyre) so ᵑ7‎,to the Gittite (melody) Ew Ol De, or either of these Hup Pe; הַגִּתֹּת ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎ wine-presses, whence Bae and others at the wine-presses, i.e. (Bae) a song for the feast of booths.

גתר.def:

גֶּ֫תֶר‎ proper name, masculine (√ unknown) a son of Aram Gen 10:23 = 1Chr 1:17.
